News.title: When will it get cold again? Latest Met Office weather forecast for week and rest of October 2026
News.content:
Next

A COOLER spell is set to sweep across the UK this week as unsettled weather takes hold.

The Met Office says temperatures will drop overnight on Tuesday, with downpours, fog and frost forecast.



After a summer boasting five heatwaves, September has been noticeably cooler as we shift into autumn.

Milder conditions continued into the start of October, with the Met Office describing it as “unusually warm”.



And while the start of October has been mild, fresh air spreading south will see temperatures dip.

Met Office meteorologist Kathryn Chalk said: “On Tuesday, to the south, people might wake up to some mist and dense fog patches, to the north of that it’s going to be cloud, to the far north, across Scotland, it will be a day of sunny spells and showers.



“As we head into Tuesday night we will see more rain on the way. Overnight into Wednesday there will be cloudy outbreaks of rain across much of England…

“Tuesday into Wednesday overnight, rural spots in the north could drop to minus 1C, and see frost in places.”

When will it get cold again in the UK?

Tuesday night could already feel distinctly autumnal in the north.

Across England and Wales, rain will spread during the night and could become heavy at times.



The Met Office says the UK will turn much cooler on Wednesday.

Heavy rain is forecast to move slowly east across England and Wales, while Scotland and Northern Ireland should see sunny spells and scattered showers.

The forecaster says Scotland and Northern Ireland will turn chilly overnight, with patchy frost possible.

Thursday through to Saturday will remain changeable, with spells of rain and heavy showers mixed in with drier and brighter periods.

What is the Met Office forecast for this week?

Tuesday brings a mixed picture across the country.



Scotland will see brighter periods and scattered showers, while northern England, Wales and the Midlands will be cloudier with showery rain.

The southeast should enjoy warmer sunny spells for longer.

Wednesday marks the more widespread change, with cooler conditions expected across the UK as heavy rain works eastwards through England and Wales.

The outlook then remains unsettled into the weekend, with rain or heavy showers at times and occasional brighter breaks.

What is the Met Office long-range forecast for the rest of October?

From October 10 to October 19, the Met Office expects a series of low-pressure systems to move across the North Atlantic.



This should bring occasional bands of rain and strong winds to the north and northwest, broken up by brighter and showery spells.

The wettest conditions are most likely over western hills and particularly in the northwest, where rainfall is expected to be above average.

Southern and eastern areas have a better chance of more prolonged dry spells.

However, while the Met Office says “brief cooler interludes are possible”, with temperatures likely to be a little above average in many areas across the period.

This changeable pattern is expected to continue into early November.



Low-pressure systems are likely to keep passing close to the UK from the Atlantic, bringing showers or longer periods of rain.

The west and northwest are expected to see the wettest and windiest conditions, while sheltered southern and eastern areas should generally be drier.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

There may be occasional colder spells, but the Met Office does not currently forecast sustained unusually cold weather.

Temperatures are expected to be near or slightly above average overall.

News.title: Housekeeper, 71, ‘stole princess’ wedding ring & other irreplaceable jewels from London home before trying to sell them’
News.content:
JEWEL HEIST Housekeeper, 71, ‘stole princess’ wedding ring & other irreplaceable jewels from London home before trying to sell them’







Next

A HOUSEKEEPER allegedly stole a princess’s wedding ring and a hoard of priceless jewels from a mansion, a court heard.

Maria Taborda Henao, a 71-year-old Colombian cleaner, is accused of raiding the 80-year-old royal’s collection while Princess Firyal of Jordan was visiting family in 2020.



It is alleged that the housekeeper, who had worked for the princess for 11 years, systematically looted diamond rings, bracelets, watches and earrings.

Jurors at Southwark Crown Court heard Ms Taborda Henao was the sole person permitted to access the property in Belgravia, London, in her employer’s absence.



The alleged stolen haul reportedly included a Cartier brooch and the sentimental wedding band given to the princess upon her 1964 marriage to Prince Muhammad bin Talal of Jordan.

The alleged theft unravelled when Pierre Jeannet, a partner at the high-end jeweller JAR, contacted his royal friend to warn her that a bespoke sapphire and diamond ring made expressly for her was being auctioned in Kent.



Upon further investigation, the princess identified multiple pieces of her stolen collection being sold through Canterbury Auction Galleries since June 2020.

Olly Wellings, prosecuting, said the royal provided a lengthy inventory of the stolen goods, backed up by receipts and photographs of her wearing the gems.

He told the jury: “The items which appeared in the Canterbury auction represent a small selection of the total items missing.”

Among the fenced items was a unique pair of enamel and gem-set earrings, originally purchased from Sotheby’s for £28,750 in 2011, which were reportedly sold off for a mere £400.



It is alleged that the Ms Taborda Henao’s 43-year-old nephew, Julian Ramirez, orchestrated the sales, netting roughly £90,000 in revenue from the auction house while claiming he was trying to open a restaurant.

The prosecutor outlined that Mr Ramirez then transferred £17,835 to his aunt between June 2019 and November 2020 as her share of the illicit proceeds.

When the divorced royal finally returned to her London residence in May 2021, she tragically “found much of her jewellery missing”, the court heard.

Mr Wellings told the court that every genuine gemstone had been stripped from the home, leaving behind only worthless pieces of costume jewellery.

Following a police investigation, officers searched Ms Taborda Henao’s Fulham address in November 2020.



The court heard that cops reportedly discovered several items believed to have been plundered from the Belgravia estate.

Mr Ramirez was arrested the same day at an address in Rochester, Kent, but subsequently skipped bail.

It is understood the nephew fled the country in October 2023 and is currently believed to be in Colombia.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Ms Taborda Henao, who appeared in the dock assisted by a Spanish interpreter, denies theft by an employee.

The princess is expected to give evidence on Wednesday.

News.title: Hunt for two women after more than £1,000 of clothing & items stolen from Next & Boots at two shopping parks days apart
News.content:
THEFT PROBE Hunt for two women after more than £1,000 of clothing & items stolen from Next & Boots at two shopping parks days apart







Next

COPS are hunting for two women after more than £1,000 worth of clothing and stock was stolen just days apart.

The suspects nicked a “large quantity” of items from Next and Boots during their shoplifting spree across retail parks in Berkshire.



The thieves first targeted Next in Reading Gate Retail Park at around 4.30pm on September 3, Thames Valley Police said.

Just days later, they brazenly swiped goods from a Boots store in the Calcot Sainsbury’s Retail Park at around 1.45pm on September 7.



In both thefts, the pair ransacked display shelves before leaving without making any attempt to pay, the force added.

The total value of the stolen goods, said to be mainly clothing, is understood to be in excess of £1,000.

Officers have now released CCTV of two women they wish to identify in connection with the thefts.

PC Richard Tarrant, of the West Berkshire Local Command Unit, urged anyone who recognises the women to get in touch.

He said: “I am appealing to anyone who recognises the two women shown in these CCTV images to get in touch.

“We believe they may have vital information that could assist our investigation into these theft offences.



“If you recognise either of these women, or have any information that may help, please contact us.”

Anyone with information can contact the force online or via 101, quoting reference numbers 43260466137 and 43260465972.

A Thames Valley Police spokesperson added: “You can provide information anonymously via Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111 or via their website.”

News.title: Putin unleashes devastating missile and jet drone strike on Ukraine killing civilians as tyrant marks 74th birthday
News.content:
Next

VLADIMIR Putin has marked his 74th birthday with one of the cruellest and most devastating missile and jet drone strikes on Ukraine.

The tyrant’s forces staged blistering attacks across Kyiv’s energy and industrial infrastructure as he plots to freeze Ukrainians this winter.



Footage shows one of dozens of devastating missile strikes – in this case a streaking North Korean-made KN-23 – attacking the city of Dnipro.

At least two people were killed in Kyiv’s Darnytskyi district, with the toll expected to rise across Ukraine.





Residents huddled in metro stations as the onslaught engulfed the capital.

“It’s hell here,” reported one terrified resident.



Missiles – including Kh-101s – flew low in large groups towards their targets overwhelming Ukrainian air defences.

Swarms of strikes hit the hydro-electric plant in Kremenchuk – a key energy hub for all of Ukraine.

Critical infrastructure was also targeted in Oleksandriia, Kirovohrad region, leading to multiple casualties, mayor Serhiy Kuzmenko said.

And Kyiv’s northern industrial zone was engulfed in flames after at least three Russian Iskander-M/RM-48U S-400 ballistic missile strikes.



Residential areas were also hit with people are reportedly trapped under the rubble of a five-storey building flattened by a cruise missile strike in Pryluky, Chernihiv.

“The missiles are falling one after another. At least 10-12 explosions from what I can count. It’s pretty loud in the city centre,” said Kyiv Independent’s Tim Zadorozhnyy.

Ukrainian intelligence had warned in advance of the massive strikes coinciding with Putin’s birthday.

Ukrainian national security commentator Andriy Kovalenko accused Russian “criminals” of planning in advance “to celebrate Putin’s birthday by terrorising civilians.”



The Russian dictator ordered ten Tu-95MS and three Tu-160M strategic nuclear-capable bombers into the sky.

The Putin terror was unleashed on Ukraine as birthday messages arrived from other dictators.

North Korean despot Kim Jong Un told the Russian ruler: “I am firmly convinced that the just, sacred struggle of the Russian people to defend the country’s sovereignty, security interests, and territorial integrity will inevitably triumph.

“I once again assure you of my unwavering support for you and the Russian Federation.”



Pyongyang’s communist leader has long-supplied Putin with weapons, ammunition, troops, and military technology for his bloodthirsty war.

Belarus tyrant Alexander Lukashenko praised Putin’s alleged selfless service to the Motherland.

“I am convinced that the trusting relationship that has developed between us will allow us to continue to stand together on issues of bilateral and international importance,” he said.

The, an ex-collective farm boss from the Soviet era, has ruled Belarus since 1994.



The dictator never faced proper opposition after he ruthlessly crushed protests following his 2020 election ‘win’.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Lukashenko was Putin’s closest ally in the invasion of Ukraine, hosting the Russian army before it crossed the border to attack Kyiv.

Belarus now also hosts Russian nuclear weapons on Nato‘s doorstep.

News.title: M5 ‘closed for several hours’ after crash & fire as commuters warned of long delays
News.content:
Next

A MAJOR motorway has been forced to close after a horror smash and car fire – sparking commuter chaos.

Drivers travelling on the M5 have been warned it will be shut for “several hours” following the crash near Rubery, West Midlands, last night.



Emergency crews were scrambled to the busy stretch at around 10.20pm.

The road then closed in both directions between Junction 4, for Rubery, and Junction 3, for Quinton, while investigations were carried out.



It later re-opened on the southbound carriageway, but traffic heading northbound is still being affected this morning.

Issuing an update on X, National Highways confirmed recovery teams and carriageway assessments would follow the police probe.



A spokesperson said: “A full Police Accident Investigation is taking place.

“Once the Police Accident Investigation is complete, vehicle recovery will take place and any carriageway damage will need to be assessed.

“If this closure impacts on your planned route, please allow extra journey time.

“Plan ahead, you may wish to re-route or even delay your journey.”



Drivers heading northbound have been urged to follow the Solid Circle diversion symbol.

Northbound diversion Northbound road users are advised to follow the Solid Circle diversion symbol on road signs Exit the M5 at J4, take the exit onto the A491 westbound.

Continue on the A491, westbound and northbound to A491/A456 roundabout.

At the A491/A456 roundabout, take the 3rd exit onto the A456 eastbound.

Continue on the A456 eastbound to the A356/M5 J3.

At the A456/M5 J3 roundabout, take the 1st exit to re-join the M5 northbound at J3.

News.title: Student, 19, ‘strangled to death by her stepdad in uni halls after he developed sexual obsession with her’
News.content:
UNI HORROR Student, 19, ‘strangled to death by her stepdad in uni halls after he developed sexual obsession with her’







Next

A STUDENT was strangled to death by her stepdad in her university accommodation after he developed a sexual obsession with her, a court heard.

Carla Georgescu, 19, was discovered dead on what would have been her 20th birthday on the University of Lancashire campus in Preston.



Her stepdad Nathan Owens, 34, is accused of driving through the night to murder Carla after becoming “sexually fixated” with her, jurors heard.

Preston Crown Court heard he was possibly driven by “sexual jealousy” after discovering his stepdaughter was due to meet up with a new lover.



Owens allegedly left the home he shared with Carla’s mum Janina in Hartlepool in the early hours of February 4 and strangled her to death.

The second year clinical psychology student was found the next day slumped against a wardrobe door with injuries to her face.

Nicholas Lumley KC, prosecuting, said: “Her death was the culmination, the end point, of weeks, months and perhaps years of a one-sided sexual obsession.

“And it was the beginning of a complex murder investigation, which led to his door in Hartlepool.

“For it was he who was sexually fixated on Carla and it was he, Nathan Owens, who had killed Carla.”

Jurors heard Owens made up a story about visiting Carla’s flat to collect her mother’s purse after she left it during a previous visit.



But he did not tell his wife about the journey and spent around 90 minutes in the flat, it was said.

Owens also parked his car “some distance” from the accommodation and covered himself with a blanket, the court was told.

When he left, he was allegedly “shielding” himself with an umbrella and wearing a face-mask and Carla’s trainers, while carrying several bags.

Carla’s mum raised the alarm when she failed to contact her daughter and the police were called.

Officers initially believed the student had taken her own life but a forensic examination suggested there was “more” to her death, jurors heard.



A post mortem also revealed Carla had been subjected to two heavy blows to her head, slash marks on her cheek and cuts and bruises to her mouth and nose.

Carla’s hands were covered in blood after she attempted to defend herself and she had sexual injuries, the court heard.

The jury was told sex toys and Owens’ DNA were found at the scene.

Mr Lumley said “some form of grievous sexual activity” had taken place which was “hardly surprising” given Owens’ sexual obsession with her.

He alleged in the months leading up to Carla’s murder, Owens had been collecting photos of her taken without her knowledge.



Owens had also allegedly filmed himself having sex with her dolls and toys – including one that was a life-sized “effigy” dressed in Carla’s nightie.

He was also said to have manipulated innocent selfies of Carla into sexual images which he viewed in the week before she died.

“The only possible reason for looking at those images is that Nathan Owens had a wholly improper and dangerously entrenched sexual obsession with his stepdaughter,” Mr Lumley told the court.

Jurors were told Carla – a second year psychology student at the University of Lancashire – was fit and well in the weeks before she died.

The prosecution also alleges Mr Owens removed Carla’s phone and laptop and dumped them on the drive between Preston and Hartlepool.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Owens denies charges of murder, intentional strangulation and grievous bodily harm with intent.

The trial continues.

News.title: Ex-World Conker Championships winner, 84, QUITS as mascot two years after being cleared in cheating scandal
News.content:
CONKED OUT Ex-World Conker Championships winner, 84, QUITS as mascot two years after being cleared in cheating scandal







Next

A FORMER World Conker champion has quit as mascot two years after he was caught up in a major cheating scandal – from which he was later cleared.

David Jakins, 84, had held the honorific position for two decades but is now walking away due to old age.



The stalwart of the brown seed smashing contest had rocked the sport in 2024 over allegations he cheated his way to his first ever win.

Jakins, then aged 82, was caught with a steel conker in his pocket.



He was accused of swapping the all-natural conker for the metal replacement to take his first title after 40 years of trying.

The veteran was cleared of any wrongdoing after a probe reviewed video footage.

But the controversy cast a shadow over last year’s event and led to “airport-style” security checks being brought in.

Mr Jakins says he is stepping down “with great sadness” due to reduced mobility.



The crown will be passed to his daughter Fee Aylmore and World Colmer Championships chairman Jim Packer, who become the new King and Queen Conker.

Mr Jakins said: “It is with great sadness that I step down from my role as King Conker after 20 wonderful years.

“However, I am extremely pleased to pass this role onto my daughter, Fee, who will be a wonderful Queen Conker, supported admirably by Jim, who will be supporting her as a new King Conker.”

Organiser StJohn Burkett said: “It will be sad to see David go as he has served his role admirably.

“He is struggling with his mobility due to arthritis in his knees so feels now is the right time.



“I don’t think the cheating scandal weighed that heavily on his decision – he feels he has cleared his name regarding that matter.

“However, we have since kept his steel conker in a Perspex box which we display at the event to make sure there is no repeat of the events of 2024.”

Fee said: “It is a great honour to take over from my dad, who loved his conkers and served with honour all these years. His will be a hard act to follow.”

Jim said: “He never let on about the steel conker, even to me. I hope I’m up to the job.”

This year’s event takes place in Southwick, Northamptonshire, on Sunday.

News.title: Kemi ready to throw the gauntlet down to Labour today on taxes as she capitalises her momentum
News.content:
POLITICS FIX Kemi ready to throw the gauntlet down to Labour today on taxes as she capitalises her momentum







Next

KEMI Badenoch is adamant that young people simply can’t be left on the jobs scrapheap.

The Tory leader vows to slash Labour’s so-called “Jobs Tax” to help young people take their first step on the jobs ladder.



She is attempting to assert her position and challenge Chancellor John Healey to follow suit at the Budget later this month.

Badenoch recognises the national scandal of nearly one million young people not in education, employment or training.



She highlights that not being in work at a young age will negatively affect lifetime earnings.

For a young person, lifetime earnings drop by £52,000 but this figure rises to £293,000 for those aged 18 to 24 who are out of work or education.

So she will lower taxes for employers hiring people aged 21 to 24 to encourage them to take on more youths.

Labour is awaiting the outcome of a report by Labour grandee Alan Milburn on youth inactivity before making its next move on young people.

The Treasury know better than anyone that money is tight and pledging a £2.3 billion tax cut will likely prove out of reach for Mr Healey.

Kemi Badenoch has so far had a strong few days with the party faithful in Birmingham.



Her biggest challenge is to elevate the Tory brand and try and put some distance between the Conservative party that was booted out of office two years ago.

But as she addresses the conference in Birmingham today the pressure will be on her to capitalise on her recent momentum.

News.title: American Airlines flight carrying 287 makes urgent landing after six toilets stop working
News.content:
American Airlines flight carrying 287 makes urgent landing after six toilets stop working

The plane was swiftly diverted to New York after all but two toilets broke mid-air, with the pilot declaring a 'pan pan' signal to indicate an urgent problem

View 2 Images The 287 passengers were diverted to New York (Image: Getty Images)

A flight carrying 287 people was forced to make an emergency landing after six toilets suddenly stopped working mid-air.

‌



‌



American Airlines Flight 37 departed Madrid on Tuesday morning and was due to land in Dallas around 11 hours later, but the plane was swiftly diverted to New York after all but two toilets broke.

‌



With four hours of fuel left, the Boeing 777 was over its typical landing weight - which can cause the brakes to easily overheat, catch fire, or fail completely.

‌



The pilot declared "pan-pan" - a term to signal an urgent problem needing immediate attention, but not a life threatening emergency.

In a statement, the Federal Aviation Administration said: "American Airlines Flight 37 landed at JFK International Airport in New York after the crew reported an inadequate number of operational lavatories."

View 2 Images The crew reported 'an inadequate number of operational lavatories' (Image: Getty Images)

‌



As the plane approached John F. Kennedy International Airport, the pilot told air traffic control: "So (we) have only two potties operating on board for American 37."

"You said only two potties. Is that right?" the controller replied. "That's affirmative," the pilot said.

The plane landed in New York safely before continuing onto Dallas after more than three hours, according to tracking site FlightAware.

‌



The Mirror has contacted American Airlines for comment.

While it's not clear why the toilets stopped working, an expert has told how the devices are complex, as they rely on air pressure to run, which can sometimes get blocked or otherwise malfunction, reports CNN.

Nigel Jones, a former engineer for British Airways told the publication in 2024: "It's only a tiny pipe, and people put things like (diapers) down - I've seen cutlery go down, and (soft drink cans) - they're fascinated to see whether it will go down or not.

Article continues below

"It can take days to rectify because there's an awful lot of pipework, and it has to be broken down to find the blockages."

News.title: Man City charges LIVE: Punishment agreement, UEFA consider action, HMRC investigation revealed
News.content:
Manchester City are still waiting to discover their punishment for being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules, though they have appealed the decision

Hello and welcome to Mirror Football's live blog on Wednesday, October 7, where we will bring you the latest after an independent commission found Manchester City guilty of breaking Premier League rules in a strongly-worded report released last week.

City were found to have inflated revenue by more than £830million over a nine-season period between 2009-10 and 2017-18. However, the Etihad club have since appealed against the decision and continue to deny any wrongdoing.

However, it is being reported that Premier League clubs believe City should be expelled from the top flight next season if their appeal against the financial charges fails. That’s according to Sky Sports, who are reporting that clubs in the top-flight believe a points deduction would not be sufficient if it resulted in City spending just one season outside the Premier League.

UEFA are also believed to be monitoring developments and will wait until the end of the Premier League's disciplinary process before deciding whether to take any potential action against City.

The Financial Times is reporting that HMRC probed City in 2018 over whether it used complex arrangements to underpay tax. The report claims a civil investigation into the club’s tax affairs followed the publication of leaked internal emails by Der Spiegel in 2018. The Financial Times says Man City and HMRC declined to comment.

And former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher believes City should face a multi-year punishment for their financial misdemeanours. There is still much discussion about potential outcomes, so stay right here for all of the latest...

News.title: 'I ruined a marriage by telling the mum what her child's name really means'
News.content:
'I ruined a marriage by telling the mum what her child's name really means'

A childcare worker has revealed how she accidentally 'ruined a marriage' after telling a confused mum what her daughter's name really meant, and now she's riddled with guilt

View Image The mum is now living with her parents (stock image) (Image: Getty Images/Tetra images RF)

While some parents name their children after loved ones, others turn to their favourite books, films and TV shows for inspiration. But one mum was left stunned after discovering the real reason her husband had chosen their daughter's unusual name - and she only found out when it was too late to change it.

‌



‌



A childcare worker has now revealed how she believes she "ruined a marriage" after accidentally exposing the truth to the oblivious mum, and she has been left riddled with guilt ever since. Taking to Reddit, the woman explained that she works in childcare and had recently welcomed a new baby named Vriska. She said: "I work in childcare and recently we enrolled a new baby named Vriska. Now we are encouraged to build a rapport with the parents and to talk about them about shared interests whenever possible, so I often talk to some parents about nerdy things or others about fashion and make up etc.

‌



"When I meet the mother for a pick up I told her how cool it was that her child was named Vriska (even though I personally don’t think it’s cool to name your children after your fandoms but I wasn’t about to say that) and told her that I also loved Homestuck thinking it would be a quick way to build rapport."

‌



However, the mum gave her a look of genuine confusion before asking what Homestuck was.

She added: "I told her it was a comic and one of the characters was called Vriska but sensing the awkward air I quickly said 'Oh nevermind! "It’s probably a coincidence, don’t mind me, haha!'

"I was confused because I’m sure the name Vriska didn’t exist before Homestuck."

‌



It's a 'cute, original name'

The mum then explained that Vriska was a "cute, original name" her husband had come up with, inspired by the word "Vrishchika", which is Hindi for Scorpio.

She added: "Apparently he went so far as to create a fake paper trail of his research and showed her books and sites on the word Vrishchika so she’d believe him without looking into it.

‌



"She’s one of those crystals and astrology types, and was gushing about how thoughtful he was because he’s not into her beliefs and that he thinks they’re stupid so it was such a sweet gesture for him to go into so much trouble researching a name that aligned with her beliefs.

"I’m just nodding along politely because I’m internally losing my mind."

But the childcare worker soon discovered that her innocent comment had uncovered far more than she had expected.

‌



The next thing she knew, the mum had pulled her daughter out of daycare and moved in with her parents.

'She personally thanked me'

The mum also thanked the childcare worker for telling her the truth about her daughter's name.

The worker added: "She personally thanked me because she googled Vriska and got her now ex to fess up the whole truth.

‌



"[He told her] basically that he really loved character Vriska and that she didn’t know about it because that love was of the ‘waifu’* love rather then the ‘I relate to this character’ love.

"As you can imagine she was furious and decided to leave her husband for lying to her, among other things.

"I’m honestly guilt ridden that I directly shattered a marriage and now baby Vriska will suffer because of this, which is why I think I could be the a***hole, I don’t know the whole story, maybe he’s a really good father?

Article continues below

"But I also think maybe I’m not the a***hole because who wants a husband who quite frankly sounds manipulative and insane."

*Waifu is a term used to describe a fictional female character that someone feels a romantic or sexual attraction towards.

News.title: Dr Amir Khan says everyone born before 1990 should have £20 item at home
News.content:
Dr Amir Khan says everyone born before 1990 should have £20 item at home

The popular ITV regular claims it is important once people reach a certain age

View 2 Images Dr Amir Khan claims these devices could be 'life-saving' (Image: ITV)

Dr Amir Khan, known for his appearances on ITV's daytime shows like Lorraine and This Morning, claims that people over the age of 35 should consider investing in an at-home blood pressure testing device. These pieces of equipment do not have to be expensive, with options available online from the likes of Argos, Amazon, Boots, Superdrug and more.

‌



‌



Speaking on his No Appointment Necessary podcast, he said: "First of all, high blood pressure is a silent killer. You don't know you've got high blood pressure often until you've had a heart attack, or you've got eye disease, or you have a random blood test that shows you've got kidney disease.

‌



"Having a blood pressure monitor at home could be absolutely life-saving for you." For most people born before the 1990s (aged 35 and up), Dr Khan suggests checking once a fortnight.

‌



He added that people who are younger may also benefit from having access to a device at home, as well as those who have a family history of "high blood pressure, type 2 diabetes or heart attacks".

Content cannot be displayed without consent

What is the ideal blood pressure range?

According to the NHS website: "You're usually considered to have high blood pressure if your reading is 140/90 or higher when checked by a healthcare professional or 135/85 or higher when checked at home."

‌



Dr Khan claims on his podcast that people with regular readings "above 135 over 85" should monitor their situation more closely than the average person. He suggested "two or three times a day for a week" to establish an "average pattern" and, if consistent, then these readings should be taken to "see your doctor".

If your blood pressure is too high, it puts extra strain on your blood vessels, heart and other organs, such as your brain, kidneys and eyes. If it's not treated, it can increase your risk of serious conditions such as heart attacks, strokes, kidney disease and vascular dementia.

View 2 Images Having one of these monitors at home could be life-saving (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

Can high blood pressure be managed or 'reversed'?

Doctors will usually prescribe medication for high blood pressure based on your age, ethnicity, and underlying health conditions. These medications are often long-term solutions.

In early or specific cases, hypertension can be 'reversed' to normal levels through lifestyle changes or by treating an underlying cause. Healthy lifestyle changes can help lower your blood pressure into an 'ideal' range (below 120/80).

The NHS suggests adopting a "healthy, balanced diet" paired with at least 150 minutes of regular exercise a week. Alongside this, people should avoid too much salt, alcohol or caffeine and quit smoking if that is a part of their lifestyle. News.title: I thought it was 'period cramps' - then lost half my stomach to cancer
News.content:
I thought it was 'period cramps' - then lost half my stomach to cancer

Kirsty said she went into 'immediate shock' after hearing the diagnosis

View 3 Images Kirsty Adam thought her stomach cramps were period-related before being diagnosed with a rare cancer (Image: Kirsty Adam © SWNS)

A woman went to her GP after she kept getting stomach cramps she couldn’t explain. At first, she was told it was likely linked to her period cycle, but within weeks, her health began to deteriorate in ways that didn't fit.

‌



‌



Over the next two months, Kirsty Adam began losing weight and experiencing diarrhoea alongside intense abdominal pain. She says she felt dismissed more than once, with the symptoms later being put down to food poisoning, but the discomfort kept returning and becoming harder to manage as she tried to carry on with day-to-day life.

‌



By May 2026, the 33-year-old childcare worker from Glasgow went back again, and this time her GP referred her to Glasgow Royal Infirmary because of concerns it could be related to her appendix. At the hospital, she had blood tests and was asked to provide a stool sample as doctors tried to narrow down what was going on.

‌



With her dad living with Crohn’s disease, Kirsty suspected she might be facing the same condition. She went into the next stage of testing expecting an inflammatory bowel diagnosis rather than anything more serious.

View 3 Images Kirsty first started experiencing stomach cramps in March 2026 (Image: Kirsty Adam © SWNS)

The stool results indicated significant blood, and she was booked in for a colonoscopy. It was after that procedure, she says, that a doctor told her she had cancer, news that left her stunned and struggling to take in what was being said.

‌



Speaking to Talk to the Press, Kirsty described mentally shutting down in the moment, with her partner taking in the details on her behalf. She said: "As soon as they mentioned cancer, I just stared at the door handle, wanting to run out of the room."

A portion of the tumour was then sent away for biopsy to confirm exactly what doctors were dealing with. In June 2026, Kirsty was told she had squamous cell carcinoma in the bowel, a form of cancer so rare that specialists needed to rule out the possibility it had gone elsewhere.

View 3 Images Kirsty suspected she could have Crohn's disease before getting her real diagnosis (Image: Kirsty Adam © SWNS)

‌



She underwent scans of her head, neck and cervix to check for another primary cancer, but those tests came back clear. According to Kirsty, she was then advised that chemotherapy was unlikely to be effective for this particular type, leaving surgery as the main option.

Surgeons carried out a six-and-a-half-hour operation to remove the tumour, along with part of her bowel and half of her stomach. Kirsty says she was told the procedure was vital, and that without it she might not have survived.

Now recovering, she lives with a stoma bag and returns for CT scans every six months so clinicians can monitor for any sign of recurrence. She says she is clinging to the hope that her bowel will heal enough for the stoma to be reversed in future.

Article continues below

Kirsty also spoke about the emotional impact of the changes to her body following surgery. She said adapting to the stoma has been difficult, and that she is still coming to terms with the scar and the daily reality of managing the bag.

News.title: Freed Hamas hostage Emily Hand, 11, finally able to sleep alone at night three years after horror
News.content:
Freed Hamas hostage Emily Hand, 11, finally able to sleep alone at night three years after horror

Emily Hand's dad said: "She's stopped pulling her mattress right up to mine in the middle of the night, and is now almost entirely independent - much to my relief”

View 5 Images Brave Emily Hand with her beloved dog Johnsey (Image: Paul Martin/Cap-Rep.net)

Freed Hamas child hostage Emily Hand is bravely finally coming to terms with her horrific ordeal on the third anniversary of the October 7th attacks.

‌



‌



She was just eight when she was snatched by Hamas gunmen, and had her ninth birthday while being held for 49 days. Now in an exclusive interview with the Mirror, her dad, Irishman Thomas Hand, said his daughter, now 11, was growing stronger every day.

‌



He revealed that his daughter had only "in the last month or so" stopped needing to climb into his bed at night to feel secure from her fear of attack or kidnapping.

‌



He said: "She's stopped pulling her mattress right up to mine in the middle of the night, and is now almost entirely independent - much to my relief. And she's also just recently stopped calling me on her mobile phone to come and fetch her from a friend’s house after dark on our temporary kibbutz."

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 5 Images Emily Hand is loving horse riding again (Image: Paul Martin/Cap-Rep.net)

‌



Donald Trump reveals US bombers removed from RAF Fairford after 'threats' READ MORE :

Emily and her dad, like many of those who were attacked on Kibbutz Be'eri, on the border with Gaza, have been given prefab houses on a kibbutz that is further from the border and was not attacked on October 7.

Thomas said: “We're really looking forward immensely to moving back to our first kibbutz, Be'eri, which until the attack was seen by me and by Emily as paradise.

View 5 Images Emily Hand will pay respects on the 3rd anniversary of 7th October attacks (Image: Paul Martin/Cap-Rep.net)

‌



"I'm still a bit nervous though - literally and figuratively - about trying to build our lives up again there. Many houses and buildings on our kibbutz remain wrecked, including the kindergarten and playground. And it's so close to Gaza, from where we were attacked."

He and Emily are due to go back to Be'eri "for a very emotional reunion of all our kibbutz members and friends" on October 7.

It’s the third anniversary of the attack that left 102 people from his kibbutz dead and led to 34 others being taken hostage. All but four of the kibbutz's hostages eventually returned alive.

‌



View 5 Images Emily's brave dad Thomas Hand (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Horse-riding has been Emily's main outdoor pursuit - and also, according to her psychologists, a means of making her feel she is in control rather than a buffeted victim.

"With her love for animals -- though she's no longer obsessed with snails -- she hopes one day to become a vet," said Thomas.

‌



Emily's beloved pet dog Johnsey still sleeps cuddled up to her every night. The dog came with Thomas in an Israeli military vehicle as Emily was about to be brought back across the Gaza border into Israel.

For their reunion, Thomas knew Emily loved her pet so much she would hug the animal first, "and I could then get the second hug". He said: "I thought in her child's mind she would feel like I had betrayed her - by not coming to save her from the gunmen."

View 5 Images Brave Emily Hand (Image: Paul Martin/Cap-Rep.net)

‌



However, in fact Emily rushed straight into her father's arms, with Johnsey yapping at her heels; a moment Thomas still looks back on with delight and amazement.

Recently Thomas and Emily got a surprise visit from one of the most famous hostages, Noa Argamani, who had been held with Emily for most of her 49 days in captivity, alongside her friend Hilla, who kidnapped when she was 12.

Thomas said: “Noa just turned up unannounced, and she and the two girls sat outside on our porch and chatted and laughed. These sort of meetings with ex-hostages take place occasionally, and though they stir up hard memories, they're in some way therapeutic."

‌



Argamani had been filmed terrified on the back of a kidnapper's motorbike, then, after Emily and Hilla's return, had disappeared for over year until being rescued in a raid by Israeli troops.

Thomas added: “Back on our destroyed kibbutz tomorrow, I'll be thinking of all of those 102 dead people. I knew all of them so well. The freedom-loving Western world should help us make sure we are never subjected to these vicious terrorist onslaughts again.”

More than 1,200 people were killed when Hamas gunmen stormed through the border fence on October 7th 2023. 36 of them were children. A total of 251 people were taken hostage. All living hostages were freed by the end of 2025.

Article continues below

The Palestinian Ministry of Health said the death toll of Gazans stood at more than 74,000 with 172,000 injured. Israel launched air strikes immediately after October 7th, and a full scale ground invasion on October 27th 2023.

News.title: Premium Bond holders told to 'watch prize rate' as NS&I 'steps up its game' with major October change
News.content:
Premium Bond holders told to 'watch prize rate' as NS&I 'steps up its game' with major October change

AJ Bell's head of personal finance says all eyes will be on Premium Bonds in the coming weeks

View 2 Images Premium Bond holders could see a rise in the prize rate

A financial expert says Premium Bond holders will be keeping a close eye on prize rates in the coming weeks after NS&I announced new issues of British Savings Bonds on sale with increased rates. NS&I, which is the UK Government savings bank, has launched new fixed-rate savings accounts paying up to 5.17 per cent interest.

‌



‌



Being Government-backed, it is also the only savings provider that secures savings in excess of £120,000 - which is the maximum protected by the FSCS Deposit Protection Limit. The added protection combined with the increased savings rate make it an even more attractive option for savers.

‌



But Sarah Coles, head of personal finance at AJ Bell, says that all eyes will be on Premium Bond rates, which are also set by NS&I. Your money does not accrue interest in Premium Bonds, but you are instead entered into a monthly prize draw.

‌



Ms Coles said that, given that there had already been two rate rises this year, a third was not out of the question - especially given the Bank of England could raise interest rates before the year is out.

She said: “NS&I is stepping up its game to compete in a tough market. It’s boosting the rates on its fixed rate bonds for the fourth time in less than four months. They’re pretty substantial hikes too, which put them within shouting distance of the best on the market. It’s a sign of just how hard the organisation is having to work to attract cash.

“NS&I has a duty to balance the needs of savers with those of taxpayers, so they are careful not to over-pay. However, they are pushing harder than they usually do. The three-year rate is now among the top 10 most competitive in the market, while the fixed rates for other periods are in the top 20.

‌



“Loyal NS&I customers who are wedded to the brand will be paying less of a price than in previous years for their staying power if they snap up these fixed rate deals.

View 2 Images Money in Permium Bonds does not accrue interest in Premium Bonds, but you are instead entered into a monthly prize draw

Better rates 'elsewhere'

“However, you can still make more money elsewhere – with 5.12 per cent available over a year and 5.35 per cent over five. For those drawn by the 100 per cent Treasury guarantee, there’s every chance they have the protection they need from the FSCS guarantee on the first £120,000 saved with each institution.

‌



“So it’s well worth checking cash savings hubs and online banks, which tend to offer competitive deals.

“The fact NS&I’s rates have been hiked yet again owes much to the fact that the market is so competitive right now. In August, NS&I revealed that in the first three months of its financial year it had raised just £1 billion of its £15 billion target, so it needs to knuckle down to secure some serious fundraising. It’s going to hope that this latest round of hikes will be enough to move the dial.

Premium Bonds

“Premium Bond fans will be keen to know whether we will see the Premium Bond prize rate rise again too.

Article continues below

“We’ve already seen it increased in July and September, so it currently sits at 4.35 per cent. Another increase could make the bonds more attractive and raise even more money for N&SI, even if the prize fund rate doesn’t actually mean holders are guaranteed to make any money on their holding.

“It isn’t out of the question considering how ferocious the savings market is right now, especially if the Bank of England decides to raise rates next month.”

News.title: Man badly burnt saving his dog after freak accident watching TV
News.content:
Man badly burnt saving his dog after freak accident watching TV

He was more concerned about her injuries while his own were getting worse

View 6 Images Lorraine, Christian and Peaches

A devoted dog owner suffered horrific burns rescuing his dog from scalding hot water. Christian Barker was enjoying a night in watching television with his Cavapoo, Peaches, when the freak accident occurred.

‌



‌



The hot water bottle he had behind his back to ease sciatica pain exploded suddenly, splitting “like a sack” down the middle. Filled with boiling water, terrified Peaches yelped with pain and soiled herself in shock as she was doused in the liquid.

‌



Christian, from Essex, picked up the scalded pup and rushed her to the kitchen to soak under cold water, before dashing to the emergency clinic – not realising her was burning himself in the process, and that his were worsening.

‌



View 6 Images Christian and Peaches on their first day back from the vets

He said: “All I was thinking about was Peaches – I just felt so, so guilty that she’d been hurt and in my head I just felt that everything was my fault and that I’d killed the dog. About 15-20 minutes into the journey, I began to feel really excruciating pain in my right thigh.

“It had been tingling a bit before that, but in the scrambled way my brain was at the time, I just assumed it was because I was soaking wet.”

‌



Peaches was treated at the emergency Vets Now clinic, where Christian’s wife, Lorraine, had phoned ahead to warn them of the unfolding drama. Staff took Peaches for urgent burns treatment, by which point Christian’s own injuries were becoming more apparent to him – leaving him “frantically” taking off his clothes that were sticking to his inflamed skin.

View 6 Images Peaches' burn wound

Veterinary nurse and first-aider Sophie Watson ushered him through to the staff shower room where he was able to get privacy and douse himself with cool water.

‌



Sophie said: “I’ve worked in vet clinics for 25 years and, as a trained first-aider, there have been a few times where I’ve needed to help humans as well as pets. But I’ve never been in a situation as critical as this.

“All the way from his chest down his right side, his skin was completely scalded and was very rapidly blistering. I phoned 999, but unfortunately there weren’t any ambulances available, so we made arrangements for Christian’s uncle and his wife to take him to accident and emergency.

View 6 Images Peaches on day one of recovery

‌



“Overall, he was in and out of the shower for an hour and a half just trying to contain the injuries as best we could, and all the time he kept asking, ‘How’s Peaches, how’s Peaches?’

“We meet a lot of very devoted owners, but I don’t think I’ve ever met someone quite as visibly attached to their pet as Christian – it was really quite humbling to see how, even though his injuries were much worse than his dog’s, it was the dog he was concerned for, not himself.

“Of course, there were no clothes he could put on – so we had to dress him in one of the blue clinical gowns that we use when operating on a pet. Then I arranged for the car to come to our side door so that Christian didn’t have to walk out through our main reception half-dressed.”

‌



View 6 Images Peaches was badly injured

While this was going on, Sophie’s colleagues were giving Peaches analgesia and intravenous fluids while continuing to cool her skin. At Ipswich Hospital, specialist burns staff wrapped Christian’s injuries in layers of cling film before then peeling off the scalded skin.

Christian said: “It was incredibly painful, but I was in safe hands and incredibly grateful for the excellent treatment I received – not to mention the first-class help Peaches got.”

‌



After a night under observation, Peaches was well enough to leave the clinic at 8 am the next day and even ate a little bit of chicken before she went – with her shaved fur showing very extensive burns down her left side.

And Christian got home later that day too. He said: “When I saw Peaches I nearly burst into tears – the Vets Now staff had done a brilliant job keeping her alive, but they were very honest with Lorraine that recovery wasn’t guaranteed.

“And after a day or so at home she took a bit of a turn for the worse and didn’t want to drink or eat. We had to give her water through a syringe and try, and hand feed her.”

‌



View 6 Images Peaches has now recovered

Day by day though, Peaches began to get a little stronger, whilst Christian as well began to get better. He said: “Our two recoveries have kind of mirrored each other – which feels very fitting.”

Peaches is now back to her normal self – chasing after her ball and back with Christian on the sofa barking at her favourite bit of TV: a dog food advert. And Christian is back in his full-time carer role, looking after Lorraine, who has rheumatoid arthritis.

‌



Lorraine said: “We’re used to some pretty challenging circumstances in our family – but this really has been very difficult for all of us. It happened in October last year, but it’s all very raw still - it feels like it was yesterday.

“After the accident we have thrown out all our hot water bottles, and we’ll never, ever, again have one in the house. The one that exploded was one of the long thin ones that a lot of people use for back pain and was almost new, so it’s not like it was ancient and out of date.

“I’m just so grateful to Sophie and her colleagues and always will be – in our hour of need they saved my husband, and they saved my dog. I literally do not know what we’d have done if they hadn’t been there to help.”

Article continues below

Sophie, who recently won a Vets Now customer star award for her work with Christian, said: “It was a total team effort and I’m lucky to work with brilliant colleagues. I have to say: Peaches is such a cute little character – and she’s very brave too.

“We’re all just so touched that she and Christian have made full recoveries. This job can be a bit of an emotional roller-coaster at times, and a happy outcome like this with such lovely feedback from Christian and Lorraine is something we just treasure as a team.”

News.title: What we know about Christa Pike’s ‘unprecedented' recovery
News.content:
US death row inmate Christa Pike is "conscious and speaking" after surviving a failed execution attempt in the US state of Tennessee last week. Pike continues to receive critical medical care while handcuffed in hospital, according to a statement from her attorneys on Tuesday.

An aneasthesiologist advising Pike's defence team said her survival is highly unusual, and while her prognosis remains unclear, "at a minimum, we expect a long recovery".

The BBC's Sarah Smith breaks down recent events after Pike's failed execution.
