News.title: UK not prepared for food shortages, experts warn
News.content:
Britain has no way to feed its population of 66 million people in a crisis, a letter addressed to the Prime Minister has warned.

Climate change, cyber-attacks, geopolitical shifts, and energy shocks could put Britain’s food supply at great risk – and the UK is “complacent”, the letter says.

The document was delivered to Andy Burnham on Monday and was signed by 180 experts including academics, farmers, local council leaders, and foodbank workers.

Britain’s food supply is now heavily globalised, with roughly 45-50 per cent of food imported from countries like Spain, the Netherlands and France, as well as South Africa, Columbia and Brazil.

The system provides a cheap and constant supply of food – seasonal or not – but if international supply chains are disrupted, the UK’s home production is “woefully inadequate in [being able to produce] many different food types” , the letter argues.

It adds that “international food supplies can be weaponised”.

Crucially, the UK operates a ‘just-in-time’ food system – meaning hardly any food is stocked and stored in reserves, but is constantly moving from farms and ports directly to supermarket and wholesale shelves when needed.

“When you go to a supermarket and check out, you think, well, ‘it’s adding up the bill’ – it is, but what it’s also doing is reordering,” Tim Lang, emeritus professor of food policy at City University, a signatory of the letter and author of the Just in Case report – a major review that analysed the UK’s food system for the National Preparedness Commission, previously told The Telegraph.

News.title: Kenya confirms first ever case of Ebola after man dies in Nairobi
News.content:
Kenya confirmed its first ever case of Ebola on Tuesday after a Kenyan citizen who had travelled from the Democratic Republic of Congo died in Nairobi.

Kenya is the third country to record a case linked to the Ebola epidemic in eastern Congo, the second largest on record. Uganda reported 20 cases and two deaths earlier in the year but was declared Ebola-free in August.

The patient had been ill for about a month before travelling ‌by road ‌from Congo to ⁠Uganda’s capital, Kampala, and then flying to Nairobi on Saturday, health minister Aden Duale told a news conference.

After arriving at Nairobi’s international airport, he passed through health screening and was later taken by a relative to Nairobi ⁠Hospital. He was admitted with fever, chills and bleeding beneath the skin and was quickly placed in isolation, Duale said.

He died late on Monday.

News.title: Tories promise to scrap Labour’s mansion tax
News.content:
The Tories have pledged to scrap Labour’s “mansion tax” on homes worth more than £2m.

Andrew Griffith, the shadow chancellor, pledged to abolish the “vindictive levy” in his keynote speech to the Conservative Party conference, warning it would hit people living in “ordinary homes”.

Under the tax, which was announced by Labour last year, properties valued at more than £2m face an extra levy on their council tax from 2028.

The shadow chancellor said: “They pretend it’s a mansion tax, but it will hit people here in Birmingham, in Manchester, and those living in ordinary homes making long commutes to our capital city. For many, it will be simply unaffordable.”

He pledged to follow in the footsteps of Nigel Lawson, Margaret Thatcher’s chancellor, and cut one tax at every Budget if the his party returns to power.

Elsewhere in his speech, Mr Griffith promised to scrap a net zero “grocery tax” which pushes up the cost of the weekly shop and cut the cost of a new build by £50,000.

The shadow chancellor also accused previous Tory leaders of failing to govern as free market conservatives, and said Andy Burnham and John Healey want to take Britain back to a “socialist fever dream of the 1970s”.

News.title: How worried should we be about the Russian plague lab leak?
News.content:
A fire breaks out at a laboratory in Siberia where secretive research into infectious diseases is taking place. A technician, racked with guilt over the accident, disappears into the tundra and shoots himself. Hunters discover his body, but what they don’t realise is it is infected with a manipulated version of the plague bacterium. The pathogen quickly spreads around the world, wreaking death and destruction at a scale unprecedented in human history.

This is the plot of Biological War: A Scenario, a recent book by US author Annie Jacobsen which imagines what could happen if a weaponised bacterium escaped from a laboratory.

The book describes an absolute worst-case scenario but the beginnings of this fictionalised pandemic share an eerie similarity with events in Russia over the last week. Reports have emerged about the death of a 28 year old female worker at the Antiplague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East in Shelekho, a city in Irkutsk. Rospotrebnadzor, the country’s infectious disease agency, said the woman was diagnosed with a “pneumonia of unknown origin”.

However, according to reports in Russian media the woman, identified as Daria Shipilova, died of pneumonic plague after dropping a test tube filled with live samples of the pathogen, Yersinia pestis. She was taken to hospital on Tuesday September 29 but died two days later. Nearly 200 contacts are now being monitored for signs of the disease, according to media reports.

So how worried should we be?

Sports.title: Lionel Messi breaks down in tears alongside Argentina team-mates as he scores in highly emotional final game
Sports.content:
Next

EMOTIONAL Lionel Messi scored in his final Argentina game as he brought his incredible 21-year international career to an end.

And a tearful Enzo Fernandez led the tributes for his country’s iconic retiring star.



The World Cup finalists welcomed Benin to Buenos Aires as they fielded their superstar No10 one last time.

A sellout 85,000 crowd watched as Messi walked out for the match alongside his kids; Thiago, 13, Mateo, 10, and Ciro, eight.



The 39-year-old was then in tears as the Argentine national anthem was sung by Fabio Santana, a veteran of the Falklands War, while a huge “Messi 10” shirt lay over the pitch.

Messi’s 208th and final international match then got underway, but was paused after just 10 minutes, marking the ex-Barcelona star’s squad number, for him to receive another ovation from the highly-charged crowd.



Fireworks went off during the stoppage as Messi waved to his adoring public.

As the first half wore on, Messi missed a pair of golden chances to score.



But Argentina were not to be denied, and it was their retiring star’s corner that was fired home by his fellow veteran Nicolas Otamendi on 48 minutes.

Messi then grabbed another assist just after the hour mark, poking the ball over to Nico Paz.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The Como attacker, a front-runner to succeed Messi as his country’s No10, then fittingly curled in a left-footed shot that his hero would have been proud of.

When Argentina were awarded a penalty on 70 minutes, only one man was ever going to take it.



Messi stepped up to convert, scoring his 126th and final international goal.

When the final whistle sounded, Messi was lovingly mobbed by his team-mates – plenty of whom then paid emotional tribute.

Manchester City star Fernandez said: “We will miss Leo… how much did I cry tonight, incredible.”



Messi’s World Cup-winning manager Lionel Scaloni added: “We will now build with new talents, new young players, we will look at new ways… but I have never seen such aura like Lionel Messi has.

“We will start a new chapter, but what Leo transmits, that’s impossible to replace.”

Manchester United‘s Lisandro Martinez said: “I told Leo Messi that I love him with all my heart.”



Messi himself gave a 10 minute speech to the crowd, calling it the “most difficult day” of his career to quit Argentina.

He said: “I have nothing left but to give thanks; it was pride for me to represent this jersey for 20 years. Even in the worst moments, I never stopped fighting, giving my all, and wanting to always be here.

“Not coming back anymore will be a huge pain, I’d love to come forever because playing for Argentina is the most beautiful thing that can happen.”

On his achievements, Messi continued: “I thank my team-mates for this time that I got to share with this group.

“They made me fulfill my childhood dream, of being a world champion, of Copa America, of Finalissima… I knew I was surrounded by warriors who gave their lives.”



Messi’s Inter Miami and Argentina team-mate Rodrigo De Paul said of his close friend: “He made me grow not only as a footballer, but also as a person.

“I became a better person, a better human being, a better athlete, a better father and a better friend.

“I want to tell him that I love him. He knows that he is my brother and that he has an enormous heart.”



And long-time Argentina running mate Angel Di Maria added: “Seeing him with so much happiness, and that tranquillity of knowing that he gave everything he had, is what makes us all happy.

“I thank him for life.”

Ex-Barca pal Neymar wrote on Instagram: “Whoever loves football has enjoyed it over the years…

Today is your last game with the jersey of your team, of your country and I hope you enjoy every second, that all the tributes today make you happy.

“It’s not just Argentina that thanks you, the world thanks you for everything you did for football.

“Thank you for making me love football even more, it was an honour to have played against you and even more to make history by your side.

“THANKS @leomessi”.

Sports.title: ‘I am in great shape’ – Harry Kane hints he could break Cristiano Ronaldo’s record of 146 international goals
Sports.content:

HARRY KANE equalled Peter Shilton’s all-time England caps record with a double – then targeted becoming the greatest international goalscorer.

Kane, 33, levelled legendary keeper Shilts on 125 appearances for the Three Lions with a brilliant display as England cruised past the Czech Republic 3-0.



The Bayern Munich hotshot scored his 90th and 91st goal for England either side of half-time after his 27th-minute cross forced Vladimir Coufal to turn the opener into his own net.

After adding even more goals to his tally, Kane set his eyes on Cristiano Ronaldo’s astonishing international goalscoring record of 146 goals.



The England skipper said: “That’s maybe the ceiling we’re talking about, see how far we can get.

“That is another 50 odd goals. It’s an awful long way away right now, but who knows.

“I am in great shape. I’ve said before about some of the players who have played well into their late 30s and still at the highest level, and even 40s now.

“It’s season by season for me. As long as I feel like I can help the team and be available for the team, I’ll be around.

“At the moment I feel like I can help the team a lot and that’s just the way I am.

“We will have to see. Let’s see if we get to 100 first and then we’ll go from there.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Ronaldo, who is yet to retire from international football, has scored his 146 goals in 234 appearances for Portugal.

Kane, who is already England’s record goalscorer, will have a long way to go, having just earned his 125th cap and is focusing on celebrating that achievement first.

He added: “There are so many milestones throughout a career.



“I look back to my England debut and how much of a dream that was and I think this is even beyond my wildest dreams.

“To be joint at 125 has been a privilege.

“I love coming to every England camp and I love playing in every game and representing my country in the best way possible.

“Tonight was a special night, and the most important thing is the win.”



The veteran striker got his first goal on the evening with a close-range finish from Morgan Rogers’ excellent ball.

And he headed home Lewis Hall’s corner to make it 3-0.

England boss Thomas Tuchel said: “He delivers all the time; it makes no difference.

“It’s of course special that he did it when he equals the record with Peter Shilton. If it needed any proof, it doesn’t of course, he shows it again and again.



He had a very good performance again. He played all four matches for us, he was eager to play and start all four matches. He is a top captain.”

BAYERN MUNICH are the latest club to join the transfer race for wantaway Manchester United wonderkid JJ Gabriel, according to reports.

The teen turned 16 on Tuesday, opening the door for him to depart Old Trafford and Carrington for clubs in Europe following his demand to leave last month.



German giants Bayern Munich are one such club and might have moved ahead of rivals in the chase after contacting Gabriel’s camp this week.

That follows previous contact between the two parties in May, while the likes of Real Madrid, Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona are all known to be interested as well, though the latter club has publicly distanced themselves.



Vincent Kompany, the former Manchester City defender who is now the Bavarians boss, is a big fan of Gabriel, who requested United cancel his registration because of a lack of involvement in the first team.

However, Sky Sports report Gabriel’s camp is demanding an incredible seven-figure salary.

Although, as reported by The Times, whether that includes a spot in the senior team at Bayern remains to be seen.

They have fast-tracked players to the senior side in the past, having promoted Lennart Karl as a 17-year-old from their Under-19s last year.

Gabriel holds an EU passport via Irish and Cypriot relatives which allows him to join any club located in the European Union.

Sports.title: Three things we learned from England win over Czechia as two stars stake claim and Kane could reach 150 goals
Sports.content:

ENGLAND completed an impressive week with a 3-0 victory over Czechia at Wembley.

Hot on the heels of their 7-0 demolition of Croatia, Thomas Tuchel‘s men celebrated Harry Kane winning his record-equalling 125th cap with another dominant display.



Kane grabbed himself a brace and played a major part in the Czechs scoring an own goal.

That takes his international tally to an incredible 91 strikes.



England are all but through to the semi-finals of the Nations League with tonight’s results.

A Mikel Merino brace helped Spain beat Croatia. England could lose their last two games and Croatia could win both and they would STILL have to lose to Croatia 8-0 to go out.



But England look more attack minded with every passing game following their meek World Cup exit this summer. Here are three things we learned from tonight’s victory.

Harry Kane keeps finding new levels

Harry Kane showed for the umpteenth time why he’s England’s main man.

The captain equaled Peter Shilton’s record of 125 caps and marked it with two goals to take his haul to a whopping 91 international strikes.

His first was a clinical first- time finish from a dynamic move on 40 minutes. His second was a clinical header from Lewis Hall‘s corner just before the hour.

He’ll get to 100 goals soon enough and it does not seem implausible that he could one day reach 150.

Trent vs. Quansah

Why not play both? The pair have been vying for the right back slot throughout this elongated international break but here they played together with Bayer Leverkusen man Quansah starting at centre-back.

The Czechs never really posed that much of a threat but the combination worked well enough.

Trent had some nice contributions going forward and almost broke the deadlock with an excellent free kick.



England’s wingers

Sports.title: Scotland 1 Slovenia 2: Scots facing NIGHTMARE route to Euro 2028 after letting lead slip in brutal start for Pocognoli
Sports.content:
Next

SCOTLAND’S miserable second-half collapse left them staring at a tougher route to Euro 2028 after a streetwise Slovenia sealed a well-earned comeback win.

New boss Sebastien Pocognoli suffered back-to-back home defeats at Hampden, after Ryan Christie‘s first half backheel was quickly cancelled out after the break.



With group leaders Switzerland pulling away, Scotland and Slovenia are locked in an unofficial battle for a runners-up spot in their Nations League B1 group.

The decision to start Christie paid off when the Bournemouth midfielder cheekily flicked home a close range opener inside 31 minutes after Jack Hendry – back from suspension – headed off the post.



A win would have put Scotland second in Group B1 with two games left to play. Finishing runner-up guarantees a higher seeding pot for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw in Ireland in December.



But the visitors turned on the style as Aljosa Matko and Danijel Sturm took turns providing and scoring to suck the life out of a flat Glasgow crowd.

First Matko raced through in behind the Scottish high-line and slotted in to pull level 11 minutes after the restart.

Sturm lashed an effort over the bar and Matko was denied a second by the offside flag before they did take the lead. The pair combined again, with Sturm guiding the ball home.

Sliding into Pot 3 would leave Scotland facing a nightmare path to Euro 2028 against tougher European competition, making the race for one of two reserved host-nation automatic spots all the more critical.



The Scots host North Macedonia next month on Friday 13 before travelling to Switzerland, who cruised to a 3-0 win at Hampden last week following Hendry‘s early red card.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Questions will be asked about Pocognoli’s dangerous high line, after Slovenia, who picked up just their third win in the last 13 matches, capitalised on the gaping holes with countless runs beyond the wall to let rip at Angus Gunn’s goal.

Matko’s low driven finish, followed by a fast move where the scorer provided a rolled cross across the face of goal for an unmarked Sturm, resulted in Scotland suffering successive home defeats for the first time since 2019.

The wait went on for Hull striker Oli McBurnie, who was hauled off on 66 minutes and is yet to score in 20 caps after a long exile under ex-boss Steve Clarke.

Clarke was in the building to honour skipper Robertson’s 101st cap, and the Tottenham full back somewhat proved his worth with a heroic sliding block to deny Zan Vipotnik on the stroke of half-time, but ultimately suffered a sour evening.



Sub Josh McPake made a strong impact in the final 15 minutes, but Slovenia picked up a rare away win and first ever victory against the Scots across seven meetings.

It could have been worse for Pocognoli, who has suffered two defeats in his opening four matches, as Hendry was forced to clear Adam Gnezda Cerin’s early effort off the line.

Scotland lost against a side outside the top 50 Fifa ranked nations for the first time in 17 competitive games.

On a night that started with the return of his three predecessors – Gordon Strachan, Alex McLeish and Clarke – for a presentation marking Robertson’s century of caps, the new boss was schooled off the park.

Robertson told BBC Scotland: “Not good enough. The whole team on the pitch, I don’t think it was a good performance at all.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“It’s been a long camp, I don’t know if it was down to tiredness, but as far as I’m concerned, Slovenia have played the same amount of games as us. They looked a lot fresher, a lot more hungry.

“As Scotland, we might lack quality or make mistakes, but I don’t think people accept being outfought. I think that’s what happened tonight.”

Sports.title: Eberechi Eze makes Anthony Gordon look even more undroppable as Arsenal star struggles to seize England chance
Sports.content:
Next

EBERECHI EZE had the chance to put some pressure on Anthony Gordon – but ended up making the man of the moment look even more undroppable.

Barcelona winger Gordon is in the form of his life having caused carnage in the other three England games during this elongated international break.



The electric wideman was bench here, though, presumably to manage his load in a game that turned out to be the routine victory many expected.

In his place came Eze, a man who Thomas Tuchel has shown more faith in than most players during his tenure.



Indeed, the Arsenal star has been called to every single one of Tuchel’s squads since the German took charge.

His start here meant the 28-year-old has featured in 16 of the 26 games the ex-Chelsea boss has presided over for our country.



Yet his performance was OK at best here and certainly would have not had Gordon sweating over his place.

While the plethora of other talents queueing up to be Tuchel’s back-up left-winger will have not been left disheartened.

Eze did not do anything wrong, as such. He worked hard and kept England’s shape well enough, even filling in in central midfield late on.

But his display down the left wing had none of the dynamism that Gordon produced to put the fear of God into Croatia in Rijeka on Saturday.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Granted, Eze does not have Gordon’s rapid pace. They are very different kinds of players.

He is an inventive playmaker though, capable of moments of ingenuity, as proven by his time at Crystal Palace, even if we have seen it less regularly at Arsenal.

A technician who has it in his locker to play the kind of first-time cross Morgan Rogers fired in for Harry Kane’s first here, or the clever swivel Gunners team-mate Myles Lewis-Skelly pulled off to have the crowd oohing and aahing early into the second half.

Eze offered a brief hint of his flair with a tasty little dribble round two players around the hour mark, and a late dribble into the box which failed to win a penalty.



His inability to stretch teams like Gordon meant England were far less dangerous than they have been of late.

Gordon also has a strong understanding with left-back Lewis Hall from their years together at Newcastle, which, understandably, Eze could not emulate.

Eze was involved in the opening goal of what proved to be the easy win many expected.



But, if anything, he should have actually done better in the move.

Kane had fired in a cross which Eze ought to have strained every sinew to get on the end of but instead eased up.

Unaware he was under no pressure from Eze at all, ex-West Ham full-back Vladimir Coufal comically fired into his own net.

Eze looked at his best in a central area, rather than out wide, late on when the Czechs were tiring.

Tuchel loves him for his ability, attitude and versatility.

Remember, the Gunners man is yet to start a Premier League game this season and still there was almost no doubt he would be in this squad.

But with an embarrassment of riches we have in reserve for the attacking trio behind Kane, including Morgan Gibbs-White, Rio Ngumoha and Cole Palmer, it does not seem unreasonable to expect a little more from Eze to justify his spot as a squad undroppable.

Sports.title: Hamilton: Ferrari have to catch up with rivals on power
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton is urging Ferrari to improve the performance of their power unit for the 2027 Formula 1 season as the 41-year-old eyes a shot at a record eighth world championship next year.

A first Ferrari grand prix victory for Hamilton in Barcelona in June provided hope that he could launch a 2026 title challenge, but an underwhelming run after the summer break saw his deficit to Mercedes' championship leader Kimi Antonelli grow beyond 100 points.

Hamilton ended a streak of six races without a podium by finishing third at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on Sunday, with only a poor choice of starting tyre costing him the chance to use his impressive pace to battle Red Bull's Max Verstappen for victory.

Following that encouraging display, he explained why he has confidence in his team going into next year.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton recovers from P15 to podium places

Hamilton told Sky Sports F1: "I think fundamentally we've got a great car, and that's down to an amazing group of people back at the factory, who are really intelligent and have made the right decisions.

"As I've said before, we have been innovators this year. We've had things on the car that everyone else has often followed.

"It's just that we know we're down on power, and that's something that we just live with. We have to catch up for next year. We live with that deficit for the rest of this year."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia at the Sepang International Circuit

With seven rounds of the 2026 season remaining, starting with a first ever Sprint event in Singapore this weekend, Hamilton is hopeful he'll have the pace to compete for more victories.

"But still, the car is improving, and I think we've got races coming up ahead that hopefully we'll still be able to get maybe a little bit closer," he added.

"We just keep trying. And I'm enjoying the racing still. I still feel fit, still feel focused."

Hamilton hopeful 'negative chatter' goes away

The build-up to the Bahrain Grand Prix was dominated by speculation over Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur's future, after former Red Bull chief Christian Horner had expressed an interest in the position.

Ferrari publicly backed Vasseur ahead of the event, while Hamilton criticised a "negative narrative" around the team.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ahead of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, Lewis Hamilton shares his confidence in Fred Vasseur despite 'negative' outside sources

Asked whether he thought a strong overall result, which saw team-mate Charles Leclerc finish a place behind him in fourth, would reduce negativity, Hamilton added: "I hope it's not too negative chatter after Malaysia.

"We still got good points with third and fourth."

Vasseur retained a philosophical outlook as he said it was easy reacting to a strong performance, but more important to ensure the team remain "solid" when things don't go to plan.

"You know perfectly the weekends are much easier to manage when you are doing a strong performance," Vasseur said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chaotic formation lap halts race start at Bahrain GP in Malaysia

"The most important thing is to be solid when it's not the case. Sometimes it won't be the case.

"It will happen to everybody. It was a tough weekend for McLaren. They came with a lot of expectations. It was difficult for them.

"But it's also in this situation that you have to react as a team and to stay together.

"It's always easy to deal with a good weekend."

Sports.title: 'No excuses' for Reed after injury as he looks to increase Race to Dubai lead
Sports.content:
Race to Dubai leader Patrick Reed says becoming the second American to be crowned European No 1 would mean "a lot" and insists he has "no excuses" as he looks to extend his advantage over Rory McIlroy after returning from a shoulder injury.

Reed will tee it up at the Open de Espana from Thursday in his first appearance since withdrawing during the second round of the flagship BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth last month.

The 36-year-old - aiming to follow in the footsteps of compatriot Collin Morikawa, who won the Race to Dubai in 2021 - is around 300 points clear of McIlroy with five events remaining.

McIlroy is not playing in Spain this week but is set to appear at the DP World India Championship in New Delhi from October 15.

Image: Rory McIlroy has won the last four Race to Dubai titles

Reed has topped the standings since February after victories at the Hero Dubai Desert Classic and Qatar Masters sandwiched a play-off defeat at the Bahrain Championship, with the 2018 Masters champion also recording three further top-10 finishes.

The Texan said: "I've always prided myself as being that American that likes to play around the world. To have the opportunity to come over here, not only just play on this tour, but also to have a chance to win the Race to Dubai, it would mean a lot.

"[Gary Player once told me], 'if you want to be a worldwide player, you've got to go out and play outside of the PGA Tour.

"Once I got the opportunity to come over and play, I really enjoyed it. Hopefully I can bring more Americans over and more of the top players come out and play around the world, help grow the game."

I've always wanted to earn my spot rather than having a spot given. Those guys on LIV, there are pathways, whether it's to here on the DP (World Tour) or to the PGA Tour. I feel the only way you should be able to get back is by going out there and letting the clubs do the talking."

Reed 'uncomfortable' but 'still able to perform'

Reed, runner-up to Shane Lowry at the Amgen Irish Open in September, said of the injury he sustained at Wentworth: "Never saw it coming. It was my first time withdrawing during a round of golf due to injury. I would rather shoot a million than withdraw.

"When I went in, the hand was all swollen. Any time it was touched, I was in a lot of pain, so they thought I might have broken something inside the hand. The hand was OK and it ended up being a shoulder issue. The good thing is it only set me back one week.

"It might be uncomfortable but at the same time I'm able to perform and do what I'm supposed to do in swinging the golf club.

"So no excuses - go out there, continue grinding and hopefully finish off the year strong."

Image: Three-time champion Jon Rahm will not play in his home tournament this week as he waits for the birth of his fourth child

Three-time Open de Espana champion Jon Rahm will not play in his home tournament with Spanish media saying the 31-year-old is in the USA awaiting the birth of his daughter.

England's Marco Penge is the defending champion in Madrid, while the field also includes Lowry, Justin Rose, Ludvig Åberg and Sergio Garcia, as well as Eugenio Chacarra, who sits third in the Race to Dubai standings behind Reed and McIlroy.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Captains Jim Furyk and Luke Donald look ahead to the Ryder Cup at Adare Manor in 2027

Reed, who quit LIV Golf earlier this year in order to pursue a return to the PGA Tour from 2027, has not played in the Ryder Cup since the 2018 edition in France, at which he criticised captain Jim Furyk's decisions as America tumbled to a heavy defeat to Europe.

Furyk is back as US skipper for the 2027 tournament in Ireland and asked at a year-to-go press conference on Tuesday whether Reed was in his plans, he said: "We are going to put the best 12 guys, the best team of 12. If Patrick Reed is one of those, that's great."

The 130-rated Dartan takes the drop-in class after being tailed off in a handicap hurdle at Haydock in April. He has since had wind surgery which could bring about some much-needed improvement, given his chase record currently reads zero from four. Champion jockey Sean Bowen retains the ride.

Snipe - trained by champion trainer Dan Skelton - is far more exposed over fences than Dartan, having won four times in 24 over the larger obstacles. He was beaten in a three-runner race at Warwick last month by a short head and drops in trip today to two miles and seven furlongs.

King Roly is two from four at Worcester, with the most recent of those victories coming on his penultimate start over today's distance. He bolted up at 5/1 under James Bowen that day but is now 6lbs above that mark.

1.50 Sedgefield - Interesting Arms Park makes hurdle debut

Arms Park is an interesting runner in our opening Mowden Park RFC Maiden Hurdle, making his debut over obstacles.

This son of Walk In The Park is lightly raced after picking up one victory from three bumpers, where he travelled strongly to make all under James Bowen at Taunton. He tanked through the race in eye-catching style that day and he arrives as an exciting prospect for the upcoming season. Interestingly enough, Act Of Innocence won this race in 2025 before going on to score in the Sidney Banks prior to producing a career best in the Turners Novices' Hurdle at Cheltenham.

Dunstall Star is the most experienced in here but disappointed last time at Worcester and will need to be better to compete with Arms Park. Military Cross chased home a potentially nice horse of Gordon Elliott's in a Cartmel maiden hurdle the last day and could serve it up to Arms Park.

2.50 Sedgefield - Jet Of Dreams attempts to defy 7lb penalty

Jet Of Dreams will attempt to defy the penalty given to him in the Jodie Standings Point-To-Point Recruits Handicap Chase.

Warren Greatrex's eight-year-old followed up his seasonal reappearance with a nice victory over course and distance last Tuesday, being nursed into the race before winning well. If he produces a similar display today, he could be hard to beat.

Kientzheim - owned by JP McManus - hasn't taken to fences thus far but her peak hurdling rating of 121 suggests Ben Haslam's mare has plenty of ability if she can rectify her jumping. Kevin Brogan comes in for the ride, replacing Harry Cobden.

Neigh Botha was pulled up at Worcester in July but had notched up three wins from his four starts prior. This Greenall and Guerriero runner will have benefitted from a break and if fit, could be right in the mix. Lady Kara completes the quartet and looks to be on the up, having only been beaten two lengths by Jet Of Dreams over this course and distance last month.

Best of the rest

Perfect Pitch, a Wootton Bassett colt with an entry in the Criterium International, runs in Chantilly's Prix du Grand Vivier at 11.17am. He was a tad disappointing on debut at Saint-Cloud but should progress today in the Juddmonte colours.

Worcester's 2.35pm CopyBet Supporting UK Horse Racing Fillies' Juvenile Maiden Hurdle sees Miss Moffett - a half-sister to Nube Negra - make her debut for the Skelton team. After failing to fire on the Flat, Big Orange's half-sister Miss Malone To You tackles hurdles for the first time.

At Sedgefield, Sam England's Littletown Lad goes for the hat-trick in the 3.50pm Winning Connections Conference Hire Handicap Hurdle.

Sports.title: Kane sums up England legacy on special night - but can he make final step?
Sports.content:
Some things are inevitable in life. Harry Kane delivering for England is always one of those inevitabilities. On his momentous, milestone match, he stuck to the script perfectly.

On his 125th cap, Kane did what Kane does best under the Wembley arch - stealing the show, leading the way, winning the game for England.

Everyone knew he would score in this match. It's the same feeling you get in every match. But he still gets the buzz.

"I think this is even beyond my wildest dreams," he said after the game. "To be now at 125, it's just an extreme privilege."

This match - and the three goals he contributed to England's cause on his special night - was a perfect summary of Harry Kane's England career.

The first goal saw him venture out to the right wing, highlighting Kane's ability to pop up anywhere on the pitch. Quarterback, out wide, it doesn't matter. It's classic Kane.

But his two goals were classic centre-forward strikes. Right in the heart of the penalty area, almost a throwback to the classic No 9.

Image: Harry Kane stole the show on his 125th England cap

"He's playing at a level that is unmatched," said Jude Bellingham on Kane's record-breaking night. "He's scoring goals for fun, he's dropping deep and playing passes in behind and contributing, making tackles and everything. He's only getting better."

What makes Kane's achievement even more incredible is he has reached 125 caps despite making his England debut at 21. For a generational talent in the modern game, that's somewhat rare. Bellingham, for example, was 17 when he played his first game.

Kane did not have the teenage sensation moment Wayne Rooney or Micheal Owen had. Bukayo Saka and Rio Ferdinand were also 19 on their England debuts. Declan Rice and Phil Foden were 20. Kane was the slow starter who forged his way up through the EFL and became a national hero.

And what has followed is 125 caps in 11 years. The remarkable consistency is summarised by his availability. He's always there for England.

In England's last 101 competitive matches - which spans a decade - Kane has been available for selection for all but one of them: the Nations League loss to Greece in 2024.

Every single other game, he has been able to be called upon for the Three Lions. A century of near-perfectly consistent England performances.

Now it's important to recognise that Kane hasn't always been 100 per cent fit in those 100 matches. The Euro 2024 campaign and final spring to mind where he was clearly carrying something but playing through the pain.

Image: Kane hasn't always been at 100 per cent fitness during his 125 caps

"I think every player at some stage plays through the pain or niggles or some sort of injury," he said.

"I think the last six years or so I've been extremely consistent in that sense and been available. I think availability is one of the biggest strengths you can have at this level."

His predecessor at the England elite level in Rooney was riddled with injury sagas through his career - Euro 2004 and the 2006 World Cup especially.

The main image of his 2010 World Cup highlight reel was him shouting down the TV cameras to England fans, then he faded out of form in 2012, 2014 and 2016 - to the point where he was no longer the main man. Kane has shown the consistency Rooney never could.

Now Rooney, Owen and Co were part of a different generation where playing for England was not as attractive as it is now. Turning up regularly for international duty was not as common, with the 'club first culture' well-documented on many levels.

But then again, Kane's big night came on the same evening that Cristiano Ronaldo revealed his reasons for leaving the Portugal camp. Even the very best can easily turn away from the national team for any reason. Kane has never even given a glimmer of that attitude in his 11 years.

"To reach the highest level on a consistent basis you've always got to be hungry, you've always got to be striving for more," he said.

"I think sometimes players or people can reach the top and think it's time to take their foot off the gas and that's when you see players maybe fall.

"For me it's the opposite. When I'm at the top it's to do even more, find even more improvement. That's what I'm doing right now."

Kane is the exemplary player England needed for this generation - but all that remains is for him to confirm his place as the greatest player in any generation.

Is he already England's best? Quite possibly. Record appearance maker and goalscorer is hard to top and argue against. But the one thing Ronaldo, Bobby Charlton and Bobby Moore have over him is silverware at international level. "For sure I'd swap all [the caps and goals] to win something with England."

Image: Kane still needs the silverware at the top of the international game

But Kane also said: "Every player has a ceiling." What is his? Has he already reached it? "I hope not. I hope there's still more to go. I guess only time dictates that, where everyone's ceiling is.

"Right now I still feel like I've got room to improve. I just said that I've come off the back of my best season ever at 32 years old and right now I feel even in a better place."

There is still plenty for him to get. Kane is first eyeing up 100 goals at international level, joining a very elite club of strikers to manage that feat. He will surely get there.

"I try not to think about it too much," he said, with a sense of humility. "It's like being a cricketer in the 90s, the more you think about the 100, you don't know where to get there.

But in this all-time great innings - as well as the upcoming Ballon D'Or trophy, which he surely has more than half a chance for - delivering a first major international trophy since 1966 is the ultimate prize.

Kane has at least one more bite at the trophy cherry. He looks set to appear at Euro 2028 and possibly he can squeeze out one last crack at the World Cup, following this summer's disappointment.

"I'm in great shape," he said. "Some of the players I've played with went into their late 30s and are still at the highest level and are even in their 40s now. It's season by season with me.

"As long as I feel like I can help the team and be valuable for the team I'll be around. At the moment I feel like I can't help the team, I won't and that's the way I am. We'll have to see."

For now, one message stands with Kane. "Don't give yourself any regrets." He has done so much - but it's time for the last, big challenge. Win it all. Win what remains.

Sports.title: Should 'cracking kid' Bamber be awarded England call-up?
Sports.content:
Should England add Ethan Bamber to their battery of seam bowlers in Test cricket?

The Warwickshire star, 27, was the leading County Championship wicket-taker in the country in 2026, with his 69 scalps at an average of 19.39 helping the Bears to the Division One title.

Bamber is an Ollie Robinson figure as opposed to a Jofra Archer one, relying on skill and nagging accuracy rather than pace and hostility.

Image: Bamber recorded match figures of 9-94 as Warwickshire beat Leicestershire to secure the title

But with it now in vogue for wicketkeepers to stand up close to the stumps to seamers wobbling the ball, perhaps Bamber has a chance of a maiden international call-up?

Bamber for England? 'Never say never...'

Sky Sports' Michael Atherton said on the England prospects of the former Middlesex man, who has 308 scalps in 89 first-class matches at an average below 27: "A few years ago, you'd have said no - a bowler of 78, 80 miles an hour, wobbling it about.

"But now everybody's keen on the wobble seam and the wicketkeeper standing up. So never say never. I wouldn't imagine so but I see him as a very, very good county bowler.

"England have got Ollie Robinson there at the moment and they'll always have one of those fellas in the mix, won't they?

Image: Bamber picked up four five-wicket hauls during the 2026 Championship season

"Whether it's Robinson or Sam Cook, who seems to be kind of Robinson's understudy at the moment, so you could see Bamber maybe in that role.

"He's a cracking kid and somebody who wants to get absolutely the most out of every little bit of talent that he's got.

"He moved to Warwickshire with ambitions to go to a club that's challenging for things and is making the most of what he's got."

Bamber brushed off the likelihood of international honours while speaking to Cricinfo at the recent Professional Cricketers' Association awards in London, saying: "If that ship was ever in the harbour, it's definitely sailed now.

"What I'm thinking of is how I can contribute next year for Warwickshire, and try to help us continue to be successful moving forward. That's really what makes me a bit nervous and excited."

There's definitely a role for his sort of bowler. He doesn't miss. He's as skilful as anyone around. I think if there's a gap for him, he would definitely do a great job. He's very humble and says that ship has sailed, but I don't agree.

'Archer at peak of his powers - now the leader of the attack'

England's attack starred during the 3-0 rout of Pakistan this summer, with Robinson bagging 21 wickets at an average below nine and Archer 12 at 26.66.

Gus Atkinson and Josh Tongue also played their part, while Cook, Sonny Baker and Matthew Fisher are back-up options.

The quicks will return to red-ball cricket from December 17, live on Sky Sports, for a three-Test series in South Africa - Stephen Fleming's first assignment as head coach.

Image: Ollie Robinson enjoyed a brilliant return to Test cricket this summer

Former England seamer Chris Woakes, speaking at the launch of the ECB's 'Cricket for Teachers' initiative, told Sky Sports News: "The bowling attack looks great, plenty of depth.

"Robinson has come back in and done fantastically well - South Africa will be a different challenge but he has the skills to succeed.

"The beauty of Jofra is that he has played a lot of cricket over the last few years and stayed injury-free - he looks as fit as ever and is kind of the leader of the attack now.

Image: Chris Woakes says Jofra Archer (pictured) is now the leader of England's attack

"He has matured a lot as a bowler and a person. He is at the peak of his powers and wants to be playing his best Test cricket.

"His best is ahead of him."

Sports.title: Harry Kane doubles up on landmark night as England cruise past Czechia
Sports.content:
It was a night that belonged to Harry Kane. Yet another one. It began with him being shown a replay of his first England goal during a pre-match interview with ITV – the header against Lithuania in 2015, just 79 seconds after he came on as a substitute for his debut. It ended with him reflecting on two more in what was a supremely comfortable Nations League victory over Czechia. Some things never change.

It remains a numbers game for Kane. They are getting bigger and ever more impressive. On the occasion of his 125th cap, the one that took him level with Peter Shilton at the top of the all-time England list, he moved to an astonishing 91 goals. Nobody will be surprised if he reaches the century. The only question appears to be when.

England know how to beat the game’s smaller fry. Under Thomas Tuchel, they have played 16 matches against teams ranked outside the world’s top 20. They have won 15 and drawn one – against Ghana at the World Cup. They have conceded only once – against the Democratic Republic of the Congo, also at the World Cup. Czechia, who are ranked No 50, were never in the contest.

Kane is similarly inevitable. The captain even claimed the assist for the breakthrough goal with a cross into the corridor of uncertainty that spooked Vladimir Coufal so severely he shot into his own net. Kane’s passing was very good. When he was withdrawn in the 82nd minute, he left to a great ovation.

The victory meant that England virtually guaranteed their progress into the Nations League quarter-finals and, perhaps more importantly, saw them close out this elongated window with plenty of optimism. One of the main goals was to put as much distance as possible between themselves and the World Cup semi-final defeat against Argentina. It was mission accomplished.

Kane will break the caps record when England host Croatia in November and that will be the night when he is truly feted. As an aside, he would want to do it at Wembley rather than in Madrid against Spain where England’s next-but-one game will be staged. Was that why he was so keen to play in all four of the matches during this window? It might have been a part of it.

Then again, Kane always wants to play. He was one of only three England players to start each of the matches in this series. The others were Manchester City’s Marc Guéhi and Elliot Anderson. Was the City manager, Enzo Maresca, happy about that? Probably not. Does he have bigger problems at the moment? Yes.

Kane’s act of drawing level with Shilton was the box-office detail. His name was on everybody’s lips; his face on the big screen before kick-off. He was pictured alongside Shilton when his name was read out with the teams. The Wembley crowd roared.

Kane was at the heart of the opening goal, providing the teasing cross from the right and it was some finish from the player just inside the six-yard box. One that Kane would have been happy to call his own. The problem from a Czechia point of view was that it came from their right-back. Coufal could feel Eberechi Eze at his back as he faced towards his own goal, albeit the England winger was not that close. Coufal stretched and everybody had the time to have the same thought: you do not have to do this. Coufal did it. He could not check his momentum and steered firmly past his goalkeeper.

View image in fullscreen Czechia’s Vladimir Coufal scores an own goal to put England ahead. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA

Trent Alexander-Arnold, who Tuchel recalled at right-back, was involved in the buildup and he caught the eye, especially when surging up and inside. He repeatedly got into advanced areas and there was one moment in the first half when he stormed into the No 9 position on to an Anderson pass. He just could not bring it under his spell. Alexander-Arnold had extended Lukas Hornicek with a whipped free-kick at the outset.

Jude Bellingham was excellent. Of course he was. There were fizzed passes from him that took the breath, getting England into dangerous positions, including one for Morgan Rogers in the 25th minute that the Chelsea attacker wasted. There were those strutting runs and it was Bellingham, as much as anybody, who advertised the fact that England were going to break through.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Anderson should have made it 2-0 after a Bellingham lay-off; Kane sparked the move and Alexander-Arnold’s cross drove it. The second goal arrived before half-time and it had to be Kane. It would have been all about the buildup were it not for the identity of the scorer. Anderson’s lofted ball up the inside right was a beauty and Rogers’ first-time cross on the half-volley was even better, cut unerringly towards you-know-who in the middle. Kane was unmarked. Hornicek was helpless.

Kane wanted more. As usual. He got it. As usual. There was the moment shortly after the restart when he unloaded from the edge of the area and watched the shot kiss the top of the crossbar. Hornicek was beaten. Then he was for real.

View image in fullscreen Harry Kane’s header puts England 3-0 up at Wembley. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA

It was Lewis Hall – impressive at left-back – who swung over the corner, which came after Hornicek kept out an audacious Bellingham flick. Only Jiri Slama knows why he gave Kane so much room in front of goal. It was always going to end badly for the Czechia defender. Kane rose and the header had too much power for Hornicek.

There was the minor irritation for Tuchel when Myles Lewis-Skelly got himself booked in the 53rd minute for pulling back Pavel Sulc. The midfielder will be suspended for England’s next game and it was certainly not a great idea for him to get in the face of Michal Sadilek shortly afterwards. Sadilek had fouled Rogers and was booked. It was a needless risk from Lewis-Skelly.

England toyed with Czechia in the second half with Eze running through some of his party tricks. It was Kane who provided the substance.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi bids tearful farewell to Argentina after scoring in 3-0 win over Benin
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi brought the curtain down on his 21-year international career on Tuesday, bidding farewell to adoring Argentina fans in an emotional final appearance for the former world champions in Buenos Aires.

In a perfectly scripted finale, the 39-year-old widely regarded as the greatest football player in history signed off with his 126th international goal in front of 85,000 supporters as Argentina cruised to a 3-0 victory over Benin.

Messi, playing in his record-extending 208th international, also provided the assist for the opening goal scored by veteran Nicolás Otamendi, with Nico Paz also scoring.

But the match was a footnote to the occasion itself, which saw Messi savoring the adulation of the Monumental Stadium crowd one last time for an event which had been billed as The Last Tango.

Beforehand, Messi wiped away tears as the bus carrying him and his Argentina teammates made its way through crowds of well-wishers en route to the stadium.

Messi took the field alongside his three children and received affectionate waves from his wife, Antonela Roccuzzo, and his mother, Celia Cuccittini, who were watching from a VIP box.

Shortly before kick-off, a giant Argentina jersey bearing the word “Gracias” (Thank You) above the football superstar’s No 10 was laid out on the pitch as the crowd roared their approval.

View image in fullscreen Messi takes on the Benin defence. Photograph: Luis Robayo/AFP/Getty Images

Messi welled up again as Falklands War veteran Fabio Santana sang the national anthem beside a banner which read – “The Malvinas are Argentine” – the same banner held aloft by players after their 2-1 World Cup semi-final win over England.

The match was halted in the 10th minute – in tribute to Messi’s famous shirt number – for a minute-long ovation to the former Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain star.

He crowned the occasion with a goal from the penalty spot in the 71st minute.

‘I gave it my all’

At the final whistle a drone show lit up the night sky above the stadium, showing Messi’s image and thanking the eight-time Ballon d’Or-winner for his career.

View image in fullscreen A drone display featuring Messi is seen at the end of his final match for Argentina. Photograph: Julian Bongiovanni/AP

Messi’s farewell came two and a half months after Argentina’s World Cup final defeat to Spain in New Jersey, where Messi exited in tears after making little impression in an ill-tempered 1-0 loss. “I gave it my all; I have nothing left to give, and besides, there are great young players coming up who deserve their chance,” Messi wrote at the time.

Before Tuesday’s game, the University of Buenos Aires awarded Messi an honorary doctorate in a ceremony at the Argentine Football Association (AFA) headquarters. Messi, who has in the past spoken of his regret at not studying more, expressed pride at the distinction. “To be able to say that I am an honorary doctor!,” he joked.

Outside the Argentina Football Association headquarters, fans unfurled a huge Argentine flag with his image inscribed “The joy of my life”.

Former Barcelona teammate Neymar paid tribute to the departing champion on X. “It’s not just Argentina that thanks you, the world thanks you for everything you did for football. Thank you for making me love football even more,” he said.

Messi remains under contract with Inter Miami until 2028, although following the death of his father, Jorge, two months ago, he revealed he may hang up his boots for good sooner than anticipated.

Messi’s departure comes four years after his greatest triumph in international football, leading Argentina to victory at the 2022 World Cup to end the country’s 36-year wait for a third title, cementing his status as Diego Maradona’s heir.

“I believe Messi gave everything, absolutely everything, so it doesn’t bother me at all that he’s leaving. He has more than earned it, let him enjoy himself, let him rest,” Cecilia Adriano, 52, told AFP.

During his time with the Albiceleste, Argentina won one World Cup, were runners-up twice (Brazil 2014 and North America 2026) and were also crowned Copa America champions in 2021 and 2024.

Sports.title: Justin Ellis helps US cap a perfect international window with 1-0 win over Canada
Sports.content:
Before 1878, a referee trying to get players’ attention was left to waive a white handkerchief in the air. It was an imperfect practice, asking an infractor to be self-aware enough to look for a doffed doily after hard contact. The game forever changed when Joseph Hudson, a Birmingham-bred tool maker who founded Acme Whistles, showed up to an FA Cup match in 1878 with his signature product in tow.

On Tuesday, nearly 150 years after Hudson’s innovation, referee Steven Madrigal paid the architect a hearty tribute.

The United States and Canada closed the lengthy window with a stop-start, physical, and at times ugly affair, with the hosts claiming a 1-0 victory on an otherwise gorgeous autumn evening in Minnesota. Justin Ellis bagged his second goal for the US with a first-time finish, while Brian Schwake kept a clean sheet in his first international start.

As for the music to Hudson’s belated ears: 43 fouls committed between the sides, with the US also leading that count by one.

The regional rivals wasted no time in letting the game get chippy, as games between them tend to get. In the 2026 World Cup, only group opponents Bosnia and Herzegovina and Switzerland averaged more fouls per game (14.4) than Canada; their 11 yellow cards trailed only Argentina (13) and Egypt (12) despite playing fewer games than each.

Marsch’s side committed nine fouls in the opening 16 minutes to the hosts’ three, keeping the US from building a head of steam whenever they had the ball. Boos followed each foul on Tuesday, with the loudest jeering saved for touches by Canada goalkeeper Dayne St Clair, returning to the venue for the first time since leaving Minnesota United for Inter Miami as a free agent after seven seasons in Saint Paul.

A heavily rotated US side struggled to find avenues while keeping the ball on the ground, slinging passes from side to side in a fruitless attempt to unsettle the Canadian defensive block. Justin Ellis was the unfortunate first victim of a hard challenge, staying on the Allianz Field pitch for a few minutes after a collision in the 20th minute, but he was able to continue after some medical treatment.

Perhaps the physios ought to be credited with a second assist for their efforts. Five minutes after re-entering the game, Ellis navigated the channel as Alex Freeman worked a one-two to get the ball into the final third. The pair of Orlando academy products connected with aplomb, as Freeman’s cross bypassed St Clair for Ellis to slam home. The 19-year-old has two goals in his first three appearances for the US – doubling his club goal tally from 19 MLS appearances to date.

The game failed to regain any normal flow from there, as the US showing greater willingness to meet Canada’s muscle. Costa Rican referee Steven Madrigal was kept busy throughout the first half, sussing out which way to award blame on 50/50 challenges and struggling to play the advantage with consistency. The fouls ledger was better balanced by half-time, with Canada’s 13 cautions outpacing 10 from the US.

The end of the half was the pinnacle of stop/start soccer. Canada conceded three corners in succession, with the third leading to a US free kick at the edge of the box after a Gio Reyna dribble; the ensuing attempt was promptly sent behind the goal by Canada for a fourth US corner. Despite five dead balls in close range of goal, the US failed to turn any one of them into a dangerous look as Reyna and Tillman alternated service. At last, Madrigal was able to close the half and give his whistle a break.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Marsch made one substitution at the break and Pochettino made two, yet little about the game’s composition altered after half-time. Auston Trusty took a particularly poignant clattering from Jonathan David in the 59th minute as the Atlético Madrid striker tried to win a header, coming up a split-second after the Celtic defender headed it clear.

Cole Campbell became the 13th player to make his US debut in the window in the 61st minute, and was immediately trying to force the Canada defensive block to retreat with upfield scampers. Canada began to mine more set pieces of their own, but failed to maximize the threat. Julian Hall ran on to a ball beyond the Canadian defense for a one-on-one with St Clair, only for his shot to catch the outside netting.

By the end, each team had managed just two attempts in the second half, with only one of Canada’s efforts landing on target. As if negotiated in the locker rooms, the sides maintained an identical 72% pass completion rate entering second-half stoppage.

In true Minnesota fashion, most of the crowd politely stuck around through the final whistle to bask in the beautiful fall weather that’s typical for the region. A bright and clear sky at kickoff made way for crisp air after sundown, which allowed the fans’ cheering, the drum corps’ beat, and the post-win rendition of “Country Roads” to linger a bit longer than usual.

As did that whistle, blown early and often.

Sports.title: Sturm warning rocks Pocognoli as abject Scotland turned over by Slovenia
Sports.content:
The nature of this Scotland defeat felt far more significant than the fact it arrived at all. Sébastien Pocognoli is already in tricky territory, just four games into his tenure as Scotland head coach. Slovenia comprehensively outplayed the fragile hosts at Hampden Park, which leaves Pocognoli staring at a third-placed finish in a soft Nations League section. Brave new dawn or beginning of an error?

Scotland were defensively disorganised. Their attacking play was timid. Long before full time, the 39-year-old Belgian had the look of a coach throwing darts blindly at a board. And missing. Wastefulness from Slovenia prevented Scottish embarrassment.

A scathing assessment arrived from the Scotland captain, Andy Robertson, who admitted his team were “outfought”. Robertson added: “They looked a lot fresher, a lot more hungry.”

Pocognoli was more circumspect. “We didn’t play the game we wanted to,” he said. “We were not at the level we expect to be. I will not say everything is perfect or everything is bad but we need to improve many things. We have enough quality.”

A pre-match presentation to Robertson, who reached the 100-cap mark during Scotland’s win in North Macedonia on Saturday, carried wider meaning. Gordon Strachan and Alex McLeish, Robertson’s first two Scotland managers, were joined on the Hampden pitch by Steve Clarke. This marked a swift and welcome return to the national stadium for Clarke, who departed the Scotland job in unsatisfactory circumstances following failings at the World Cup. Clarke, bashful by nature, took as significant a bow as was ever likely before supporters.

Scotland find themselves in a post-Clarke state of flux. He was the manager who made this country relevant on the wider stage once again. There was, however, widespread criticism that Clarke’s team lacked ambition. Pocognoli has been charged with not only maintaining at least decent results but also delivering an alternative brand of football. It is a fanciful quest, perhaps.

The first quarter mirrored the opening half when these teams met in Ljubljana. Scotland looked uncertain. Slovenia were perfectly comfortable, not only in a defensive sense but when springing into attack. Adam Gnezda Cerin should have afforded the visitors a 13th-minute lead but failed to connect with appropriate force, allowing Jack Hendry to boot clear when just three yards from his own goal. This venue, which should be an asset to Scotland, was eerily quiet.

Ryan Christie raised the mood. That the goal was horribly ugly mattered not a jot to the Scottish contingent. A short free-kick was played wide to Ben Gannon-Doak, whose deflected cross was headed on to a post by Hendry. Modern football’s madness means Oli McBurnie will be credited with an assist for the header with which he was undoubtedly trying to score. The ball instead landed at the feet of Christie, who tapped home from close range.

View image in fullscreen Ryan Christie gives Scotland the lead from close range. Photograph: Robert Perry/EPA

Robertson demonstrated his ongoing value before the break. Zan Vipotnik seemed certain to equalise before the Tottenham full-back’s rescue act, courtesy of a sliding block. Ominously for Scotland, Danijel Sturm had totally bamboozled their three-man defence when supplying Vipotnik.

It was impossible to argue Slovenia were not worthy of their equaliser, which arrived 11 minutes after half-time. It came from a Scotland throw-in, where possession was cheaply conceded. Sturm played through the centre and towards Aljosa Matko, who brushed Luis Binks aside as if the Brøndby defender was not even there. The Scotland goalkeeper Angus Gunn, as is something of a theme, was weak in trying to deal with Matko’s shot. Sturm should have sent Slovenia in front two minutes later but saved the blushes of a hilariously open Scotland defence by shooting over. This had to be alarming for Pocognoli.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Slovenia were swaggering around their hosts. Pocognoli switched to a back four for the first time in this elongated international window shortly before Matko was denied his second goal of the night by an offside flag. The decision was not at all debatable.

View image in fullscreen Scotland’s Sébastian Pocognoli looks away in horror on the touchline. Photograph: Ian MacNicol/Getty Images

Neither was the goal which took Slovenia ahead. This time Matko turned supplier, having rampaged down the right flank and crossed for the onrushing Sturm. Gunn was left with no chance as Sturm slammed the ball past him. Pocognoli was now subjected to Tartan Army boos.

Findlay Curtis and Josh McPake had penalty claims rejected for Scotland. Desperation had indeed become the order of the day. McPake was at least lively, having stepped from the bench. Too many of his teammates either underperformed or are not cut out for this level. It is up to Pocognoli to source answers, and sharply. This is no patient football domain.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo accuses Portugal coach Jorge Jesus of broken promises
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo has accused the Portugal head coach, Jorge Jesus, of twice breaking his word, saying a failed agreement to publicly explain ⁠his omission against Norway drove him out of the camp but insisting he remained available after any punishment.

In a lengthy statement, the 41-year-old gave his ⁠account of the dispute ⁠that prompted his ​departure from Copenhagen before Portugal’s Nations League match against Denmark last week.

Ronaldo said Jesus had agreed a plan under which the forward would ⁠miss the Norway and Denmark matches to manage his fitness. However, on the day of the Norway game, the coach told him he would play for 30 ⁠minutes.

“Everyone knows the rest. I warmed up from half-time onwards, watched the minutes tick by and wasn’t called ​on,” Ronaldo said. “The manager had broken his ‌word to me.”

Portugal’s captain and ‌all-time leading scorer said a subsequent meeting with Jesus, attended by his club side Al-Nassr’s sporting ‌director Simão Coutinho, produced an agreement for the coach to clarify events at his next press conference.

According to Ronaldo, an eight-point document was prepared saying he had never demanded playing time, had respected Jesus’s decisions and that the coach asking him to warm up without bringing him on had been a mistake. Ronaldo said the agreed notes did not require Jesus to apologise to him ‌but said the coach’s public remarks bore no resemblance to their private discussion.

“It was the second time he had broken his word to me,” Ronaldo said. “I decided ​to leave the training camp without waiting for any further broken promises.”

The statement provided Ronaldo’s account but on Sunday, after Portugal’s win over Norway, Jesus denied he had made any agreement with the player but left the door open for his return.

The Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) did not immediately respond to a request for ⁠comment about Ronaldo’s statement.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Ronaldo apologised for failing to greet supporters after the Norway ​match and for leaving his ​teammates, accepting that his captaincy made ​his conduct more serious. “The consequences of my actions must be assessed and punished ​by the Portuguese Football ‌Federation,” he said.

Despite ​the rupture, Ronaldo said ​he was not limiting his international ambitions to a farewell appearance. “If I’m physically fit, playing for my club – scoring goals, I hope – after serving whatever suspension is imposed on me, I’ll be available, as I’ve always been until now, to compete and win for our national team,” he added.

Sports.title: Fifa reportedly allowed DR Congo into World Cup despite ineligible player in qualifying
Sports.content:
Fifa allowed the Democratic Republic of the Congo to compete at this summer’s World Cup despite reports suggesting an internal investigation found that the country had fielded an ineligible player in qualifying.

The player in question, the goalkeeper Lionel Mpasi, starred for his nation at the tournament, including against England in the last 32. Mpasi, who was born in France and played for Les Bleus at youth level, had never completed the process of switching nationalities, Fifa reportedly found. No punishment was levied against the Congolese federation, Fecofa.

The news will again raise questions over the Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, with a series of governance scandals having brought heightened scrutiny on his position. Fifa’s investigative teams are independent and the president has no input into their proceedings. Fifa is understood to have denied that Infantino played a part in the decision-making process over Mpasi, but his name is likely to remain in focus owing to a former university associate, Véron Mosengo-Omba, being elected unopposed as president of Fecofa this May.

The Nigerian Football Federation submitted a complaint over the DRC apparently fielding ineligible players during a World Cup playoff tie between the nations, which the DRC won on penalties, in November.

According to reporting by the New York Times and Le Monde, Fifa investigators were aware of Mpasi’s situation before the DRC defeated Jamaica in a final intercontinental playoff round in March. Faced with a series of possible responses, including banning the DRC from the playoffs, Fifa chose to reject the Nigeria complaint on the grounds it had not been submitted within the necessary timeframe.

Nigeria appealed against the decision and government representatives have suggested they could seek financial compensation for their loss, with a member of the national sports commission , which regulates Nigerian sport, telling ESPN: “Nothing has been decided yet, but we will seriously consider seeking compensation from Fifa for all of the economic losses this has cost Nigeria.”

Concacaf, the North and Central American and Caribbean confederation, which includes Jamaica among its members, said it “takes player eligibility matters very seriously and expects the applicable regulations and procedures to be applied consistently and fairly in all competitions”. In a statement it asked that any “concerns regarding player eligibility” be “thoroughly reviewed and addressed through Fifa’s appropriate governance and disciplinary bodies”.

Fifa, Concacaf, Caf, the Nigeria Football Federation and Fecofa, were all approached for comment.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

On Tuesday the Norwegian football federation confirmed it had submitted a three-pronged complaint to Fifa over its governance, including the decision to overturn a red card awarded to the USA’s Folarin Balogun after a telephone intervention by Donald Trump. The other instances cited by the NFF are the Fifa peace prize and the abandoned plan to sell a share in the World Cup to investors, known as the Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme.

“Each of these cases must be assessed based on the facts of each individual case,” said the president of the NFF, Lise Klaveness. “At the same time, the cases point to a more fundamental question: has Fifa’s position, authority or influence been used in a way that was not appropriate, and if so, did the mechanisms that were supposed to prevent this function work as they should?”

Sports.title: Too nice: do Arsenal lack the grit and tenacity to end WSL title drought?
Sports.content:
Arsenal, 10 points adrift of the Women’s Super League leaders, are poised to undertake a “big review” of their season during this international break to try to determine where things have gone so horribly wrong – again – in the early stages. After their 4-2 loss at Manchester City on Sunday, it felt as if the agenda needs to include an unusual but potentially critical question: is this team nasty enough to win a WSL title?

The technical ability throughout the world-class squad Arsenal have assembled could hardly be higher but the levels of grit, resilience and tenacity need examining in a group that appears unable to match Chelsea and Manchester City when it comes to the mental aspects of a title race. Arsenal last won the WSL in 2019.

When speaking to sources close to the Arsenal players, it is common to hear of the squad being like a “family”, very supportive of each other and full of “great people”. Those admirable traits, and a general sense the club is full of nice characters, often come across when watching games or during player interviews. Arsenal have built a team of good eggs; polite, courteous and professional individuals who people would be glad to call friends. In the vast majority of scenarios in life this is, quite obviously, a good thing. But are they too nice to beat City?

It is quite hard to imagine many of the Arsenal squad raising their voices in anger. It is equally hard to recall the last time anybody at the club engaged in so-called “housery”; perhaps not since Katie McCabe’s hair pull against Chelsea in last season’s Champions League quarter-final. The irony is that McCabe is one of the senior, influential players who left this summer – in her case to join Chelsea – and McCabe, regardless of what fans might think of her, is someone Arsenal could rely on to roll up her sleeves and get stuck in, to raise her game in a hostile atmosphere and be combative.

Last term, no Arsenal players – not even McCabe – registered in Stats Perform’s list of the top 20 WSL players for percentage of duels won. Only one Arsenal player has been shown a red card in a WSL game since 2021-22. Admirable discipline, yes, but are they lacking that fire in the belly?

This season, the team appear to be without a dogged, refuse-to-lose type of character in the mould of Lucy Bronze, whose never-say-die attitude has frequently come to England’s aid in crucial moments at major tournaments; or the gritty battling spirit of Erin Cuthbert, who has helped Chelsea lift seven league titles; or – to take an Arsenal example – a leader such as Gabriel Magalhães, a rock for others to lean on during tough games.

It is possible to be successful without a Roy Keane in your squad and Arsenal do have Leah Williamson, who has led England to two European titles, so it would be wrong to imply there is no leadership in this group. Leaders can step up in different ways but recently Renée Slegers, when praising her senior players’ reactions to their disappointing draw in Paris, mentioned there had been “lots of hugs” and praised how supportive everybody had been for each other. That sounds like the sort of unified workplace culture millions would envy, but to win titles sometimes you need to fall out, yell, be angry and demand higher standards.

View image in fullscreen Only one Arsenal player has been shown a red card in a WSL game since 2021-22. Photograph: Molly Darlington/WSL/WSL Football/Getty Images

On Friday I asked Slegers whether Arsenal had enough of a nasty edge to win the league, and she replied defiantly: “I think so, and nastiness or that grittiness, that can express itself in different ways, and I think we have certain ways in which we express that and [in] which we can do that. But of course, with our performances where we haven’t been at our best, you maybe don’t see those moments as much which we can bring, but we’re convinced that we can bring that to games as well, in our way, the Arsenal way, because it’s definitely there.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

That was not evident on Sunday in the little – but important – moments, such as shortly after Arsenal had twice taken a lead they would surrender. City seemed unfazed and carried the resolve of a team who had no doubt they would win.

Part of the way that belief has been instilled into the defending champions was evidenced in a clip, released by Sky Sports, of Andrée Jeglertz’s pre-match team talk, which he concluded with the words: “The most important thing: we are Manchester City, we are playing at home and we are winning this game.” The matter-of-fact, defiant instruction was not easy to imagine hearing in this Arsenal dressing room with any real conviction right now, not from the players and not from Slegers, who has many excellent qualities as coach, and is, by all accounts, an intelligent, detail-oriented coach of whom the players are very fond.

In decades to come, all the nice characteristics this Arsenal squad demonstrate will no doubt stand them in good stead in the real world, with their friendships, but the cliche “nice guys finish last” is starting to feel increasingly appropriate for this amiable side.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi breaks down in tears on Argentina bus ahead of legendary international bow
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi breaks down in tears on Argentina bus ahead of legendary international bow

Lionel Messi was captured in tears on Argentina's team bus ahead of his final international game.

The football icon is gearing up for his last-ever match for the Albiceleste as he prepares to tie the bow on his glittering international career against Benin in Buenos Aires.

3 After 207 games and 125 goals, Lionel Messi's Argentina career is in its final hours Credit: AFP

Messi will lead his nation out at the Monumental Stadium in what promises to be a hugely emotional night.

The 39-year-old will draw the curtain on a decorated Argentina career which has produced one World Cup win and two Copa America triumphs.

And while there was a good chance of tears on the pitch at full time, Messi seemed overcome by the occasion well before kick-off.

Messi emotional ahead of farewell

Footage shared online showed Messi being reduced to tears while the Argentina team bus made its way to the Monumental.

Fans were seen lining the streets waving flags and banners as they looked to give their national hero a fitting send-off ahead of his swansong.

However, the warm reception clearly proved too much for Messi, who was reduced to tears by the show of affection.

The camera panned to Messi in the window seat of the bus, where he was captured wiping away tears inside the bus.

With the football icon clearly overwhelmed by the enormity of the occasion, the tributes continued inside the stadium ahead of kick off.

Fans displayed a banner reading 'Thank you for everything, my captain' alongside a tifo of Messi lifting the 2022 World Cup trophy - the highlight of his storied Argentina career.

The match promises to be a fitting farewell to his 21 years on the international stage.

3 Messi could be seen wiping away tears inside Argentina's team bus ahead of his international farewell
