3 Fans also unveiled a special banner for Messi bearing a 'thank you' message ahead of the clash Credit: AFP

To mark the occasion, Argentina kit supplier adidas have designed a special one-off kit for Messi to wear.

The Inter Miami star will wear a strip which features several subtle tributes, as it features striking gold details on the Argentina crest, numbers and what look distinctly like a set of goat horns.

Messi's personal logo also appears on the chest, while his name and famous no.10 are presented in gold.

The shirt will bid a fitting farewell to his Argentina career, where he has scored 125 goals in 207 appearances for his national team - including eight goals at this summer's World Cup.

Sports.title: EFL club at risk of FIFA sanction after being accused of ordering player back from international duty early
Sports.content:
EFL club at risk of FIFA sanction after being accused of ordering player back from international duty early

QPR face a possible FIFA sanction after midfielder Glen Kamara returned to the club from international duty earlier than expected.

The Football Association of Finland has claimed that the Championship club withdrew Kamara before Tuesday's Nations League game against Belarus.

3 Kamara cut short his international commitments with Finland to return to QPR Credit: Getty

FIFA rules state a player released for international duty must be available to their nation for the entire international break, unless an agreement is in place for an early return.

In addition, any withdrawn player cannot play for their club five days after the end of the window, without the consent of the national team association.

Quoted on the Finnish FA’s website, head coach Jacob Friis said: "Glen was in a difficult situation as his club insisted he leave the camp and return to London.

"He had to make a decision that was obviously not what we wanted."

Marco Casagrande, general secretary of the Finnish FA said QPR had ordered Kamara to leave the camp prior to the clash with Belarus.

He added that the west London club had even organised a flight to return him to London with Friday’s crunch Championship clash at West Ham, live on talkSPORT 2, in mind.

However, Kamara is now at risk of suspension for the game at the London Stadium after the Finnish FA filed a complaint to FIFA.

Finland chief points finger at QPR

Casagrande said: “It’s really unfortunate that he’s being put in a situation where he’s practically forced to make a really difficult choice due to pressure from the club.

“The player is in a difficult position. We regret it and, of course, understand it.

“The regulations are very clear, and in our view, they were not fully followed in this case.

3 Kamara joined QPR on loan this summer from French side Rennes Credit: Getty

“FIFA will definitely be informed. The player has not been available for the entire international window, as the regulations say he should be.

“After that, it’s up to FIFA how they proceed with that matter.”

QPR boss Julien Stephan confirmed that the club are in dialogue with the Finnish FA over the situation.

“There is dialogue between the club and Finland federation which I am not involved in,” Stephan said this week.

“I will know in two or three days what the exact situation is with Glen for Friday’s game.”

Kamara has started three of QPR’s eight Championships games this season while coming off the bench on four occasions.

3 Stephan says he doesn't yet know whether he can call on Kamara for Friday's trip to West Ham Credit: Getty

The 30-year-old, who has clocked up 72 caps for Finland, was an unused substitute in the first of his country’s Nations League fixtures – a 7-0 win against San Marino.

He played 45 minutes in each of the subsequent matches which saw Finland draw 0-0 with Belarus before edging past Albania 2-1.

Sports.title: Harry Kane is England GOAT, says Jude Bellingham, as Thomas Tuchel demands captain wins Ballon d’Or
Sports.content:
Jude Bellingham has declared that Harry Kane is the greatest England player in history.

On a night in which he went level with Peter Shilton on a record 125 Three Lions caps, captain Kane excelled once again as he scored two goals during a comfortable 3-0 win over Czechia in the Nations League.

3 Kane was back at his very best for England on his landmark 125th appearance at international level Credit: Getty

His first came on 40 minutes with a close-range finish from Morgan Rogers' stunning cross, and the second arrived via a Lewis Hall corner midway through the second half.

Kane also assisted the opener, an own goal from Vladimir Coufal, and now sits on 91 goals in 125 appearances for England.

The 33-year-old became the oldest player to score two goals in two consecutive appearances after his double against Croatia, and sits on 13 overall for 2026.

Kane will undoubtedly be regarded as one of the greatest to have worn an England shirt but, for Bellingham, he's the best ever.

Bellingham calls Kane the England GOAT

When asked to put Kane's achievements in perspective, he explained to ITV: "There's not really much more you can say that hasn't already been said.

"I can only really talk from my perspective and that's that he's, first and foremost, an unbelievable human being. As a captain, as a man, he looks after each and every single person, he's the one to always take responsibility when something needs doing off the pitch.

"Then on the pitch, you're running out of superlatives - he's the best England player that's ever worn the shirt and it's an honour to play with him."

"I think you'd have to say so," Bellingham replied on whether Kane is better than ever. "He's playing at a level which is pretty unmatched when you look across the world.

"He's scoring goals for fun, still dropping deep and delivering those passes in behind and wide, and contributing in so many areas... and he's getting back as well, tackles and everything!

"He's only getting better, so we'll have to use that for as long as we can."

3 For Bellingham, Kane is the very best player to have represented England amid his latest Three Lions success Credit: Getty

Tuchel: Kane deserves Ballon d'Or glory

Kane has 12 goals in 11 appearances for England and Bayern Munich so far this season.

He is also one of 30 nominees for the 2026 Ballon d'Or, which will be awarded during its ceremony on October 26 in London.

And when asked by talkSPORT if Kane should win, which would make him the first English champion since Michael Owen in 2001, England boss Thomas Tuchel emphatically said: "Of course.

"I'm his coach. He was my player at Bayern Munich. Now he's my player in the England national team. So he has my vote, but I unfortunately don't have a vote."

On the striker's latest success at international level, Tuchel added: "He is special. I don't know why he's special, but I think he puts in a lot of work and he's a brilliant role model for everyone.

"He's just a fantastic leader, very calm personality, very focused and very calm to speak with in camp. And like I said, leads by example and he did it again today.

3 Tuchel believes that Kane should win the Ballon d'Or, making him the greatest player in world football Credit: Getty

"He's just so high in quality in finishing his actions. But the way he plays at the moment, he's involved in the build up, he's involved in the switch off play.

"So, he's in very, very good shape, puts the intensity in as the first one to lead the high press for us. It's very impressive."

Sports.title: Harry Kane the star of the show with 9/10 rating but England teammate has ‘too many wobbly moments’
Sports.content:
Harry Kane the star of the show with 9/10 rating but England teammate has ‘too many wobbly moments’

England made it three wins on the bounce as they rounded off the international break with a dominant 3-0 win over Czechia.

On a night where Harry Kane equalled Peter Shilton’s record of 125 Three Lions caps, the captain marked the occasion with two goals to inspire his team to victory in the last of their four Nations League games.



6 Kane made it six goals from four games in this international break on a memorable night at Wembley Credit: Getty

Returning to Wembley after their 7-0 thumping of Croatia, Thomas Tuchel’s side were looking to put in another strong display.

And they did just that against Czechia, as England took the lead after 27 minutes when ex-West Ham defender Vladimir Coufal turned Kane’s dangerous cross into his own net.

From then on, the home side looked a threat on every attack with Kane dropping deep to start moves with some pinpoint passing.



And on 40 minutes, the Three Lions' talisman got the goal his performance deserved as he finished off a brilliant team move by tapping home Morgan Rogers’ sublime first-time cross.

Kane's 90th England goal was also his fifth of the international break, and it wasn't long before he extended his tally to six.



In an equally dominant second half, Kane grabbed his second goal on 57 minutes when he rose highest to head home Lewis Hall's corner.

This sealed a result which sees England end the extended international break with three wins from four - claiming victory in each of their last three outings after losing the first to Spain.



After another strong showing, you can read all of talkSPORT's Adrian Durham's Three Lions player ratings below...

6 Vladimir Coufal gave England a helping hand as he diverted Kane's cross into his own net for the opening goal

6 It was a familiar story as Kane grabbed another two goals for the Three Lions Credit: Getty

Kane praise on historic night

It was always going to be a memorable night for Kane as he made his record-equalling 125th international appearance, and the England captain delivered a virtuoso display to go with it.



As well as two well-taken goals, the Ballon d'Or candidate showcased all of his playmaking abilities by dropping deep and picking out his teammates with a number of incisive crossfield balls.

And Durham was full of praise for England's all-time record goalscorer as he wrote his name into the history books again.

"Absolutely stunning yet again, as he equalled Peter Shilton’s England caps record," was the talkSPORT commentator's assessment.

Pickford concern

Despite a clean sheet in the comfortable victory, Jordan Pickford's display did little to convince Durham he should remain England's No.1.



After returning between the sticks in England's thrashing of Croatia having been dropped for James Trafford in their first two games, the Everton stopper was shaky in the early stages tonight.

Pickford almost got caught in possession twice in the opening 20 minutes, but came away unscathed on both occasions.

Durham gave him a 6/10 rating - the joint-lowest of England's players - and said: "Too many wobbly moments but another clean sheet."

6 Jordan Pickford failed to convince Durham despite having little to do against Czechia Credit: Getty



More to come from MLS?

After dropping to the bench against Croatia, Myles Lewis-Skelly returned to the starting XI against Czechia with a fine display.

And Durham has handed the Arsenal youngster an 8/10, praising him for a moment of sublime skill early on in the second half which ended in Kane crashing the crossbar.

He said: "Incredible moment in the second half when he fooled one Czech player with a trick, nutmegged another and got us going forward with a move that led to Kane hitting the bar."

Durham also piled praise on manager Tuchel, hailing the England boss for rotating his players and building a squad with real chemistry.



He concluded: "Changed things up and got it right again, he’s creating harmony in the squad as well."

6 Myles Lewis-Skelly impressed with his ability on the ball as he started in his third match of the international break Credit: Getty

6

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo accuses Jorge Jesus of broken promises in explosive statement as he details Portugal departure saga
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo has delivered a lengthy statement in which he hits out at Portugal coach Jorge Jesus over broken promises.

Ronaldo dramatically left his national team's camp last week over his apparent frustrations with game time in the international break.



4 Ronaldo has released a strong statement that gives his side of the story amid a fallout with Jesus Credit: Getty

He and Jesus agreed that he would play in the first and last of their four matches but on the morning of the second match against Norway, the latter said he would play him for 30 minutes.

Ronaldo did not feature at all during the match and stormed down the tunnel at full-time of the 2-1 victory for Portugal before leaving the camp.

Now, in a statement posted by Fabrizio Romano, the 41-year-old has given a detailed account of his side of the story.



Ronaldo told not to retire after World Cup

"This is the truth on what has happened with Jorge Jesus. As I promised, I decided to recount, in the first person and directly, the circumstances surrounding the last training camp of the national team," Ronaldo said.

"After the 2026 World Cup I prepared a letter to the Portuguese people, which I still keep, with the words I want to address to them when I leave our team for good.



"At the end of the competition, already on the flight back from the United States, the president of the federation asked and insisted that I reconsider the decision to leave, because the FPF wanted me to continue. Right afterwards he asked me for my opinion on the name of the current head coach, which he was considering alongside other names he did not reveal to me.

"I told the President of the Federation that, in my opinion, it would be the right choice. That is why, on the day the current head coach was presented, I was genuinely happy with the choice. It was the right option, as the results are confirming. A few days later I received a first contact from the new national team coach saying he would like to meet me in person.



Ronaldo accuses Jesus of broken promises

"I said yes and we scheduled it for the end of my holidays. We met at the Cidade do Futebol, where my club was holding its pre-season training camp. That day the coach told me he was counting on me and that my presence was fundamental to his project.

"He presented me, right there, with a plan for my participation. He told me I would play the first match and the last one, and that for reasons of physical management he would always make three to four changes per match.

"At that point he raised the possibility of me not travelling with the national team to Norway and Denmark. He proposed that I play the first match and stay in Portugal, then rejoin before the match at the Dragao.

4 Ronaldo has revealed what he was promised by the Portugal boss, who he claims to have 'broken his word'



"I refused this proposal immediately. It seemed obvious to me that I could not accept it. It was not because I would not play the matches abroad that I would stop captaining our team. That privilege of staying in Portugal would not be a good example. The coach ended up agreeing with my analysis.

"This conversation was attended by Simao Coutinho, sporting director of Al Nassr, the person to whom the current coach reported throughout last season and one of those responsible for his signing by the club in 2025. On the eve of the start of the camp the coach came to my house in Lisbon, at his request, for another conversation with me.

"The conversation was calm and all the principles agreed in August were maintained. I played the match at Alvalade and, although substituted, I made no problem of it. I put the armband on Bruno Fernandes myself, far from imagining that I might be taking my last steps as a player and captain of the national team. What mattered to me that day was our victory. Winning is always good; in Portugal and for my country, even better.

"At lunchtime on the day of the match in Norway, an assistant to the coach came to the table where the group was having lunch and informed me that the coach wanted to speak to me.



"To my absolute surprise, the coach asked me if I was fit to play 30 minutes. I was fully focused on my physical recovery, integrated with my teammates as always, and thinking that I would not play that day. Without any problem.

"This request was something outside my physical recovery and training plan — because I was only going to play on the 4th at the Dragao — but of course I said yes.

"He replied that I should then be ready because I would play 30 minutes. The rest everyone knows. I warmed up from half-time, watched the minutes go by, and was not called. The coach had broken his word to me.

"At the end of the match I only wanted everything to finish with the victory and to be alone. I did not go to greet the fans. A failing that is solely my responsibility and that should not have happened. I apologise to the Portuguese who supported us intensely there, I apologise to the fans, and I apologise to those who, without being Portuguese, may have travelled there to see me and whom I may have disappointed.



Ronaldo and Jesus' crunch meeting after Norway match snub

Ronaldo also revealed key details of a meeting that he had with Jesus.

"48 hours later we had a conversation — myself, the coach and Simao Coutinho — since he had been the one accompanying our conversations in August. It was a deep moment, very frank, without any kind of filter. We agreed that there was only one way to close this "case": that the coach repeat what he had just told me in private, in the presence of Simao Coutinho, but in the press room.

"What was agreed was simple: the coach would begin the press conference with this subject, seeking to close the matter by telling the truth. He would say that I never asked to play any minutes, that it was the coach and no one else who proposed the plan for this camp to me, and that it was a mistake to put me on to warm up and then not bring me on, and that if it happened again he would not do it.

"We ended that meeting with the coach asking me for a hug, promising me that he would say at the conference what he had just said to me, and that the matter would be overcome. I would not play in Denmark and I would play the match at the Dragao. All of this in the presence of Simao Coutinho, always.



4 Ronaldo only played one of Portugal's four matches in the break, which was their 1-0 win over Wales Credit: Getty

"At the coach's request, a meeting then took place between himself, Simao Coutinho and Tiago Craveiro by video conference, in which what we had discussed was summarised. A short document was produced which I myself validated and which, with my knowledge, was delivered to the coach, as he had requested.

"The conference was what is known: the posture had nothing to do with our meeting; I heard expressions and an aggressiveness that I do not believe I deserved, an attitude of "I want, I can and I command" that he never showed me, not even remotely, in private the day before.

"The notes I validated were the following: "I think it is important, also because it is the truth, to clarify a few things before talking about Denmark:



1. I myself, and no one else, proposed to Cristiano a plan for him this sporting season with the National Team. It was a long and very good conversation.

2. I know how much he lives and loves the national team and the weight he has in the world, and even more the weight and the positive influence he has had on the national team for 24 consecutive years.

3. The plan I proposed to Cristiano was accepted.

4. He never questioned my options. He was exemplary, loyal and professional.

5. The match in Norway was not part of the plan I drew up for him. However, I felt that he had managed to recover physically from the first match and I warned him that I might have to use him. Cristiano agreed.

6. I made a mistake by putting someone of the stature of Pele or Maradona on to warm up and then not putting him in the game. If it were today I would not do it.

7. To close the subject: I want Cristiano in the National Team. In fact I do not want him a little, I want him a lot. Fortunately he also believes in me. He believed at Al Nassr and he does here as well.

8. About not greeting the fans. We have already spoken about that. Someone who has played more than 230 matches for the national team does not receive lessons from me on love for Portugal. It was a moment of frustration that erases nothing. He is the player who gives the most autographs, takes the most selfies, and shows the most affection to the fans. Let us not invent problems where they do not exist. When we are not happy we react. That was all.

"None of these notes, therefore, said that the coach should even apologise to me. It was the second time he had broken his word to me. I decided to leave the camp without waiting for any further breach of word. For me the truth is still the most important thing in the relationship between people.

"However much it hurts, let them tell me the truth. In fact, in a conversation I had with the President of the FPF and with the coach on the morning of the day of that press conference — they can certainly confirm this — I reaffirmed that if they did not want me there they should tell me. It was enough for them to be frank with me. I would accept that and I promised that we would prepare something beautiful, as I dream will happen, and no one would be left angry.

"I remember it as if it were today. They replied in unison that no. That my place was in the national team. Never, at any moment, have I interfered in any technical or tactical decision of any coach or national team manager in almost 25 years of career. I accept, for better or worse, what they propose that I do.



4 Ronaldo also apologised to fans and his teammates for the drama surrounding his exit Credit: Getty

"I respect the decision, and when they break their word to me, I feel that my place is not there. I also owe an apology to my national team teammates for having left the camp.

Ronaldo insists he's not retiring

Many will have questioned whether or not Ronaldo may have played his last match for Portugal amid his exit - but he has insisted that this is not the case.

"Despite the absolute breach of trust in the coach's word, as those who witnessed these conversations can attest, I should not have done it. The responsibility is exclusively mine. I apologise to the Portuguese people once again, but the breaking of one’s word has, for me, a defining impact.



"I felt that, from that point on, my remaining would only harm the working group, and I did what I have always said I would do if I did not feel useful: I packed my bags and left.

"The consequence of this act of mine must be assessed and punished by the Portuguese Football Federation. I understand that the punishment should have no mitigating factors. I am not just any player; I am team captain, and that constitutes an aggravating factor.

"I have already apologised, but I know that attitudes must have consequences. Anyone who is in football as I am knows that, regardless of each person’s status, the rules are the same for everyone.

"On this subject, I have heard a great deal of talk about farewell matches, that I must have a dignified farewell and that the Federation wants to give me that opportunity.



"I learned in life, often hungry and with nothing to eat, that no one gives anything to anyone. I can promise all my fans, naturally and especially all Portuguese people, that we will have one or more farewell matches; there will be time for that.

"But when I think of the national team, what I really think of is competing. That is what I thought on the day I was given the news of my father's death.

"I was at a camp with our national team and I decided to stay there until the end of the match the following day. I did for the country what I would never do for any club.

"Therefore, if I am physically well, playing for my club, with goals I hope, after serving the suspension that may be applied to me, I will be available, as I have always been until today, to compete and win for our national team. This is, believe me, the purest of truths. Cristiano Ronaldo."



Portugal won all four of their Nations League matches against Wales, Norway and Denmark.

They faced Norway on two occasions, with a 2-1 win on Sunday night capping off their international break.

Sports.title: EFL icon reveals he ‘died twice in four days’ as he bravely opens up about cocaine and alcohol addiction battle
Sports.content:
EFL icon reveals he ‘died twice in four days’ as he bravely opens up about cocaine and alcohol addiction battle

Former Millwall and Crystal Palace stalwart Matt Lawrence has bravely opened up on his near-death experiences while battling a severe drug addiction.

Lawrence enjoyed an career in the EFL spanning nearly 20 years, making over 600 appearances for the likes of Fulham, Millwall and Palace.



4 Lawrence captained Millwall in their first ever FA Cup Final appearance in 2004 Credit: Getty

Best known for his six-year spell at the Den, the ex-defender captained the Lions in the 2004 FA Cup final against Manchester United.

In 2006, Lawrence moved across south London to rivals Palace - then under the ownership of talkSPORT's Simon Jordan.

He would spend four years at Selhurst Park, featuring 135 times in all competitions before a stint at Gillingham between 2010 and 2012.



But after hanging up his boots in 2015, Lawrence struggled to cope with the transition and battled with a crippling drug addiction.

This culminated in him technically dying twice in the space of four days in March 2021 after the cocaine he bought in New York was laced with a fatal dose of fentanyl, which the 52-year-old revealed in a recent interview with the Daily Mail.



Lawrence shares addiction story

Having now been sober for over a year, Lawrence sat down with Jim White and his former chairman Jordan to bravely share his story.

The former EFL star admitted he had been unable to cope with the end of his playing career and the structure it provided him.



Lawrence told White and Jordan: “When football stopped, life stopped for me almost. And I don't think that's being melodramatic either, it did.

“I very much enjoyed the structure, the regimentation. I was a student first, and then I was a footballer. And all of those times, you have a timetable.”

He continued: “I made a very foolish mistake of, because I'd been to university, because I had a degree, I thought that I was going to be smart enough to just do okay without a plan.

4 Lawrence played for Crystal Palace between 2006 and 2010 - departing in the same year Jordan left Selhurst Park Credit: Getty



“I didn't have a plan.”

Sharing how his struggles then spiralled into addiction, Lawrence revealed this began with alcohol before he began to suffer with drug abuse too.

He explained: “I very much got dictated to by drugs and alcohol for probably a decade of my life, until 423 days ago when I got clean and sober.

“But first I fell into alcohol, and then with alcohol came cocaine. And then the cocaine controlled me.

"I was, again, stupid but smart. I thought I'd be able to control my habits. And as so many addicts, it's very, very hard, if not impossible, to control habits and they get a hold of you.”



'The priest gave me the last rites'

As mentioned, the darkest point of Lawrence's addiction came five years ago in Manhattan, when he ingested cocaine that turned out to be laced with deadly synthetic opioid fentanyl.

4 Lawrence opened up his addiction struggles and journey to recovery

Narcan, a brand name for naloxone, an emergency drug used to combat the effects of opioids, was able to help save his life on two occasions, as the same sequence of events happened twice within days of each other.

Lawrence revealed that while his near-death experiences initially prompted to get sober, the road to recovery has been a long one.



He told talkSPORT: “In 2021 I died twice within the space of four days. It was March 17th, 2021, and then March 21st, 2021.

“And that in itself, me saying it out loud, is a help because I haven't been able to really – I've been able to compartmentalize it. It didn't happen to me.

“Because I passed out, because I stopped breathing, and I was resuscitated, and I got injected with Narcan and taken to hospital, I wasn't aware that I had died twice.

“When I came out of the hospital, I looked fine. I felt fine. I had got shocked. I did get sober for six months, but then I just got back on that sort of carousel wheel of the same destructive personality and destructive traits.



4 Lawrence opened up his addiction struggles and journey to recovery Credit: Getty

“And it's only been recently that I've got clean, and it's been hard work. It's been the hardest thing I've ever done."

Explaining just how touch-and-go things were in his a second drug-induced near-death experience, Lawrence revealed he was even given his last rites before he was saved by medical staff.

He bravely shared: “I was in the pub having a drink after work, and the person that I was with, the owner of the bar is a Catholic, and I knew the priest.



"The priest gave me the last rites, which is as close as you can get without seeing the light at the end the tunnel, and somebody welcoming you in, whoever you believe in.

“So I got issued with the last rites and lived to tell the tale.”

Now 423 days sober, Lawrence shared an uplifting message to listeners, as he vowed to do his utmost to continue this way.

Rounding off, he said: “I know that today I'm 423 days clean and sober and tomorrow I will be 424. But I can't really look a great deal further than that.

"I can't possibly sit here to anybody listening or to you guys and say, 'I'll come on the show next year and I'll be sober then' - I can't say that.



“But I will try my damnedest to be clean and sober in the years to come.”

Sports.title: Premier League club set to buy land by stadium in £1.6m deal
Sports.content:
Coventry City are reportedly set to finalise the purchase of £1.6million worth of land next to their stadium.

The Sky Blues are in their third spell at the Coventry Building Society Arena, the first of which began in 2005.



2 Coventry are set to buy more land near their home stadium as part of a deal with the local council Credit: Getty

It was announced in August 2025 that they had finally completed the purchase of the stadium during the week of its 20th anniversary.

Coventry are now on course to provide further investment at their ground with their latest purchase.

As reported by the BBC, they will buy the area that is currently home to Car Park C.



It is owned by Coventry City Council, who will sign off the £1.6m deal on October 13 during a cabinet meeting.

Car Park C is one of three such spaces at the stadium and, situated on the other side of the A444, can fit 900 vehicles.



"Control of the car park will enable CCFC to plan for the future and look at wider regeneration of the area, which is exciting," the council's deputy leader Councillor Lynnette Kelly said.

The money is also set to be paid over ten years and go to the club's Sky Blues in the Community charity instead of the council.



As per a contractual obligation, the cash must fund in the region of £160,000 of sport and culture activities in Coventry each year.

"It really is a win-win situation that will help our Premier League Sky Blues to grow stronger, and the people of the city, especially those that have less access to opportunities, to grow healthier," Kelly added.

Coventry owner Doug King said: "This deal will allow us to bring Car Park C alongside all the other areas already in the existing head lease and simplify future regeneration."

2 The land that holds Car Park C, which sits on the other side of the A444, will soon come under Coventry ownership Credit: Google Maps



Tough top flight return for Coventry

After a 25-year exile, Coventry won promotion back to the Premier League by winning the Championship title last season.

England and Chelsea legend Frank Lampard was on hand to guide them into the top tier in his first full season as manager.

However, they were given a rude awakening as they lost all of their four opening fixtures this season.

Coventry managed to then pick up their first victory just before the international break with a 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest.



They are 18th in the Premier League with the worst goal difference of minus nine.

Fulham and Tottenham Hotspur, two of their next three opponents, sit below them.

Sports.title: England 3-0 Czech Republic REACTION: Kane scores two on record-equalling cap as Three Lions end break with win
Sports.content:
England 3-0 Czech Republic REACTION: Kane scores two on record-equalling cap as Three Lions end break with win

England completed their international break with a comfortable 3-0 win over the Czech Republic in the Nations League.

Three Lions captain Harry Kane equalled Peter Shilton's all-time men's appearance record by making his 125th cap.



He marked the occasion with two goals to inspire his nation to a victory that all-but secures progression from the group.

The captain's two strikes came after former West Ham defender Vladimir Coufal scored an embarassing own goal at Wembley.

England will now have a month away, returning to club football before the next break comes in November.

Thomas Tuchel's side impressively won three of their four games over the three weeks of their newly extended camp.



Recap all of the action from Wembley in our live blog below...

Sports.title: Harry Kane EQUALS Peter Shilton's all-time England appearance record as Three Lions captain wins 125th cap against Czech Republic
Sports.content:
Harry Kane EQUALS Peter Shilton's all-time England appearance record as Three Lions captain wins 125th cap against Czech Republic

Harry Kane equalled Peter Shilton's record tally of 125 England caps when he stepped onto the field against the Czech Republic.

The England captain is already the country's record scorer with what is now 91 goals and added another record to that at Wembley in the Nations League.

Kane, 33, made his senior international debut in 2015 against Lithuania and scored a header within 80 seconds of replacing Wayne Rooney.

Since then he has built an extraordinary career with the Three Lions, reaching two European Championship finals and the semi-finals of the World Cup.

Shilton, meanwhile, said in a video message: 'Hi, this is a message for Harry Kane. Peter Shilton here. I would just like to congratulate you on equalling my caps record for England. And you will go on and beat it in November, I'm sure of that.

'Maybe you will set a record that will never be beaten, because you are still going strong Harry, still playing well and scoring goals, and I know how much dedication and hard work you actually put into achieving this, especially as a striker.

'I think that is probably the hardest position to play and goalkeeper is just behind that because of the responsibility.

'You have been a great captain and will be in the future and obviously good luck for tonight, obviously it's another game in the Nations Championship but I am sure we will get a good result.'

Peter Shilton's message to Harry Kane as the #ThreeLions captain equals his all-time caps record ❤️🦁 https://t.co/ssT8Wv6t1G — England (@England) October 6, 2026

Harry Kane has equalled Peter Shilton's record of 125 caps for the England national team

Kane picked up an assist for the opening goal of the game at Wembley, with his dangerous cross diverted into the Czech goal by Vladimir Coufal. He then scored his 90th goal, with Elliot Anderson and then Morgan Rogers putting it on a plate for their captain to tap in from a few yards.

He then made it 3-0 in the second-half when he headed in from Lewis Hall's corner, taking himself to 91 senior goals for his country.

He said after the game: 'It was the perfect night for me personally and for the team. It's an extremely proud evening for sure.'

The Bayern Munich striker is the seventh highest scoring man of all time in international football, though he has some ground to make up on record-holder Cristiano Ronaldo's 146.

His remarkable career with England would never have happened had he chosen to play for Ireland, where his father is from. As a child he paid regular visits to his dad's homeland.

Kane has far outstripped the previous top scorer, Wayne Rooney, whose 53-goal tally he surpassed in 2023.

The Bayern Munich striker is also England's record goalscorer at World Cups, having hit 14 to nearest rival Gary Lineker's 10.

By this stage he is becoming synonymous with the word record and that's not just in the scoring department.

He was the quickest player to reach 100 caps for England, blitzing to that stage in nine years, 167 days, from March 27 2015 to September 10 2024.

Incredibly, he has racked up a record 92 caps as England captain, a number which outweighs most players' total number of caps.

Kane also has the most goal contributions at major tournaments, having bagged 21 times – a national record in itself – and provided four assists to tally 25 overall.

He scored inside 80 seconds of coming on for England on his debut against Lithuania in 2015

He replaced Wayne Rooney and scored within 80 seconds - and the rest is now history

He said on ITV prior to the game: 'I think it is always special walking out now and seeing the stadium with the excitement of what's to come. I try and not take it for granted - it is a special night tonight but we have to focus on the job.

'I felt like I was waiting on the sideline for ages to come on for Wazza. It was just as I dreamt it - coming on and scoring and it was the start of something special.

'I am extremely proud to represent and play for England. I have been lucky enough to do it a fair few times.

'We have been extremely close to a trophy for a while now. I think we are closer than we have ever been. The team is in a good place, I'm in a good place.'

Sports.title: Trent Alexander-Arnold finds his feet in new role under Thomas Tuchel - while Jordan Pickford will have to excel in one key area to hold on to his England No 1 shirt from James Trafford, writes JACK GAUGHAN
Sports.content:
Trent Alexander-Arnold finds his feet in new role under Thomas Tuchel - while Jordan Pickford will have to excel in one key area to hold on to his England No 1 shirt from James Trafford, writes JACK GAUGHAN

Thomas Tuchel believes that Trent Alexander-Arnold has needed to buy into the new ideas being implemented by England, to move a little bit further out of his comfort zone in order to really impact this team.

That is apparently focused on playing more vertically, happy offering more width and generally appearing more active in attacking areas.

Tuchel has seen the Real Madrid right back trying to do that, rather than constantly reverting to the quarterback role of pinging passes everywhere from deep central areas. And encouragingly, he still managed those long, raking crossfield beauties while spending much of the night in more dangerous positions.

The England boss thinks that switch in positional mentality will also help Bukayo Saka flourish - with somebody buzzing around him, under or overlapping - and Alexander-Arnold's progressive performance against Czech Republic indicated what he can offer.

Before half-time, only Marc Guehi registered more touches than his 47. Many of them were in the final third and only 11 came inside the England half. Nobody was more engaged in that first half than Alexander-Arnold and there is definitely a way for Tuchel to engender the best out of somebody who really ought to have registered more caps than 36.

'He can impress and mark his territory and show his true capacity that no one's doubting,' Tuchel said on Friday and proof of that came a few days later.

Trent Alexander-Arnold (left) has bought into Thomas Tuchel's wish to play more vertically

Harry eyes more history

Having equalled Peter Shilton's record 125 England caps, Harry Kane will have his eyes on other places in history on a more global scale before the European Championship in 18 months' time.

Two goals on the night – the first beautifully crafted, a lofted one touch pass by Elliot Anderson and a first-time cross from Morgan Rogers – took Kane to 91 in an England shirt.

That nudged him clear of Malaysia's Mokhtar Dahari from the 1970s and India's Sunil Chhetri, who retired last year. Kane finished the night with Robert Lewandowski's record of 92 international goals now firmly in his sights and could pass it next month.

Already sixth in the all-time list, it is conceivable that he surpasses Ali Daei's haul of 108, with the ex-Iran striker nestled in third behind Lionel Messi and everybody's favourite sulker, Cristiano Ronaldo.

Given that Kane contributes significantly more to the side than merely goals, dropping just as deep as normal on Tuesday night, then the idea of him being described as England's finest player ever is not particularly farfetched. One piece of silverware would rubberstamp that and his legacy may be defined by what happens across a few weeks in 2028.

Harry Kane scored twice for England against Czech Republic to take his Three Lions tally to 91

A sigh of relief (sort of) for Manchester City at last...

Manchester City have bigger problems to deal with than player fatigue at the moment but there will have been a sigh of relief from Enzo Maresca just after the hour when Guehi and Anderson were withdrawn.

Both had started every match of this camp - Guehi playing almost every minute until the Czechs - and even though Tuchel feared the Saturday-Tuesday turnaround, felt he must pick both City stars for the final match as they look to secure a quarter-final spot.

Kane is the only other to have started all four and Tuchel will be pleased that the trio came through unscathed following Bournemouth's disappointment at the handling of Alex Scott at the weekend. But Tuchel also rightly points to how for just over a fortnight, whatever England do supersedes the anxiety of any clubs.

Jordan Pickford and James Trafford bid to pass the test

Fourteen minutes to go and Tuchel had his arms aloft, gesturing in Jordan Pickford's direction. He'd just misplaced a clipped pass into midfield and to be honest, looked like he had been struggling with boredom for much of the night.

'There's nothing better than playing a pass through the lines, or a longer pass,' Pickford told us recently when asked about goalkeepers becoming even more active in the build-up. He takes great pride in that side of his game and still registered around 80 per cent successful passes for the evening, with many of them risky through the lines.

You suspect it is on that battleground where either he or James Trafford will prevail before the Euros.

Jordan Pickford's distribution will be key if he to keep James Trafford from taking his No 1 spot

Ashley educating the young

There are some strong initiatives around England home games and one of them is for an ex-international to speak with teenagers in the FA's system about his experiences. Ashley Young was at Wembley for this and talked with the Under 15s, organised by Michael Johnson, head of talent ID from the Under 14s to the 17s. Certainly not a bad experience for talented youngsters.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi leaves Argentina stars and fans in tears as he pays poignant tribute to his late father on Buenos Aires farewell: 'I don't want to leave'
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi leaves Argentina stars and fans in tears as he pays poignant tribute to his late father on Buenos Aires farewell: 'I don't want to leave'

The tears which flowed down the cheeks of Lionel Messi were some of the surely millions shed by his countrymen on the pitch and in the stands at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires. With the specter of his father hovering over him, Messi described his final match as perhaps 'the saddest day of my career.'

It was a grand occasion befitting maybe the greatest No. 10 to don the blue and white of Argentina. It was an emotional evening the other man to challenge that claim, Diego Maradona, never received.

Long after the final whistle blew on a 3-0 win over Benin, where Messi chipped in his 126th and final goal plus a pair of assists, he admitted to the over 80,000 in the audience, 'I don't want to leave.' No one else in his presence wanted to either.

Fans who prayed Messi could provide one final moment of brilliance in a career full of them weren't left disappointed as he created Argentina's opening two goals. Then, he struck the net on his own to put a final punctuation mark on his time in sky blue and white after two Copa America titles, an Olympic gold medal and - most importantly - a World Cup.

Long before the match began, tears rolled down the face of the beautiful game's Lilliputian giant both on the bus and on the pitch before the national anthem as his three sons joined him.

A large tifo of an Argentina shirt with the words 'Gracias 10' in gold was displayed on the pitch. It was a color scheme reflected on the shirts of the Argentina players, with gold names and numbers. Instead of Adidas' iconic three stripe logo, Messi's stylized 'M' logo replaced it.

The whole Monumental is buzzing with “Messi, Messi, Messi, Messi.” Unreal atmosphere. 🤯🐐🇦🇷 pic.twitter.com/J0R7RyF4ia — MC (@CrewsMat10) October 7, 2026

Lionel Messi has played his final match for Argentina in an emotional affair in Buenos Aires

Tears rolled down the face of the World Cup winner as he heard the national anthem

Messi's final match was crowned with a final goal to cap a 3-0 win over Benin

In his speech, Messi admitted the memory of his father, Jorge, overwhelmed the occasion

At the tenth minute, the game was stopped for an ovation while fireworks were shot off into the night sky. Opposition players joined in the occasion, clapping along with over 80,000 Argentines.

No one else in white and blue dared to try and steal this evening for themselves. In a country where machismo is so central to its culture, perhaps that is a testament to what Messi signifies.

Teammates paid tribute in their own ways. Goalkeeper Enzo 'Dibu' Martinez, known for his eccentric hair styles, carved Messi's 'M' logo into the back of his head for the occasion.

For all his magical moments, the revelers at the Monumental hoped to see just one more, one last chance to deservedly sing Messi's name to the heavens.

The first half produced three near-chances within a span of just a few minutes time. A teasing pass from Inter Miami teammate Rodrigo de Paul met Messi's sliding boot, but just trickled left of the keeper's right post. A trademark Messi free kick was tipped away just two minutes later.

In the 32nd minute, he missed another beautiful chance generated with a pass from Lautaro Martinez that just snuck wide.

At halftime, musician Gaspar Benegas serenaded the crowd with his acoustic guitar, accompanied by a cellist - an instrumental duo befitting an occasion branded as 'El Ultimo Tango.'

The crowd was left perhaps disappointed by the lack of a goal, yet eager to see what lay in store for the final 45 minutes of Messi's national team career.

Minute 10 tribute for Lionel Messi. 🔟🩵🤍 pic.twitter.com/vUcKILVznI — Fabrizio Romano (@FabrizioRomano) October 6, 2026

A tailor made match against Benin honored the man who did so much for Argentines

Fireworks were launched into the night sky above the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires

Messi was lauded by throngs of supporters as he warmed up before his final fixture

At the national anthem, Messi's sons - Thiago, Mateo and Ciro - joined their father

Messi's first chance at goal just rolled wide off his lunging boot only 24 minutes in

It didn't take long. Just four minutes past the restart, Messi whipped in an Argentina corner for an unmarked Nicolas Otamendi, who also played his final match for La Albiceleste. Otamendi raced over to Messi, lifting him up in celebration as the crowd sang their hearts out.

Minutes later, Otamendi received his final bow. He applauded the Monumental, hugged Messi one final time and then trotted off the pitch to be replaced by Lisandro Martinez.

Another Messi free kick was parried away in the 60th minute by keeper Marcel Dandjinou, despite the well struck chance from the No. 10.

While the occasion was built to honor the past, Argentina's future got a chance to shine.

Messi fed another ball to Como maestro Nico Paz, who curled an exquisite left-footed shot past the keeper to double the lead.

After creating chances for others, the passionate thousands wondered and begged for Messi to generate one of his own.

Messi was lifted up by Nicolas Otamendi, who is also retiring, after creating the opening goal

Nico Paz (18) celebrates with Lionel Messi after he created the Como forward's goal

Then, in the 71st minute, Messi converted a penalty for the third goal on the evening

Messi's teammates surrounded him and lifted him up after the conversion

Messi then pointed to the heavens, his trademark goal celebration, for one final time

It arrived in the 69th minute, when a penalty was given after Agustin Giay was fouled inside the box and referee Fernando Véjar pointed to the spot.

His whistle blew. Messi drew a breath, then a pause. Up he strode and then sublimely struck the ball into the top right corner to crown the evening with the moment millions in Argentina and across the world waited for.

Messi's teammates mobbed him, forming a circle and jumping around him. In the stands his sons sang with the revelers as his mother, Celia, and his wife, Antonela Roccuzzo, smiled and clapped.

Messi's point to the heavens - a goal celebration he's done for years - was done with extra meaning. The 39-year-old looked up to the night sky only months after the passing of his father, Jorge.

Time ticked down on the match and on Messi. It may be fitting that he had the final kick of the game, a set piece from 21 meters out.

Véjar handed Messi his cards before blowing the whistle on full time. Teammates and opponents came over with congratulations as Benin players took selfies to mark the evening's significance.

Fans in the audience were reduced to tears at the final sight of Messi in the Argentina shirt

Even teammates, like Enzo Fernandez, let their emotions out as Messi addressed the audience

Messi's wife, Antonela, holds her son, Mateo, as the footballer spoke to the crowd

A drone show lit up the night sky with Messi's name, number and shirt. The lights then showed him kicking a ball and holding the World Cup trophy.

As tears fell from the eyes of his countrymen, his teammates, coach Lionel Scaloni, and Messi's family, singer Soledad Pastorutti crooned an anthem and hugged the football star twice before handing the athletic hero the microphone for one final message.

Messi reflected on the passing of his father before saying, 'I can only thank you all. It has been a huge pride to defend this shirt for over 20 years. We never stopped fighting, never stopped giving everything. Playing for Argentina is the most beautiful thing.'

He also addressed the heartbreak of the previous summer: 'We were close to winning the World Cup again.'

Messi too was emotional, letting the tears out throughout the tributes to him

A final salute to the fans as Lionel Messi walked off the pitch for Argentina for one last time

Messi added, 'We gave everything at the World Cup. The game against England was huge for us... We fought with all of our power. We fought all of our lives... Have no doubt that we always gave everything for this shirt.'

After thanking his teammates, Messi mused: 'This may be the saddest day of my career, leaving the national team. But I'll be here supporting whoever comes next. When we are united we are stronger than anyone else.'

He ended his speech with gratitude: 'I don't want to leave this place. I don't want to leave the field. I love all of you, and I will miss all of you. I am proud to be Argentinian.'

Still, the tributes continued. Messi completed a final lap of the Monumental, waving to the thousands who still would not depart. At the center circle, he was joined by his family.

Then, at last, the book was closed. Messi descended the steps to the locker room - waving goodbye to his nation one final time and clearing the stage for a new generation of Albiceleste heroes to make the brave attempt at filling the chasm he leaves behind.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi's wife Antonela joined by his mother Celia for Argentina icon's emotional farewell... two months on from father's tragic death
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi's family gathered at Estadio Monumental for the final game of his international career on Tuesday night.

The 39-year-old's wife, Antonela Roccuzzo, was joined by their children and Messi's mother, Celia María Cuccittini, for the friendly against Benin.

They wore Messi jerseys and were seen filming and clapping as the No 10 emerged for warm-ups before being introduced to the 85,000-strong crowd in Buenos Aires. Messi's three sons - Thiago, Mateo and Ciro - then accompanied him as he walked out of the tunnel for before kickoff.

The Argentina icon will bring the curtain down on his international career after 21 years, 125 goals, two Copa America titles and a World Cup victory.

In Messi's 208th Argentina appearance, Lionel Scaloni's team face West African minnows Benin but the otherwise-unremarkable friendly has become a seismic moment for Argentine soccer.

The game also comes almost two months to the day since Messi's father, Jorge, died at the age of 68.

Lionel Messi's wife, Antonela Roccuzzo, is in Buenos Aires for his final game for Argentina

She was joined by Messi's mother, Celia María Cuccittini, for the friendly against Benin

Messi's three sons - Thiago, Mateo and Ciro - joined him as he walked out of the tunnel

Messi's father Jorge, pictured at the 2022 World Cup final, died in August at the age of 68

Back on August 7, Jorge Messi reportedly died in a hospital in Rosario, close to the family home, a couple of months after the family revealed he had been rushed to hospital with an ongoing 'health situation'.

Jorge Messi served as his son's agent and business manager, and following his death, the 39-year-old admitted he was unsure how much longer his career would last.

'All I ever did was play football, and now I have a fair few doubts as to whether I'll carry on doing it for much longer,' Messi said.

'You were by my side from the start, we were so close to the end (of his career). Why didn't you hang on just that little bit longer so we could finish it together?'

He added: 'Dad, I still can't believe you're gone. I can't get my head round it — or rather, I don't want to. It's so hard for me to imagine that I won't see you ever again, that we won't talk anymore. I know you were suffering and that this is for the best, but you left us far too soon. We still had so much left to enjoy together.

'You kept asking me to play in the last World Cup, and it was just days before it started that you took a turn for the worse.

'It was the first time you weren't going to be at a tournament, but Mum kept telling me you'd get better and that you'd be well enough to travel. I'd tell you that we'd make it to the final so you could travel.

'Every time a match ended, I'd wait for your message and miss it. That's when I realised the situation was really bad.'

Fans poured on to the streets of Buenos Aires ahead of Messi's final ever game for his country

The friendly was played at Estadio Monumental, the 85,000-seater home of River Plate

Fireworks exploded in the skies above the capital of Argentina ahead of kickoff on Tuesday

Following Tuesday night's swansong, Messi will continue to play for Inter Miami in Major League Soccer but on August 31, he announced he would be retiring from international football.

That decision came just weeks after the World Cup final at MetLife Stadium near New York, where Spain beat Argentina and Messi's World Cup journey ended in tears.

On Tuesday in Buenos Aires, fans let off flares and carried giant banners in honor of their retiring hero, while others showed off Messi tattoos or painted images of the 39-year-old on their face.

In Messi's hometown, Rosario, a giant jersey carrying his No 10 was flown by helicopter.

The Argentine soccer federation has turned Tuesday's game - Messi's 208th for his country - into a national homage dubbed 'the last tango.'

Around 85,000 tickets to Buenos Aires' largest stadium sold out in 90 minutes, while members of Argentina's 2022 World Cup-winning squad and their families were invited back to join the tribute.

Four years ago, Messi led Argentina to victory in Qatar, securing the country's third World Cup triumph and landing the one trophy that had eluded him for so long.

Sports.title: Argentina fans display 'Malvinas' banner laying claim to the Falkland Islands in the stands at Lionel Messi's emotional farewell match
Sports.content:
Argentina fans displayed multiple 'Malvinas' banners in Lionel Messi's farewell match, laying claim to the Falkland Islands.

In an emotionally charged atmosphere at 85,000-capacity Estadio Monumental, the biggest stadium in South America, some supporters took their chance to send a political message.

One banner read: 'Las Malvinas son Argentinas,' while another showed the outline of the Falkland Islands coloured in with the blue and white of the Argentina flag.

Plenty of fans brought plastic Messi masks but even though everyone was there to celebrate arguably the greatest footballer of all time, some still chose to put the controversial topic front and centre.

The contention around the banner follows Argentina's World Cup semi-final victory over England at the FIFA World Cup and fans of their rugby team holding up similar regalia during a match against South Africa in August.

After the World Cup semi-final triumph, Argentina's players used it as an opportunity to assert their claim over the Falklands, the self-governing British Overseas Territory in the South Atlantic Ocean located around 300 miles east of Argentina.

Some fans hung banners claiming that the Falklands Islands belong to Argentina

Argentina supporters hung one image of the Falklands decorated in the national colours

Britain has ruled the Falklands since January 1833 and in 2013 in a referendum, 99.8 per cent of citizens voted to remain as a British territory. The islands were the subject of a conflict between the two nations in 1982.

The lifting of the original banner – which also read 'Los Malvinas son Argentinas' – triggered a fierce backlash in the UK.

Former Prime Minister Keir Starmer insisted that while 'the World Cup might not be ours, the Falkland Islands definitely are. Self-determination rests with the islanders and our commitment to the Falklands will never waver.'

FIFA subsequently opened an investigation, with the governing body's rules forbidding the use of any political messaging at the World Cup.

They had, however, previously turned a blind eye to continued references to the 1982 conflict in a song sung by the players – and posted on social media by the country’s association – in the dressing room throughout the tournament.

Argentina President Javier Milei described the players' celebration with the banner as 'perfectly valid', and said the message 'reflects a sentiment shared by all Argentines'.

'I know that for Argentinians, we won the World Cup the moment we beat England because that's really what everyone wanted,' he said.

The banner at the rugby game came after the Pumas tried to mock England by wearing a kit paying homage to Diego Maradona's World Cup win in 1986, en route to which he scored the infamous 'Hand of God' goal against the Three Lions.

It came after their footballers did similar after beating England in the World Cup semi-final

Argentina rugby fans held up a 'Malvinas' banner laying claim to the Falkland Islands

Fans snapped up tickets to pay tribute to Messi at his final international match

The British governance of the Falklands remains a sore point for many Argentinians and continues to rear its head during sporting clashes.

Argentina's farewell to Messi against Benin was a chance for the nation to say goodbye to their beloved football icon.

He called time on his international career after his side fell short against Spain in the World Cup final this summer.

The farewell fixture is his 208th and last appearance and tickets sold out in 90 minutes. Elsewhere in the country, a giant replica of his No10 shirt, emblazoned with the word 'Gracias' was unfurled in his home city of Rosario.

And in Patagonia, an 85ft, 70-ton statue of him kneeling with the World Cup trophy looms over motorists, with adulation for the former Barcelona superstar reaching new heights.

Sports.title: 'We're not going to mark Messi, we're just going to enjoy the match': Benin star admits team will roll out the red carpet for Argentina legend ahead of emotional swansong in Buenos Aires
Sports.content:
'We're not going to mark Messi, we're just going to enjoy the match': Benin star admits team will roll out the red carpet for Argentina legend ahead of emotional swansong in Buenos Aires

The man tasked with defending against Lionel Messi for his final match with Argentina has admitted he has no plan to mark the icon.

Argentina are hosting Benin at midnight UK time in Buenos Aires in what is a slightly bizarre swansong for the 2022 World Cup winner.

The South Americans scheduled low-budget friendlies against Bolivia, Burkina Faso, and Benin for the international break, but have refrained from playing Messi so he is fit for his historic farewell against the latter.

An Argentinian TV channel called C5N tracked down members of the Benin squad walking around the capital city, and centre-back Tijani Mohamed said: 'You don't mark Messi. We are just going to enjoy this match.

'I'm going to look at him like this: "Messi, you are God".

'Yes, yes I've watched the matches and that's it, a match with Messi and for me he's the best in the world, as I'm telling you.

A Benin defender says there is no plan to mark Lionel Messi in his final game for Argentina

The legendary forward is preparing for a farewell match in front of 85,000 fans in Buenos Aires

'Spain was a very tough team to play against, but I wanted Argentina to win because I really like Messi.

'Benin is a very, very good team to play with, and I can't talk about Benin right now because we have to enjoy this match, and we're going to give everything so that this celebration goes really well.'

The team's doctor chimed in: 'He's the best in the world!'

Messi has played 207 times for Argentina, scoring 125 goals and winning the World Cup alongside two Copa Americas.

The 39-year-old announced his intention to retire in August, but he had made the decision just two days after losing to Spain in the World Cup final weeks before.

'It was a decision that hurt, and still hurts, to my core, but I understand that it's the right time,' he wrote on Instagram.

'I swear that I always gave my all, not just in the last few years when we won everything, but before that too. I always fought and gave everything for this jersey, to bring you joy and make you proud to be Argentinian through football.'

More than 85,000 fans are set to attend Messi's goodbye at the Estadio Mas Monumental, where members of their 2022 World Cup-winning squad will pay tribute.

But the build-up to the clash with Benin has been marred by controversy.

Messi's penultimate match against Burkina Faso had to be played against the nation's under-23s.

The first team's charter flight from Morocco – paid for by Argentina – was cancelled and the players then refused to travel over financial compensation concerns and extreme fatigue. Argentina hammered the unsuspecting youth 7-0.

Now Benin arrive on the back of a 23-hour flight during which their video analyst Jonas Bide reportedly blacked out.

They got into their hotel only to find there is no hot water, while the artificial turf and gym were deemed too low-standard for a professional team.

Sports.title: England's World Cup charge examined with one year to go: Why Tom Banton has given Jacob Bethell a problem, the 'finisher' conundrum, the search for a back-up spinner and what happens with Brydon Carse?
Sports.content:
With exactly a year to go before the 50-over World Cup in southern Africa, Daily Mail Sport examines the state of England’s one-day team, who are starting to turn things round after a few years in the doldrums.

Brendon McCullum has the team firing now that the white-ball business is his sole focus and with the help of 'specialist mentor' Kevin Pietersen, England can go to Africa with hope of adding to their sole 50-over World Cup.

But there are questions to be answered in the 12 months between now and England's opening fixture against Bangladesh on 8 October in Windhoek, Namibia.

WHO OPENS WITH DUCKETT?

The knee injury that ruled Jacob Bethell out of the recent 2–1 series win over Sri Lanka opened the door for Tom Banton – and he barged through, with a 62-ball 73 at Headingley followed by a powerful 126 off 105 at The Oval.

And with Bethell also missing this month’s tri-series in Pakistan (also involving Sri Lanka), Banton will get another chance to show that he should be Ben Duckett’s opening partner when battle commences.

It’s hard to imagine that Bethell, whose most recent ODI knock was a polished 91 against India at Lord’s in July, will remain on the sidelines, not least because he also offers tidy left-arm spin and electric fielding. But, like Duckett, he’s a diminutive left-hander, while Banton – tall, right-handed and strong on the drive – offers a tempting contrast.

It’s not impossible that England play both in the same side, with Bethell coming in at No 3, though that risks less strength in depth among the bowling line-up.

Tom Banton was superb in the recent series against Sri Lanka, hitting a 62-ball 73 at Headingley followed by a powerful 126 off 105 at The Oval

Jacob Bethell, like Ben Duckett, is a diminutive left-hander which could count against him if England want variety at the top of the order

DOES THE MIDDLE ORDER LOOK AFTER ITSELF?

At this stage, yes. This year, Joe Root went 404 runs between ODI dismissals, taking his average back above 50, and could easily move down a place to No 4 if England feel they want both Banton and Bethell in the top three.

The equally irreplaceable Harry Brook is next in, while Jos Buttler has split his time since the 2015 World Cup mainly at No 5 or 6, and was hitting the ball as cleanly as ever before a hamstring injury cut short his series against Sri Lanka.

But with Buttler missing the Pakistan tri-series, and possibly the subsequent white-ball trip to Australia, Jordan Cox can build on the good impression he made against Sri Lanka at The Oval, both during an inventive 76 off 52 balls and with the gloves, which may scupper Jamie Smith’s attempts to re-establish himself in the one-day side.

Despite the lack of domestic 50-over experience for the current generation of batsmen, England are building up a decent pool.

During the forthcoming series in Pakistan Jordan Cox can build on the good impression he made against Sri Lanka at The Oval, both during an inventive 76 off 52 balls and with the gloves

WHAT ABOUT THE No6 AND No7 FINISHING ROLES?

After England moved on from Liam Livingstone, the rise to prominence of Will Jacks, both as a finisher and a handy off-spinner – witness his five-for against Sri Lanka at Chester-le-Street – has restored their all-round ballast.

But if he bats at No 6, as he did successfully against the Sri Lankans because of injury to Sam Curran, it risks a slightly longer tail than England would like: both Jamie Overton and Rehan Ahmed feel a place too high at No 7.

The return of Curran for this month’s trip to Pakistan should bring clarity, though an ODI average of just 22 from 33 innings means it’s reasonable to ask whether he too should be any higher than No 7.

But his left-arm seam – not to mention his very slow slower ball – offers variety, and allows England to field six bowlers (or seven, if Bethell and Root count as half a bowler each).

Sam Curran is back in the England fold - but has a point to prove

HOW DO THE SPINNERS FIT IN?

England’s one-day set-up does not face the Test side’s existential crisis when it comes to spin, mainly thanks to Adil Rashid. He turns 39 in February, but remains central to the middle-overs strategy, and needs just 27 more victims to overtake Jimmy Anderson and become England’s leading ODI wicket-taker.

Just in case, though, the selectors are casting their net wide. When Rashid sat out the Sri Lanka series, Liam Dawson (who went at just 3.25 an over) fared better than Ahmed (6.26).

And, as well as Jacks, England are taking both James Coles of Sussex and Glamorgan leg-spinner Mason Crane to Pakistan.

England’s one-day set-up does not face the Test side’s existential crisis when it comes to spin, mainly thanks to Adil Rashid

But Rashid is 39 and so England are taking both James Coles of Sussex and Glamorgan leg-spinner Mason Crane (above) to Pakistan

AND WHAT'S THE FAST BOWLING HIERARCHY?

Since the last World Cup, England’s undisputed attack leader has been Jofra Archer, who has the most wickets among the quicks (29) and the best economy-rate (5.50), and is bowling as fast as ever.

Jamie Overton and Gus Atkinson have elbowed their way up the queue, and are both good enough to bat at No 8, while Sonny Baker put a pair of harrowing white-ball debuts in 2025 behind him to bowl with pace and heart against Sri Lanka. Josh Tongue, too, is now part of the 50-over battery.

The joker in the pack is Brydon Carse, who in the last three years has sent down more ODI deliveries (805) than any fast bowler bar Archer, but is currently being investigated by the Cricket Regulator after his arrest in Derby in August, and has been told by McCullum to go away and ‘get his house in order’.

Others in the mix include Saqib Mahmood, Matthew Potts and the uncapped Sussex seamer Henry Crocombe, who will be on the plane to Pakistan. But if Curran and Jacks both feature, and Rashid is a lock-in, there will only be room for three more quicks. With a year to go, there is plenty to play for.

Sports.title: Chelsea star Moises Caicedo is hit with eight-point penalty and fine for driving £160k Audi supercar without valid licence or insurance
Sports.content:
Chelsea star Moises Caicedo is hit with eight-point penalty and fine for driving £160k Audi supercar without valid licence or insurance

Chelsea star Moises Caicedo has been given an eight-point penalty and hit with a fine for driving his £160,000 Audi RSQ8 without a valid licence or insurance.

Caicedo, who is understood to earn £250,000-a-week having signed from Brighton for £115million in 2023, was pulled over in April 2025.

He was caught near Chelsea's Cobham training ground in Surrey and appeared at Crawley magistrates' court this week.

In addition to the eight points, the fine came to £1,444 and he is now nearing a driving ban. Drivers who receive 12 points in three years are not allowed behind the wheel for six months. People with international driving licences can use them in Britain for 12 months.

The Ecuadorian has been ordered to obtain the valid licence and insurance for his supercar, which can reach 155mph and hit 60mph in just 3.8 seconds.

At the time the car was seized, Chelsea dismissed it as a 'personal matter'.

Moises Caicedo was given an eight-point penalty and fine for driving without a valid licence or insurance

The Audi RSQ8 (pictured on display in Mumbai in February) is valued at around £160,000

Driving incidents among Premier League stars have been in the headlines in recent weeks, with two Hull City players flipping their cars in the same spot.

Daily Mail Sport's Lewis Steele even visited – and drove – the dangerous spot this week.

The 24-year-old, who is no longer the most expensive footballer in British transfer history, has been injured this season and only played 14 minutes for Xabi Alonso's side.

Chelsea have missed the 65-cap international, who is one of the first names on the team sheet when fit.

The midfielder was not called up by Ecuador for games against South Korea, Japan and Panama in an effort to help him fully shake off the persistent calf issue that has been dogging him.

Alonso suggested before the international break that Caicedo is not far from a return to action and he could be involved in some capacity when the Blues face Bournemouth
