Sports.title: How FIA software bug caused chaos in Bahrain GP in Malaysia – and the emergency fix that saved the race
Sports.content:
The start of the first wet-weather race of the 2026 Formula 1 season descended into chaos. Leader Max Verstappen was the first to suffer from a lack of power while driving slowly during the formation laps behind the safety car, after which Lewis Hamilton came to a standstill and several other cars followed.

Race control was forced to stop the formation lap with a red flag, after which there was a 40-minute delay before fans actually got to see some F1 action.

Read Also: Formula 1 FIA explains software glitch that caused Bahrain GP in Malaysia race delay

FIA single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis confirmed to media including Autosport that a bug in the software supplied by the FIA and developed together with the teams over the course of multiple years was responsible for the chaos.

“We didn't manage to test the software as extensively as we would have liked because there's been very little wet running this year. There was a bit of a combination of circumstances which caused this bug to kick in,” Tombazis said during an impromptu media session post-race.

“Basically, on the formation lap, some cars went very slowly and almost came to a standstill. There was a bit of a concertina effect between cars and some cars almost stopped completely. That bug prevented then the power to be redeployed and for the cars to start again.”

This is closely related to the reduction in electrical power to 250kW in wet conditions.

Although the software required for this was tested by several teams, including Red Bull and Racing Bulls, it was not tested in the conditions behind the safety car – and therefore not at these extremely low speeds.

Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing, Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

At the Sepang International Circuit, those low speeds were reached in certain minisectors, with all the consequences that followed.

“It was mainly in some sectors where the full power was reduced. I don't know exactly what speed that was, but some cars reaching this very low speed somehow entered into a loop, which meant they couldn't re-accelerate and then it looked as if they came to a stop.”

In practice, this left drivers feeling as though the throttle pedal was no longer responding, something Oliver Bearman told the media with some surprise.

“I've never seen or felt anything like that. I was shocked that… I didn't even know that the FIA could control our throttle pedal. That was quite scary, actually,” the Haas driver said.

“My throttle pedal just stopped working. It was like it was not connected and the engine was just idling. It was so weird, I mean, shocking.”

One of the questions is why the internal combustion engine was also affected, when that should not be the case at extremely low speeds. The FIA does not yet have a formal answer to that question, but the initial suggestion is that the bug caused all throttle input to go towards recharging the MGU-K, which explains why drivers felt there was no response from the throttle pedal at all.

At first glance, it appeared as though the Mercedes-powered cars were less affected by the issue than other manufacturers, but Tombazis explained that there is no technical reason for that. It was simply related to the speeds reached in certain minisectors.

Nikolas Tombazis, FIA Photo by: Kym Illman / Getty Images

“Not all cars reached the same low speeds on the formation lap. There was a bit of a concertina effect. I think Max slowed down quite a lot, being at the front, and then some cars braked harder as they were surprised and so on. That caused some cars to experience the problem and some others to not experience it.”

How the FIA provided F1 teams with an emergency fix

The FIA then had to react quickly to get the race near Kuala Lumpur under way after all, as Tombazis explained when asked by Autosport.

“Fortunately, our guys understood the issue very, very quickly. I think the update was done very competently. It was obviously a rush job. The priority was to get running as quickly as possible again, so I think the reaction time was quite fast,” he said.

“It wasn't a perfect job and, clearly, we didn't test the updates, but I think it was the way to handle such a case.”

In practice, the update meant that the FIA lifted the energy limit constraint – the restrictions associated with the 250kW limit – for the minisectors in which the low speeds had triggered the bug. Logically, this is not a watertight solution going forward, but it was an emergency measure to ensure the race could go ahead.

“In some of the sectors, some of these reductions of power were overridden,” Tombazis confirmed. “Clearly, we didn't have five days to do the updates. We only had a few minutes, but fortunately, I think we managed to do it without compromising any safety, any racing or fairness.”

How could this happen in the first place?

After the FIA update, all the teams still had to install the modified software, which explains the delay before the restart. The Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia was saved as a result, but that still does not explain how the FIA could have missed this issue throughout all its preparations and why it only surfaced in round 16 of the championship.

“The software was tested. It just wasn't tested in those specific conditions,” Tombazis replied. “What caught us out was the fact that cars went in that very, very low speed, which was not normally contemplated.”

FIA Safety Car Photo by: Rudy Carezzevoli / Getty Images

During the tyre tests in which the software was tested, the extremely low speeds were understandably not reached. Nevertheless, there is a crucial counterargument to that: in the rain, the likelihood of a safety car – and therefore low speeds – is very high. Should the FIA not have anticipated that, and was that the governing body’s biggest mistake?

Asked that question by Autosport, Tombazis responded: “Well, any bug is a product of a mistake. I don't know of any software that doesn't have bugs and updates. Your computer probably gets updated every three days and those are all bugs.

“Of course, anticipating these things is what one hopes to do, but sometimes some very combination of events isn't properly anticipated and causes the problem. I think if we had had a bit more testing, we probably would have managed to catch it in time and not to have such a situation.”

Although the cause of this problem is now known and a temporary fix has been introduced, the FIA still has many questions to answer internally – also to ensure that it does not happen again.

“We would all like it to be simpler, but the fact is when you have as much electrical energy, it does make it more complicated. I think you appreciate that the race has now finished about one hour ago and we haven't done a full debrief of the situation to see how we can avoid such an issue.

“Every race, we have a long debrief afterwards where we identify criticalities. Obviously, that was a major criticality and we need to make sure we avoid it.

“But can I guarantee it will never happen again? This specific problem, yes. A problem, no. But we will do our best to avoid it, of course.”

Sports.title: The slick tyre gamble that hurt McLaren and Ferrari's chances in Bahrain GP in Malaysia
Sports.content:
When the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia eventually got going after an hour and 33 minutes of delays, it became apparent that the intermediate was the tyre to be on among the opening laps - even if the Sepang circuit had looked like it was drying out.

At the front of the field, Ferrari and McLaren chose to go all-in on the dry tyres for the restart; Ferrari opted for the soft compound, while McLaren went for the mediums. When the race got underway behind the safety car, both teams were left to rue their choices as the circuit was still too slippery.

McLaren bailed on the plan early, stopping before the standing start to ensure Oscar Piastri could get a set of intermediates back onto the car, but Lando Norris and the Ferraris stuck with their choices. Charles Leclerc duly fed into the pitlane at the end of the lap, as the slick-tyre runners were swamped and then left behind by those who'd stuck with the intermediate for the start.

Lewis Hamilton and Norris surmised that, since they'd made their beds, they'd lie in them. Hamilton was asked if he wanted to stop again, but the seven-time champion reasoned that Ferrari might as well stick with the gamble given that the team was well behind - and pitting would only cost more time.

By the end of the eighth lap, the slick times were now equal with the intermediate runners; Valtteri Bottas' subsequent off then presented the inter-shod drivers with the chance to switch to slicks.

Speaking about the decision, Norris stated that the idea of starting on the slick was "quite convincing" and that he was unsure of the performance of the inter; on his recon lap to the grid, the Briton reported that the green-walled tyre was already feeling the pain on Sepang's rough surface.

Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Lando Norris, McLaren Photo by: Joe Portlock / Getty Images

"It felt maybe a little bit of a risk, because a slick on a wet track is always a bit of a risk," Norris said. "There was enough people on it that it was quite convincing at the time that it was possibly going to be the right decision.

"The laps to the grid on the inter when it was a similar kind of condition, they had so much grip and my Inter was completely shredded after one lap.

"I was convinced a slick tyre would work, but I think it was just the fact I've never really been on the inter before. Things just felt a lot better than they should have done in a way.

"If we would have had a read on an inter from a previous weekend, maybe I would have been able to understand it more. But that convinced us and it clearly convinced a lot of people.

"Oscar probably made the right decision in boxing and we got it wrong today, that's all."

Leclerc theorised that the roughness of the tarmac made it more difficult to read the track surface, as water pooled up in the gaps - and the drop in temperature that accompanied the rain ensured that the circuit took much longer to dry out than expected. Given the length of the downpour, any residual circuit temperature was swiftly extinguished.

Even though the Monegasque switched tyres, the time loss involved in pitting after the start kept him behind Hamilton, who ran longer on his set of soft tyres and quickly began to make up positions.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Carlos Sainz, Williams Photo by: Joe Portlock / Getty Images

Hamilton joked that he wasn't going to "go to the casino with the guys" after the team's gambles didn't pay off, although praised his team's strategy in keeping him out on the road. The Briton was ultimately less enamoured with the medium after making a stop on lap 31, but the late-race VSC (later a full safety car) presented a chance to return to the soft - which he put to use with a pass on Isack Hadjar for third.

"As we pulled out [of the pits], all the spray came out the back of Max’s car and I was like, 'okay, I’m done. My race is really in trouble,'" Hamilton recounted.

"We just had to stick with it. As everyone’s overtaken me, they [the engineers] were like, 'we stop.' I know we’ve already made another 26 seconds. What’s the difference from that with one minute 40 or whatever I was down? So I was just, 'Let’s just wait it out for the track to dry.'

"And once it did, it felt good that I was catching people. The car felt great then after that. Really good pitstops from my guys in the garage and then good strategy. But for us to get back to the podium, I never thought that that was going to be the case. Of course, I’m really, really grateful that we managed to get back here.

"We’ll definitely have an open dialogue, and I’m really so proud of my team. The mechanics every weekend, just the work they’re putting in, the engineers that accompany here every weekend, the catering, everyone really, really comes and gives it their best.

"Their heart’s all in the right spot. We’ve definitely got areas that we need to improve and we know that, and we’re not in any denial of that. So I think we’ll have a constructive chat, we’ll regroup, we’ll take the positives from this weekend, which the car was really good, and we’ll come back next week fighting."

Sports.title: FIA explains software glitch that caused Bahrain GP in Malaysia race delay
Sports.content:
The FIA has given insight into why Formula 1 cars experienced technical issues ahead of Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

The start of the Sepang race was delayed by 40 minutes due to a downpour; then a chaotic formation lap saw the likes front-row starters Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton suffer from a glitch which rendered throttle input ineffective, with numerous cars coming to a standstill. The red flag was waved.

The situation was branded “unacceptable” by Sergio Perez, who likened it to ‘being in a rental kart and running out of time’; Lando Norris described it “just horrible” and evidence that “we shouldn't have any of that stuff, the electronic side”, given this was linked to Formula 1’s new machinery, which features 47% electrical power.

FIA single-seater Nikolas Tombazis has now explained that, given F1 had never had competitive running in actual wet conditions this season, it was caught out by the power unit’s reaction to cars driving extremely slowly at that time. A software update therefore had to be carried out, hence a 53-minute delay to get the race restarted.

“We didn't manage to test the software as extensively as we would have liked, because there's been very little wet running this year, and there was a bit of a combination of circumstances which caused this bug to kick in,” Tombazis said.

Nikolas Tombazis, FIA Photo by: Kym Illman / Getty Images

“Basically, the formation lap, some cars went very slowly, almost came to a standstill. There was a bit of a concertina effect between cars, and some cars almost stopped completely. And that bug prevented the power to be redeployed and for the cars to start again. I think if we had had a bit more testing, we probably would have managed to catch it in time and not to have such a situation.”

Tombazis praised the FIA’s reaction when it came to fixing the issue as swiftly as possible.

“Once the problem happened, our guys realised very quickly what was happening and had to work under a lot of time pressure for an update to the software, which was issued to the teams, and the teams had to install it on their cars,” he added.

“So all of that took about 20 minutes. It may have felt like five hours for spectators waiting [for] a race and for everybody else, which is understandable, and we are sorry about that. But I think it was quite a fast reaction given the problem.”

Not everyone was so upset about some cars running into trouble, with eighth-placed Fernando Alonso joking at the end of an unusually good day for Aston Martin-Honda: “I had 50% DNFs this year, they never stopped the race for us.”

Sports.title: Russell: “You’ve got to laugh” at bad luck as F1 title drifts away
Sports.content:
Mercedes driver George Russell labelled his misfortune as laughable following Formula 1’s Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, where a power unit failure cost him a podium finish late on.

Russell was a lowly seventh on the grid at Sepang, but the correct choice of intermediate tyres on a damp track and a lightning getaway saw him surge to second into Turn 1, behind team-mate Kimi Antonelli.

Russell was however passed by Max Verstappen as early as lap six, but the first safety car period gave him a chance to sweep past Antonelli around the outside of Turn 5 at the restart as the race leader dropped down to third – though the Italian youngster found a way back into second place just eight laps later.

Further drama did not disrupt the status quo in the top three, but a late safety car meant Russell had a chance to challenge his rivals for victory. However, the chance never came as a power unit failure took him out of the race before the final restart.

“You've almost got to laugh,” Russell told Sky Sports F1 after his third retirement this season – his second purely technical DNF. “It's beyond disappointment. It's just, so many times this season it's happened.

“Of course, it's a real shame, but… Just keep on fighting. Just keep on trying to go.

“The podium, of course, looked very certain. Solid race, not amazing race, but solid race.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Alex Bierens de Haan / LAT Images via Getty Images

“Not the first time, so I'm pretty used to this feeling and these questions, let's say.”

As he said, Russell will “keep on fighting”, but is equally aware of his deficit to championship rival Antonelli reaching an unprecedented 84 points.

The Briton steered clear of any sensational comments – he won’t say the title is out of reach – but his assessment is bleak nonetheless.

“I don't need to say I think it's gone or whatever,” he added. “But, of course, it’s exceptionally unlikely, and that's just the reality.

“I knew if I wanted to come back I needed luck on my side. Unfortunately, I've had luck not on my side. So, you know, a three-point loss today being behind Kimi turned into an 18-point loss. Of course, if the issue was on the other side, it would have been an 18-point gain.

“So, yeah, it's a real shame. It's a real shame, but that's just how it is.”

Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff said the Bahrain GP in Malaysia had been one of his “worst experiences” personally, as Red Bull claimed its first victory of the year over the Silver Arrows and Russell suffered that setback.

“I'm so massively annoyed,” Wolff told Sky. “I'm not in a happy place.

Toto Wolff, Mercedes Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

“We didn't have the speed that we were hoping to have before the weekend, so there's a lot of homework to be done in order to recover, which I'm sure we will. Then the race literally went, if you consider the fight with Lewis [Hamilton] behind, went against us. We had such an advantage, one VSC, two safety cars. I mean, you couldn't be more unlucky. And to make things worse, PU failure with a few laps to go to the end with George, which is terrible for his championship and not good at all for our constructor points.”

After praising Antonelli for ‘doing the job’, the Austrian added: “It's just this overarching topic, the DNFs, that could cost us dearly also for the remaining seven races. A championship is quickly turned around against you or for you if you have a DNF, and that's why that can't continue.”

Perhaps Wolff was overdramatic there. At Sepang, Mercedes was outscored by Ferrari for just the first time since the summer break, and the Scuderia still is 151 points in arrears in the constructors’ championship. Meanwhile, Hamilton’s deficit to Antonelli in the drivers’ standings is up to 106 points.

Asked how to pull the team together after such a result, Wolff replied: “I think we have a good action plan. James [Allison, technical director] is really fully on top of it with his leadership team.

“That lifts my mood because I know we have such a tremendous group of people. In the same way as we have with HPP, they're going to sort it out. But that gives me real relief for the moment to know they are the best and they are going to find a solution. And I think we will come back strong.”

Sports.title: Stats: Verstappen avoids first win-less season since 2015, Red Bull-Ford’s first win and more | 2026 Bahrain GP in Malaysia stats and facts
Sports.content:
Before the unusually-named Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia began, Max Verstappen made it clear he wanted to avoid ending the season without a victory.

He put that right on Sunday, ensuring he claimed a victory for the 11th season in a row. He only failed to win a grand prix in his debut season at Toro Rosso (now Racing Bulls) in 2015.

But Verstappen needs to keep winning every year until 2030 to equal Michael Schumacher and Lewis Hamilton’s joint record of 15 consecutive winning seasons (from 1992 to 2006 and 2007 to 2021 respectively).

Verstappen claimed the first victory for car number three since his former team mate Daniel Ricciardo won the Italian Grand Prix for McLaren five years ago. Two other drivers on the grid today have won with that number: Fernando Alonso twice in 2013 at Ferrari and Hamilton three times for McLaren in 2011, both in seasons before the FIA introduced ‘career numbers’.

This was the 72nd victory of Verstappen’s career. It came in Malaysia’s first grand prix in nine years, which Verstappen also won, taking the second win of his career at that point.

The race carried the title ‘Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia’ as it took the place of April’s cancelled race in the Middle East. It is by no means unique for one country to hold an event named for another: San Marino, Luxembourg and Switzerland all gave their names to races in other nearby countries: Italy, Germany and France respectively.

But there were a few noteworthy differences. Those latter cases were all events held in addition to rounds which took place in those countries, while F1 is not racing in Bahrain at all this year as it was considered too unsafe due to the proximity to the conflict in Iran. Precisely because of that, the distance between the event and the country it was named after was much greater than those earlier cases, being some 6,000 kilometres.

So instead of the Bahrain International Circuit holding its 23rd race, the Sepang International Circuit held its 20th. In theory Bahrain will hold the first round on the 2027 F1 calendar, but watch this space.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Verstappen’s success vindicated Red Bull’s decision to build their own power unit, in conjunction with Ford. The latter last contributed to a grand prix victory in 2003, when Giancarlo Fisichella won the Brazilian Grand Prix for Jordan (now Aston Martin) powered by a Ford-Cosworth RS1.

The same power units ended Mercedes’ monopoly on pole positions this year. After 15 consecutive Mercedes-powered poles, Verstappen claimed the first for a (partly) Ford-badged engine since Rubens Barrichello put his Stewart at the front of the field for the 1999 French Grand Prix at Magny-Cours.

However a substantial amount of credit must also go to Red Bull, who had already committed to building their own power units before teaming up with Ford. Although they previously ran their Honda-designed units successfully, they deserve to be regarded as a new engine constructor in their own right, and those don’t appear very often.

If we accept this was the first victory for a new engine built by a new constructor, when was the last time this happened? Red Bull’s other wins since 2022 have been credited to ‘Red Bull Powertrains’ and Honda RBPT but all involved the same Honda-derived power units.

Other new names which appeared on the winners lists in previous years were often due to branding exercises. Red Bull previously won races with Renault engines badged as TAG Heuer. Engines produced by Honda and Porsche won races labelled as Mugen-Honda and TAG-Porsche respectively.

Using a strict definition, avoiding all rebranded engines and those related to previous designs by constructors who had already won races, Red Bull-Ford’s win is the first for a new F1 engine constructor since BMW in 1982. That win came courtesy of Brabham’s Nelson Piquet in the Canadian Grand Prix. In an extremely unusual result, his team mate Riccardo Patrese finished that race in second place powered by a different engine: his Brabham was powered by Ford.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

The others manufactures on the grid today are either yet to win (Audi) or scored their first wins long ago: Ferrari in 1951, Mercedes in 1954 and Honda in 1965.

A week ago, George Russell grabbed the eighth win of his career, in Baku. Verstappen served notice of Red Bull’s potential there, chasing his rival across the line, the pair separated by just 0.196 seconds. This was the closest finish to a grand prix since the rigged conclusion to the 2002 United States Grand Prix, where Schumacher attempted to contrive a ‘dead heat’ with team mate Barrichello, but instead was beaten to the line by 0.011s.

Finally, Fernando Alonso took advantage of the conditions in Sepang to claim Aston Martin’s best finish of the season with eighth place. Those four points leave his team just five shy of Williams.

Over to you

Have you spotted any other interesting stats and facts from the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia or Azerbaijan Grand Prix? Share them in the comments.

Sports.title: “That was a big mess”: How all 22 drivers saw F1’s formation lap fiasco in Sepang | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Confusion reigned when Formula 1 drivers headed out to begin yesterday’s grand prix.

A software glitch struck much of the grid, causing some cars to slow to a crawl and others to stop entirely. Some power units sprang back into life while others stubbornly refused to work again.

Eventually race control abandoned the attempt to start the race and summoned the field back into the pits so the FIA could issue a software update. The process took the best part of an hour.

The problem was widespread throughout the field and affected drivers in different ways. Here’s how several of them experienced the fault.

1st: Max Verstappen

Verstappen’s car almost came to a stop at the front of the field. However a switch change on his steering wheel solved the problem for him.

Verstappen Verstappen slows at turn 10

Well, this is fucked. I can’t accelerate. Lambiase OK, stand by. Verstappen Why doesn’t it work? Lambiase Stand by. Verstappen It’s not working, guys. Lambiase Yep stand by Max, we’re looking. Let’s have fail one fail please, Max. Fail one fail.

The car accelerates away Lambiase Looks like maybe Lewis has a similar problem to you. He’s still struggling between turn 11 and turn 12.

Expecting the start to go ahead, Verstappen was unhappy that the side of the grid he was due to start from was wetter than the opposite side.

I don’t think this is related to individual engine issues here Max, I think there’s some kind of relation. So Hamilton has got going. You have both Cadillacs, both Haas, both Audis crawling ahead of you, as is Lindblad.

Verstappen laughed when he saw several cars stuck on the back straight due to the software problem. However he was less amused to spot a nail in his tyre when he returned to the pits.

2nd: Lewis Hamilton

The fault struck Hamilton’s car at the same time as Verstappen’s. As a result, he appeared not to realise the Red Bull driver was suffering from the same problem as him. Ferrari had more difficulty finding a solution for Hamilton.

Hamilton I’ve lost power. Santi We are checking. Hamilton Something’s happened, I’ve got no… I’m just ticking over in first gear. Santi Coming back to you. Hamilton Throttle’s not doing anything. Sports.title: Fan’s video shows moment software glitch slowed F1 cars to a crawl on formation lap | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1’s 2026 engine regulations faced fresh criticism yesterday following the farcical start to the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

The race, which had already been delayed by rain, was postponed by almost an hour more after a software problem struck cars during the formation lap.

Pole-winner Max Verstappen and several drivers behind him slowed to a crawl as their power units would not allow them to accelerate. The cause was a software parameter set by the FIA, which required the governing body to apply new settings to the cars.

Verstappen said he had as much power as he did when the drivers raced in Lego cars in a promotional event.

“It was like the Lego race,” he said. “Same speed. It was insane, it’s the Lego power.

“At some point we were five-wide on the straight because we couldn’t understand what was going on. Then we did a lap and then I see eight other cars crawling still.

“That’s not what you want, right, for the sport.”

The FIA said the cars’ loss of power was due to “an unprecedented combination of low engine speed, low-grip conditions, wet-weather energy management settings and the Sepang circuit’s sector configuration.”

Sports.title: Mercedes ‘don’t know if upgrade made us faster or slower’ – Antonelli | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The long-awaited upgrade package Mercedes introduced last weekend may have made them less competitive, Andrea Kimi Antonelli has admitted.

Antonelli led the opening stages of yesterday’s race ahead of team mate George Russell . However both were overtaken by Max Verstappen , who went on to win the race.

Mercedes originally planned to introduce their new parts for the W17 at this weekend’s race in Singapore. They brought the upgrade forward after Formula 1 added last weekend’s round in Malaysia to replace the cancelled event in Bahrain.

However the unusually abrasive track surface at the Sepang International Circuit complicated the team’s efforts to understand the performance of its upgraded car. Antonelli qualified half a second slower than Verstappen.

He said the performance of the upgrade is “the question we need to answer because we don’t really know if it made us go faster or worse.”

However he pointed out the team has been less competitive at tracks which share some traits with Sepang. “It’s fair to say that this season, whenever we went on really old Tarmac, we’ve struggled. For example, in Zandvoort, McLaren was much quicker than us, especially on the older Tarmac.

“So I think maybe it’s just a fact that the Tarmac is very old and that for the tyres it’s very, very hard, and maybe we just struggle on this kind of Tarmac.

“But, of course, the track and the Tarmac made our life difficult in understanding whether it made us improve or not.”

The championship leader expects the team will have some answers before this weekend’s race. “I’m sure the team – they have a lot of data, especially after this weekend – and I’m sure for Singapore we will come with a much, much better view on the package and hopefully we can extract the full potential out of it.”

Sports.title: Spotlight: ‘Who decided these rules were best for F1?’ asks Sainz | Brief
Sports.content:
The farcical scenes during yesterday’s formation laps which delayed the start of the race by almost an hour prompted criticism from several drivers.

Grand Prix Drivers Association director Carlos Sainz Jnr was among those questioning why Formula 1 committed itself years ago to rules which have proved so problematic.

“[F1] needs to have a hard look at themselves and see how we ended up in this situation,” he said after the race. “It is clear the regs are extremely complicated for the drivers, for the teams, for the power units, for the manufacturers. It is too complicated.

“Again, my only question mark is who five years ago decided that this was the direction to go?”

F1 confirmed its current engine regulations in 2022, though the majority of the changes were substantially agreed before then. Mohammed Ben Sulayem became FIA president in December 2021.

Sainz’s father, multiple world rally champion Carlos Sainz, considered opposing Ben Sulayem in last year’s election, but chose not to. Ben Sulayem won re-election and subsequently moved to end presidency term limits, allowing him to serve as president as long as he likes.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Pushes Floyd Mayweather for Professional Fight
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia has set his sights on Floyd Mayweather for a fully sanctioned professional bout, insisting the retired legend reached out to him first. Ryan shut down any talk of an exhibition, making it clear he only wants a clash if Mayweather puts his 50-0 record on the line.

The Ring’s post on X detailing the challenge blew up instantly. Fans are definitely curious, though convincing Mayweather to risk his pristine ledger just before his 50th birthday is a massive hurdle.

“Okay Floyd let’s see how much you love that ‘0,’” Ryan posted on X. “And no I wouldn’t do an exhibition I want his 0 on the fucking line. How much does he actually think he got left. I’m ready Floyd, remember you made this call. I’m just returning the favor. Offer is on the table. Accept or not, if not I move foward as I have been.”

Ryan’s public callout does not mean Floyd agreed to step into a real ring. Nothing is signed, and no date exists.

Mayweather turns 50 this February. He has not fought professionally since beating Conor McGregor in 2017, and his last appearances against elite pugilists were his 2015 victories over Manny Pacquiao and Andre Berto.

Stepping into a real fight against a prime competitor after nearly a decade away is an entirely different reality. Mayweather still possesses unmatched ring IQ, yet reflex speed fades with time. Garcia’s explosive hand speed and blistering left hook could punish sluggish reactions if Floyd struggles to keep his legs under him as the rounds tick by. A decision win for Ryan seems likely, with a late stoppage well within reach if Mayweather cannot dodge incoming combinations.

Recent reports detailing Floyd’s financial headaches suggest a monster check would tempt him. Protecting that flawless record remains his primary concern. An exhibition gives him a lucrative payday with zero official consequences, but Garcia refuses to entertain that route.

Ryan also risks major blowback for targeting a man nearing 50. Floyd’s legendary status guarantees huge box office numbers, yet defeating an aged icon proves very little against the current elite at welterweight. Going after this spectacle suggests Ryan is chasing pure dollar signs, even if it hands him the historic bragging right of tarnishing Mayweather’s undefeated legacy.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Targets Vito Mielnicki Against Xander Zayas
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn wants Vito Mielnicki Jr. to face Xander Zayas in New York next summer, with both fighters taking another bout first under his preferred plan.

Vito beat Ammo Williams in his last fight, while Xander lost to Jaron Ennis. If Zayas decides against taking a fight first, he’ll be coming straight off that defeat to face Mielnicki.

“I want him to fight Xander Zayas. It’s a massive fight for New York,” Hearn said to iFL TV. “We’re promoting Xander Zayas’s next fight in February, it looks like. It won’t be that fight, but I’d like to see him come back and then fight Vito. Vito will have a fight as well around the same time, and then those two fight in the summer.”

Hearn favors that route, yet no deal exists for a bout between Mielnicki and Zayas. His proposal for February grants Xander a chance to get back in the ring before taking on Vito, even if the date and opponent stay unconfirmed.

The choice is more important to Zayas than Mielnicki. Vito comes into his next fight riding the win over Ammo Williams. Xander must prove his response after the loss to Ennis, so an interim contest allows him to test adjustments prior to taking on a rival with momentum.

Stepping directly into the ring with Mielnicki makes the comeback far tougher. Vito has every incentive to pursue the fight while the Williams victory remains fresh, as a win over Zayas hands him another prominent scalp to elevate his standing.

Hearn aiming for New York establishes a sharp promotional focus for the contest. Instead of feeding either fighter back to Ennis immediately, he seeks to pit them against one another so the victor earns a clear path back to the division’s biggest stages.

Locking down their upcoming bouts comes first. Hearn intends to get both fighters into the ring around February, securing ample preparation time for a summer clash rather than letting the plan fade away.

Sports.title: Dana White Spends Hours Working on Shakur Stevenson Fight
Sports.content:
Dana White is actively attempting to lock down Shakur Stevenson’s next bout, confirming on October 6 that he spent several hours that afternoon working on fight logistics. White’s brief update provides concrete evidence of ongoing negotiations behind the scenes, though an opponent, venue, and official date remain unconfirmed.

“Yeah, we’re working on the Shakur fight right now. Literally today, a couple hours of my day today was spent on Shakur,” White said during his post-Contender Series press conference.

Reporters pressed White for details, specifically referencing his prior remarks that Stevenson would return to action before the close of the year. White declined to reaffirm that original timeline, and he chose not to disclose which specific opponent he is targeting for the promotional launch.

That leaves the next announcement particularly important. Time spent discussing a fight is encouraging, but Shakur needs an agreement that gets him back in the ring.

Shakur pointed to money as the primary roadblock stalling bouts with Gary Antuanne Russell and Raymond Muratalla. Stevenson posted publicly on X claiming both fighters demanded three million dollars apiece to step in the ring with him, urging Zuffa Boxing to pay the price.

The figures nevertheless help explain why choosing an opponent and securing one can be very different tasks. Shakur wants meaningful fights, while the other side has its own price for accepting a difficult matchup.

White did not say whether he was working on a fight with Russell, Muratalla, or someone else. He gave no indication that a deal was close or an announcement was coming soon.

Shakur and Devin Haney have been going back and forth on X over weight. Haney has offered to come down to 145 pounds without a rehydration clause. Shakur has repeatedly asked for 144, along with a 10-pound limit on how much Haney can regain after the weigh-in.

Whether 145 is low enough for Shakur remains unclear. He is asking Haney to make two concessions: fight below the welterweight limit and restrict his weight gain afterward by 10 pounds. Haney’s offer brings them closer on the catchweight, but the rehydration clause remains a point of disagreement.

Sports.title: Emanuel Navarrete Targets Three Belts Against O’Shaquie Foster
Sports.content:
Naoya Inoue has what most world champions are still chasing: all four major belts in his division. Emanuel Navarrete can move a step closer to that position on October 24, when he faces O’Shaquie Foster in a three-belt super featherweight unification fight in San Antonio.

That gives boxing’s title picture something more useful than another list of belt holders. The Navarrete–Foster winner will leave with the IBF, WBO and WBC championships, reducing the number of separate champions at 130 pounds and putting an undisputed fight within reach. Top Rank has confirmed those three titles will be at stake.

Inoue, 33-0 with 27 knockouts, holds the WBA, WBC, IBF and WBO titles at super bantamweight. He retained the collection by defeating Junto Nakatani in May. His position gives challengers a clear target: they must beat him to take any of the four major championships at 122 pounds.

Elsewhere, winning a world title can leave a fighter with considerable unfinished business. Holding two belts makes someone a unified champion. Holding all four makes him undisputed. Adding the IBO championship does not replace a missing WBA, WBC, IBF or WBO belt.

Navarrete’s fight with Foster offers a practical example of that difference. Navarrete, 40-2-1 with 33 knockouts, brings the IBF and WBO titles. Foster brings the WBC belt. Even with victory, either man would still need the WBA championship to complete the set.

The benefit for supporters is a stronger answer to who leads the division. Separate champions can build separate careers, each defending a belt without facing the other titleholders. Unification forces at least two of those claims to be tested against each other.

Collecting belts should lead to better fights. Inoue has already completed that process at super bantamweight. Navarrete and Foster are taking another step toward it, and their October 24 meeting gives fans a fight that can settle something beyond another successful title defense.

Sports.title: Conor Wallace Questions Referee After Ben Whittaker Loss
Sports.content:
Conor Wallace believes the referee made it harder for him to finish Ben Whittaker last Saturday, allowing him to hold while hurt and declining to count falls that Wallace felt deserved knockdowns.

The late trouble also gives Eddie Hearn a reason to think carefully about a rematch. Neither Hearn nor Whittaker has committed to facing Wallace again, and the promoter has mentioned other possible opponents.

“I do definitely feel like the referee didn’t do me any favors,” Wallace told talkSPORT’s White and Jordan show on Tuesday morning. “I definitely feel like one or possibly two of them should have been knockdowns, and he was holding on for dear life. “You need to be given a chance to get going, and I was trying to get the action going. Yes, I did smother myself a little bit. Maybe I was trying too hard to put him away. I should have shortened those shots when I look back at it, but hindsight is a wonderful thing.”

Wallace puts his complaint at one or possibly two knockdowns. There is a case for examining all three falls, along with Whittaker’s repeated holding. Counting those falls and deducting points could have changed the result. Enforcing the rules on holding could also have forced Whittaker to keep fighting when he was struggling to survive.

Wallace accepts that he contributed to the missed opportunity by crowding his punches. Shorter shots and a little more room could make him harder to contain if he gets Whittaker hurt again.

He also wants to start faster, having conceded the early rounds. That requires care against Whittaker’s counter right, but Wallace now has twelve rounds of experience against him and knows he can cause trouble late.

Hearn has talked about Whittaker as a generational talent. Putting him straight back in with someone who came close to stopping him would put that description to a serious test. Wallace may have his number, particularly if he improves his opening rounds and finishes more patiently.

Choosing another opponent would be understandable from Hearn’s side. Whittaker already has his IBF mandatory position, and another Wallace fight brings considerable risk. Wallace’s confidence alone will not get the rematch made; Hearn and Whittaker still have to decide whether they want to take that chance.

Sports.title: Osleys Iglesias Welcomes Christian Mbilli Unification Despite Shared Trainer
Sports.content:
Osleys Iglesias is willing to fight Christian Mbilli even if Marc Ramsey chooses the other corner, removing a potential obstacle to a super middleweight unification should both champions win their upcoming defenses.

The two fighters share Ramsey, but Iglesias will not allow that arrangement to prevent him from facing the WBC champion.

“Whoever’s in my corner is in my corner, but there are no excuses with me,” Iglesias told The Ring.

Iglesias defends his IBF title against Oliver Zaren this Thursday, October 8, in Quebec City on DAZN. Mbilli is scheduled to defend against Canelo Alvarez on October 31 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Iglesias views that fight as a 50-50 contest.

If both retain their titles, promoter Camille Estephan would have two champions at 168 pounds and an opportunity to arrange a unification. Iglesias has made clear that sharing a trainer would not be his reason for declining it.

The bigger obstacle could be business. If Mbilli beats Canelo, his next fight could attract considerably more attention. Matching him immediately against a dangerous puncher from the same stable would risk that opportunity.

Iglesias would have more to gain in recognition. Beating the man who had just defeated Canelo could transform his career, while Mbilli might have better-paying options. Having both champions under one promoter makes negotiations easier, but it does not guarantee Estephan wants the matchup.

Ramsey would also have a choice to make. If he stayed with Mbilli, his knowledge of Iglesias’s habits could help with preparation, although Iglesias only began working with him less than three months ago.

Inside the ring, Mbilli’s pressure could give Iglesias the exchanges he wants. Coming forward against a powerful southpaw creates opportunities for straight left hands and short counters.

That danger runs both ways. Iglesias would need to land enough to interrupt Mbilli’s attacks. If Mbilli takes his punches and keeps forcing exchanges, Iglesias would have to maintain his effectiveness through a demanding twelve rounds.

Iglesias must beat Zaren first. Beyond Thursday, his willingness puts the question to his promoter: would Eye of the Tiger match its champions if Mbilli returns from Riyadh with a victory over Canelo?

Sports.title: Floyd Schofield Questions Lucas Bahdi’s Boxing Skills
Sports.content:
Floyd Schofield believes Lucas Bahdi is counting on one big punch to beat him this Saturday in Chicago, questioning whether the Canadian has the skills to win their vacant lightweight title fight any other way.

Schofield sees Bahdi’s knockout of Ashton Sylve as the approach he will try again: absorb punches, remain patient, and wait for Schofield to jump into something.

“I just think that they’re hoping I just jump in and he gets the same moment he had with Ashton,” Schofield said to Chris Mannix ahead of Saturday’s fight. “I would find it hard to believe that he thinks he’s a more skillful fighter than me or a better fighter than me. If so, then he’s crazy.”

Schofield described Bahdi’s patience and power as his best attributes, pointing out that Sylve hit him clean for six rounds without discouraging him. That is also the reason Schofield cannot afford to become careless if he builds an early lead.

Bahdi does not need to win every exchange to remain dangerous. Schofield could be landing the cleaner punches and controlling the fight, then give away everything by rushing forward with his head exposed. The temptation to force a stoppage could become Bahdi’s best opportunity.

Schofield also questioned Bahdi’s footwork and defense, saying he gets hit frequently and trips over his feet. Although Bahdi has changed trainers, Schofield doubts those habits can be corrected quickly at 31.

His father, Floyd Schofield Sr., believes his son has improved his distance control during camp and is picking his punches more carefully rather than jumping in.

That would be a useful change against Bahdi, but it has to last beyond the opening rounds. Schofield’s speed can help him score without staying in punching range. If he gets drawn into proving he can hurt Bahdi with every attack, he would be taking the very risk he believes the Canadian needs him to take.

Sports.title: Jaime Munguia Pursues Unranked Opponent Before Mandatory Defense
Sports.content:
Bektemir Melikuziev wants Jaime Munguia to defend his WBA super middleweight title against him, while the champion’s team reportedly negotiates a step-aside to squeeze in a fight with Keiber Gonzalez first.

That proposed opponent makes Bektemir’s frustration understandable. Gonzalez isn’t in the WBA’s published September top 15 at 168 pounds. Melikuziev is No. 1, yet he’s the fighter being asked to wait.

“The purse is not important, I am ready to fight for free. But please stop disrespecting me and the rules of the game!” Melikuziev wrote on Instagram. “Jaime Munguia, I was the mandatory for the title before you fought for it. You became the champion, respect me just like I would respect you or any other boxer if I was the champion.”

ESPN boxing reporter Salvador “Chava” Rodríguez reported on Instagram that Munguia’s team continues negotiating a step-aside with Melikuziev. According to Rodríguez, the negotiation window runs until October 21, with the aim of allowing Munguia to face Gonzalez before fulfilling his mandatory obligation.

Bektemir’s willingness to fight for free is an expression of how badly he wants the opportunity. It doesn’t establish that he has rejected every possible offer, but his message gives Munguia’s team little reason to assume money will settle this.

From Munguia’s side, Gonzalez looks like an easier defense before a more demanding fight. That may suit the champion, but it leaves Melikuziev waiting for a shot he had already earned before Munguia won the belt.

Even if Bektemir accepts payment to wait, that wouldn’t explain what Gonzalez has done to deserve the opportunity. The WBA would still have to justify approving an opponent outside its published top 15 while its leading challenger sits out.

Munguia has the title now. The responsibility that comes with it is facing the challenger who earned his turn. Asking Bektemir to watch Gonzalez get the next opportunity is a difficult sell, especially when Bektemir is publicly demanding the fight.

Ghana News.title: Ghana begins review of 1999 National Land Policy, targets new framework by 2027
Ghana News.content:
Ghana has begun a comprehensive review of its 1999 National Land Policy as the government seeks to align land governance with emerging economic, social, environmental and technological demands.

The review is being undertaken by the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources in collaboration with the Lands Commission and the Office of the Administrator of Stool Lands (OASL).

The process commenced with a two-day inception workshop addressed by Deputy Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Yusif Sulemana.

Speaking on behalf of the Sector Minister, Mr Sulemana said the 1999 policy had provided an important foundation for land administration reforms, including the enactment of the Land Act, 2020 (Act 1036), which consolidated about 13 separate land laws into a single legal framework.

He, however, noted that significant challenges continued to affect land administration, including delays in service delivery, land and boundary disputes, encroachment on public lands, multiple sales of land, tenure insecurity and competing demands for land.

Mr Sulemana said rapid population growth, urbanisation, economic transformation and technological advancement, together with the growing effects of climate change, had created circumstances that were not fully anticipated when the existing policy was developed.

“The 1999 National Land Policy has served the country well, but the realities of today require us to take a fresh look at our land governance framework,” he said.

He described the review as an important government priority and disclosed that the proposed policy would receive Cabinet-level consideration as part of efforts to strengthen land governance and improve the management of Ghana’s land resources.

The new National Land Policy is expected to be completed and submitted to Cabinet for consideration and approval by the end of 2027.

Ghana News.title: Tiptoe Lane’s tech takeover: The story behind Ghana’s booming informal phone market
Ghana News.content:
Accra's Tiptoe Lane has traded photographs, travel documents and now phones, but the latest transformation is turning the once-familiar street behind the Kwame Nkrumah Circle into a crowded marketplace where thousands of people make a living from technology.

Located in the Ayawaso Central Municipality of the Greater Accra Region, the narrow stretch around the Kwame Nkrumah Circle is now lined with phone dealers, accessory sellers and repair shops, drawing traders, technicians, students and customers from across Ghana.

But it was not always this way.

For Paul Kwesi Boateng of Boateng Phones and Accessories, the transformation is something he has lived through for over twenty years.

“When I first started selling phones at Tiptoe Lane, people were living in the very space where my shop now stands. As the phone business began to boom, the occupants of this house eventually rented the space to me, and I now pay for the space every year,” he said.

Twenty years later, Boateng remains in the trade, but he says the market he helped build is becoming increasingly difficult for Ghanaian traders as foreign nationals take a larger share of the business.

“For every ten shops here, eight are owned by foreigners, creating a major challenge for Ghanaian phone dealers. We welcomed them into the market, but now they are trying to take over businesses from the indigenes.”

His concern points to one of the tensions now shaping Tiptoe Lane: a market that created opportunities for local traders is attracting more competition as its reputation as a phone market grows.

But the story of Tiptoe Lane did not begin with phones.

Less than 300 metres long and stretching off Kwame Nkrumah Avenue, the lane has reinvented itself repeatedly over more than five decades, reflecting the changing aspirations, struggles and hustle of urban Ghana.

In the post-independence years, Tiptoe Lane earned its early fame through photography and nightclub businesses.

Speaking to a long-serving employee of the Modern Photo Company Limited, Acquah revealed that the company has been in existence since 1955.

According to Mr Acquah, Modern Photo Company, together with smaller studios, turned the lane into a destination for portraiture. Ghanaians dressed in their Sunday best would carefully “tiptoe” into the studios to avoid dust, keeping their clothes and shoes clean for family portraits, passport photographs and graduation pictures.

The studios processed film and hand-tinted prints, becoming social archives for families and a marker of middle-class life. The lane was also frequented by wedding parties, travelling businessmen needing visa photographs and students documenting important milestones.

By the late 1980s and 1990s, however, the character of Tiptoe Lane began to change.

Mr Acquah further explained that as television spread and demand for traditional photography shifted, the Akan Drama theatre group and other performance troupes became part of the area's entertainment scene, with the Akan Drama group operating from a nightclub known as Apollo Theatre.

“Actors, scriptwriters and costumers moved through the cramped spaces, while posters for Concert Party shows covered the walls. The lane became part of an informal creative network feeding the National Theatre, GTV and Ghana’s emerging video-film industry,” he added.

Photo Credit: David Andoh - Some Actors from the Akan Drama group

The theatre era was followed by another chapter in the lane’s social life, as nightclubs and nightlife businesses became part of its changing identity, giving the area a different rhythm before another economic transformation took hold.

Among the long-standing businesses that have also shaped Tiptoe Lane’s commercial identity is Fredie’s Corner, which continues to deal in mobile phones, accessories and related products. Odo Rice, another longstanding presence, continues to serve prepared food to traders, workers and customers who spend their day around the busy lane. The defunct Ebony Restaurant was also once part of the businesses that gave the area its character.

By the late 1990s and early 2000s, Tiptoe Lane had become increasingly associated with the pursuit of opportunities abroad.

Economic hardship, coupled with the fallout from the “Ghana Must Go” period and tighter visa restrictions, saw the area gain notoriety as a hotspot for “connection men” and document facilitators.

Internet cafés, typing pools and photography studios produced passport photographs, bank statements, invitation letters and visa forms, some legitimate, many not.

It became the lane’s most controversial period. Police raids were common, while the area developed a reputation for hustle, risk and quick adaptation. Yet the digital skills and document literacy developed during that period would later become useful as the lane reinvented itself once again.

Then came the mobile phone boom.

From around 2005, the Global System for Mobile (GSM) revolution began changing Tiptoe Lane again. As Nokia and Motorola, and later Tecno and Infinix, spread across Ghana, the lane’s small shops increasingly shifted towards mobile phones, chargers, accessories and repairs.

Today, the area is described by experts as one of Accra’s densest mobile technology micro-markets, with new and used smartphones packed into glass cabinets, repairers working in tiny spaces and accessories spilling through the narrow trading environment.

General Secretary of the Mobile Phone and Accessories Dealers Association (MPADA), Eric Asante, says traders eventually realised they had to organise themselves as their numbers increased.

He recalls that phone sellers initially operated along the roads before deciding to gather in one place so customers could easily find them.

That decision helped turn scattered roadside trading into the market that exists today.

The growth also attracted traders from outside Ghana.

Eric says foreign traders, including Nigerians, eventually joined the market as its commercial opportunities became more obvious.

“For some foreigners, when they come, and they see that they have enough to acquire some shops, then they go, prepare adequately and come back, and also join us, and that’s how we became more. So plenty of the foreigners from other places too invaded.”

For him, the expansion has now become a source of concern.

“But now the foreigners are taking the market from us. As executives, we have put measures in place, but it is not going to be easy because they are a lot now. We call on the government to help us regulate how these foreigners operate here, and they should also establish a proper layout for us to help the market become one of the world’s biggest phone hubs”

Director of Communications at Franco Trading Enterprise, Ernest Adu Kumi, has another explanation for why the area became attractive to businesses.

He says the location, close to Circle’s transport links and other businesses, made it commercially attractive.

“The first shop for Franco was established at Adabraka; that is where the headquarters is. So, like any other business, you want to expand it. So that you can serve more people, employ more people, and also make more revenue.”

“And you know, Tiptoe Lane is just close to Circle, and we have transport stations and other companies around, and a telecom company also there. So, it makes it easy; ideally, it makes business sense for you to have something like that.”

But Adu Kumi says the availability of affordable phones was what really accelerated the market’s growth.

“Franco is one of the companies that made the sale of mobile phones attractive. People would go into our shops, buy it at a cheaper cost, then come to the roadside and sell for profit. That was the genesis.”

Once the business began generating returns, he says, others followed.

“And it starts from one. If one starts making a profit, other people see, they have friends, they have relatives, and it’s a lucrative business. So, why don’t we also get ourselves involved?”

“And gradually, gradually, it started growing, and now it’s creating a lot of opportunities for the young ones.”

Those opportunities extend beyond the people directly selling phones. The growth of the market has created demand for retailers, wholesalers, repairers, importers, parts sellers and apprentices, creating different entry points into work, particularly for young people.

That gradual growth has created more than a phone market. It has produced an informal chain of businesses that depend on one another.

Technology enthusiast and music producer Kobby Spiky Nkrumah describes it as the natural evolution of an informal economy.

“I think just as every other informal market in Africa, it doesn’t start; there’s no plan. You know, it’s everyone just trying to survive.”

Businesses, he says, simply began clustering around the opportunities available.

“People realised that it was a busy hub, and people began to cluster, you know, so one person starts it, another person joins in and then through clustering, it became what it is right now.”

The clustering created its own ecosystem.

“If there are repairers, there’ll be sellers. If there are parts sellers, people selling parts, there’ll be those who are importing their parts. And if some are importing their parts, there’ll be those who are wholesaling. And then if there’s wholesaling, there’ll be retail. And then if there’s retail, there’ll definitely be customers.”

The employment potential is therefore not limited to the shops visible along the lane. As the market expands, the network around it can support more technicians, apprentices, traders, importers, distributors and other service providers.

For Kobby, however, the market’s next challenge is also about making the skills developed there more recognised. He believes certification could improve trust between technicians and customers.

“We need to create sort of like a proper certification model for these technicians, because once the people are good, once they are certified, people trust them. And then you legitimise their hustle in a place like Tiptoe Lane.”

He sees an even bigger opportunity in refurbishing old devices and recycling electronic waste, potentially creating another layer of businesses around phones and computers.

For young people, that ecosystem has become a way into work.

Dennison, a student who entered the business immediately after Senior High School, is now an employee at Stranger Phones, and says he joined the trade to fend for himself before continuing his education.

Several other students spoken to at the market gave similar reasons, saying the work helps them cater for themselves and raise money towards school fees as they prepare to further their education.

For Richmond Hammond, a laptop repairer, the opportunity came through learning a technical skill.

After completing school, he learnt phone and laptop repairs from a master at Tiptoe Lane. He has since completed his apprenticeship and opened his own shop.

But Richmond says the physical environment is becoming a worry.

“My greatest fear and worry are that the market is too enclosed, and I fear what could happen if a fire breaks out. We’re pleading with the government and the Ghana National Fire Service to provide fire extinguishers and find ways to expand or better organise the space for us,” he pleaded.

But the growth of Tiptoe Lane is also changing the physical character of the area beyond the shops themselves.

As demand for commercial space rises, some residential facilities are being converted into shops. That creates another question for the future of the market: whether continued commercial expansion will gradually affect residents, increase congestion and change the residential character of the neighbourhood.

The question is particularly relevant as the area around Circle continues to attract businesses, technology, and retailers.

The question, therefore, is no longer simply how far Tiptoe Lane’s phone trade can grow, but how that growth can be managed without pushing out the people and communities around it.

That is perhaps the clearest measure of how far Tiptoe Lane has travelled.

A street once associated with photography and theatre became a centre for nightlife and travel services before the mobile phone transformed its fortunes again.

Now, it is a place where a trader has spent more than two decades building a phone business, where students work towards paying their school fees, where apprentices become technicians and where businesses have grown around one another.

But the market now faces a new test.

Local traders want protection from what they describe as growing foreign competition. Repairers want safer and more spacious working conditions. Industry players want certification and greater organisation. Residents may also have to contend with the consequences of a commercial market expanding into spaces that were once homes.

The challenge for authorities will be to provide that structure without suffocating the informal enterprise that created the market in the first place.

Because Tiptoe Lane did not become a tech hub through a grand plan.

It grew through opportunity, one business, one worker and one new chapter at a time.

And, as Kobby Spiky puts it, “one person starts it, another person joins in.”

Ghana News.title: Abanga vows to use social media to counter NDC messaging ahead of 2028 elections
Ghana News.content:
Newly elected NPP National Youth Organiser, Abanga Fusani Yakubu, has vowed to use social media and grassroots mobilisation to counter what he describes as the NDC’s lies and propaganda ahead of the 2028 elections.

Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Tuesday, Mr Abanga said the NPP must intensify its presence both online and across the country to win young voters for Dr Mahamudu Bawumia.

He acknowledged that his target of securing four million youth votes for Dr Bawumia may appear ambitious but insisted it can be achieved through hard work, sacrifice and effective mobilisation.

“It is. You see, it requires hard work. It requires sacrifice. It requires getting the right people on the ground to get the job done,” he said.

Mr Abanga said he intends to personally lead the mobilisation rather than operate from the party’s headquarters.

“I’ll be joining them in their various regions and constituencies very soon. So we preach the gospel of Dr Mahamud Bawumia. It’s the only solution for this country,” he said.

He also accused the NDC of using social media to undermine the achievements of the previous NPP administration.

“They use social media to sway away from the good policies and initiatives of ex-President Akufo-Addo and Dr Mahamudu Bawumia did for this country by propagating lies and fake propaganda,” he said.

Mr Abanga said the NPP must respond more aggressively in the digital space.

“And I think this time round, we have to get to the grounds, make good use of social media, let them know that the NDC is not an option,” he said.

He cited fuel prices and the government’s 24-hour economy policy as issues the NPP should use to challenge the NDC’s record.

“They promise lies,” he said.

Mr Abanga also criticised the government over cocoa prices, arguing that farmers are now receiving less than they were previously promised.

“My father is a go-go farmer. My mom is a cocoa farmer,” he said.

He claimed cocoa was previously being bought at GH¢3,100 under Dr Bawumia but is now being bought at GH¢2,000.

“They said they were going to buy cocoa at GH¢6000. They should not even mention anything about global prices. I don’t want to hear that, but they knew there was something called global prices whilst they made those promises,” he said.

Mr Abanga said his role as National Youth Organiser requires him to lead the mobilisation of young people ahead of 2028.

“It’s the government that we are feeling today. We are suffering, and being a youth and representing my party as a national youth commander, I must take charge, mobilise the youth, so we can prosecute an effective campaign, so Dr Bawumia wins the 2028 election to save this country,” he said.

Ghana News.title: Okai Mintah seeks Sabah Zita Benson’s support for NDC National Youth Organiser bid
Ghana News.content:
NDC activist Okai Mintah has formally informed Ghana’s High Commissioner to the United Kingdom, H.E. Sabah Zita Benson, of his intention to contest the position of National Youth Organiser of the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC).

Mr Mintah disclosed this in a Facebook post following a meeting with the High Commissioner at her residence in London, where he said they discussed matters of mutual interest and the continued progress of the NDC.

According to him, he used the opportunity to share his intention to seek the National Youth Organiser position and asked for the High Commissioner’s “blessings and support” as he pursues the bid.

Mr Mintah expressed appreciation to H.E. Sabah Zita Benson for hosting him and for the warm reception during the meeting.

He has been promoting his campaign under the slogan “Get MINTED”, alongside the hashtags #WithImmediateEffect and #GreenArmy.

Ghana News.title: Okai Mintah vows to strengthen NDC campaign machinery ahead of 2028
Ghana News.content:
An aspirant for the National Youth Organiser position of the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC), Okai Mintah, has pledged to strengthen and adequately resource the party’s mobilisation structures ahead of the 2028 general elections.

Mr Mintah said he was committed to leading efforts to build a stronger campaign machinery, drawing on the structures used by the party in the 2024 elections.

In a post on Facebook, he said his objective would be to “upgrade and better fund” the existing mobilisation machinery as part of efforts towards the party’s 2028 campaign.

“I am committed to leading our mobilization efforts to ensure our campaign machinery is unmatched. We will upgrade and better fund the same machinery used in 2024 to secure our victory in 2028,” he said.

Mr Mintah’s message forms part of his campaign for the position of National Youth Organiser, where he is presenting mobilisation and campaign organisation as key priorities ahead of the next general election.

Ghana News.title: Mother of four and Jasikan teacher among new Telecel M’ahitti Promo winners
Ghana News.content:
Since its launch in June this year, the Telecel M’ahitti Promo has brought economic hope to thousands of people across Ghana. More than GH¢2 million has been awarded through one GH¢1 million monthly prize, as well as daily and weekly prizes

In the final week of September, Anita Addo, a mother of four, Kumasi-based entrepreneur and Telecel customer of just over a year, received her weekly prize.

After the M’ahitti Promo launched, she began receiving SMS messages about it and eventually opted in, although she had little expectation of winning.

When she received the call announcing her win, she initially dismissed it. Unsure whether it was genuine, she visited a nearby Telecel office, where the Executive Head confirmed that she was indeed a winner.

The GHC 20,000 prize has come at an important time for her family, as the new school year has just begun. Her eldest child recently gained admission to university, and she also needs to pay fees and provide school supplies for her other children.

“This is an answer to my prayers. I had no idea how I was going to pay the fees and provide all their other school necessities. I am very grateful to Telecel, and I encourage everyone to participate in its promotions because they are genuine,” she said.

In the Oti Region, Leslie Johnson Adams, a Jasikan-based teacher and Telecel customer of about 10 years, could not hide his joy when he received GH¢20,000 in his Telecel Cash wallet.

Like many weekly winners, he was initially in disbelief, as he had never won anything of this kind.

“It felt as though I was dreaming because I have been praying for funds to install a solar power system in my home on the outskirts of Jasikan. This win is indeed a blessing,” he said. Reflecting on the prize's impact, Leslie urged Telecel to continue initiatives that provide customers with meaningful financial support.

“Telecel should continue running promotions like this because people face real challenges, and gestures such as these go a long way towards helping them,” he added.

Executive Head for the Eastern, Oti and Volta Regions, Alex Kwapong, said: “Seeing the Telecel M’ahitti Promo change lives every week brings us immense joy.

This is the value we aim to deliver to our customers through the promotion. We still have two monthly GH¢1 million prizes to award, along with many more weekly and daily prizes.”

The two latest wins add to the growing number of customers who have benefited from the promotion since its launch. To date, one customer has won the GH¢1 million monthly prize, with two more monthly winners yet to emerge.

More than 30 weekly winners have each received GH¢20,000. More than 6,000 customers have each won the daily GH¢100 prize.

With about four weeks remaining, customers can still participate at no cost by opting in through the Telecel Play app or by dialling *500#. The promotion is regulated by the National Lottery Authority (NLA) on the Caritas platform.

Ghana News.title: International Youth Shakers Conclave 2026 set to bring global young leaders to London
Ghana News.content:
The International Youth Shakers Conclave & Awards 2026 is set to bring together young professionals, entrepreneurs, creatives, ministers and changemakers from across the world for a major youth-focused gathering in London.

The event is scheduled for Saturday, November 15, 2026, at the Praise Dome, Aldersbrook Baptist Church, 2 Dover Road, Wanstead, London.

The gathering is being hosted by the Global Youth Network of The World Conference of Mayors, International Praise Centre (IPC London) and Relevant Achievers Impacting Nations (RAIN).

This year’s event is being convened by David Raphaelle Kwaku Antwi, popularly known as Author Ralph Antwi, Founding President of Relevant Achievers Impacting Nations, and Dr Claude Halm-Adjepong of IPC London.

The organisers say the initiative is focused on raising a generation of young people equipped to make an impact in their communities and beyond.

The theme for this year’s Conclave is “Celebrating Youth People Leading Change and Older People Changing Youth.”

The event is expected to attract participants from the United Kingdom, Ghana, Nigeria, Europe, North America and other parts of the world.

It will feature keynote sessions, leadership discussions, business networking and other engagements focused on youth development and leadership.

Youth Shakers Awards

A major highlight of the event will be the Youth Shakers Awards, which will recognise young people making an impact across various fields.

The awards will celebrate individuals in areas including ministry, business, education, creative arts, technology, community development and leadership.

Speaking ahead of the event, convener Author Ralph Antwi said the initiative was designed to go beyond a one-day programme.

“We are not just organising a programme; we are nurturing a movement. We believe in this generation. We have seen what happens when you give a young person faith, a platform and a push — they will shake their world. On November 15th in London, history will be made.”

Dr Claude Halm-Adjepong said IPC London was pleased to host the gathering of young people and leaders.

“IPC London is honoured to open our doors for this global harvest of young giants. London will be a meeting point for purpose, power and possibilities.”

The organisers are inviting young people, professionals, entrepreneurs, creatives and other stakeholders to participate in the event.

Event Details

Event: International Youth Shakers Conclave & Awards 2026

Date: Saturday, November 15, 2026

Venue: Praise Dome, Aldersbrook Baptist Church, 2 Dover Road, Wanstead, London E12 5EA

Conveners: David Raphaelle Kwaku Antwi (Author Ralph Antwi) and Dr Claude Halm-Adjepong

Host: International Praise Centre in collaboration with Relevant Achievers Impacting Nations

Ghana News.title: Gov’t is committed to addressing teachers’ conditions of service, deprived-area allowance – Education Minister
Ghana News.content:
Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu

Haruna Iddrisu, the Minister of Education, on Monday reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to resolving outstanding grievances of teachers, including the payment of promotion arrears and the implementation of the deprived-area allowance.

He noted that the Government had initiated processes to address the concerns raised by the teacher unions and improve conditions of service in the education sector.

Mr Iddrisu gave the assurance at this year’s Ghana Teacher Prize to commemorate teachers and recognise their contribution to national development.

He said the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission, with the support of the Ministry of Finance, would engage the teacher unions on their expired collective agreement on conditions of service.

He said the Government was committed to fulfilling its manifesto pledge on the payment of a deprived-area allowance to teachers serving in underserved communities.

The education minister said discussions were ongoing to validate the data on deprived schools and communities to determine who qualified for the allowance and ensure its effective implementation.

“We are sure that there is absolute government commitment to the manifesto pledge on the deprived-area allowance. What we need to do is validate the data, then we can begin the process of implementation,” he said.

The Minister said the Government had also committed resources to clear outstanding promotion arrears to teachers.

The Ghana Education Service, in collaboration with the relevant institutions, had been tasked to validate the records of teachers who had been promoted but were yet to receive their new salary grades and associated arrears, he explained.

Mr Iddrisu said the exercise was expected to cover more than 51,000 teachers, adding that the Government would make the necessary financial arrangements to settle the outstanding arrears.

The minister commended teachers for their contribution to the development of the country, describing them as the “architects” of every profession.

“We all owe it to the teacher. No profession is possible without the teacher, and for that reason, we recognise you and celebrate you,” he said.

The education minister disclosed that President John Dramani Mahama had approved a new integrated model for basic education infrastructure.

He said the model would bring key basic education facilities together within a single development to ensure more efficient use of resources and improve access to quality education.

Under the proposed model, a basic school complex would include kindergarten, primary and junior high school facilities, as well as laboratories, libraries and information technology facilities.

He said the Government had directed Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies to ensure that new basic education infrastructure reflected the integrated model.

Mr Iddrisu said the initiative was part of efforts to address infrastructure deficits in the education sector, particularly the large number of schools without electricity.

He cited data indicating that about 10,750 schools across the country were still without electricity, affecting approximately three million children.

He said the government would work to mobilise resources through the appropriate funding mechanisms to reduce the infrastructure deficit and ensure that pupils and teachers had access to better learning environments.

Mr Prosper Tachie, the President, Ghana National Association of Teachers,called for the empowerment of teachers in three key areas; legal authority, professional confidence, and economic security.

He said teachers needed the legal authority to perform their professional responsibilities, including maintaining discipline in schools, while also having the confidence and financial security to meet their basic needs.

He cited a World Bank report on the global teaching profession published in May 2026, which emphasised the importance of teachers to the skills development of the global workforce.
