World.title: The 5 Things Croatian Island Residents Say Are Urgently Required
World.content:
October the 6th, 2026 – There are 5 things Croatian island residents say are urgently required in order for any real life to be consistently maintained on the country’s many islands.

High property prices, losing their maritime connection with their hometown during study periods, and having to travel to the mainland for every specialist examination are just some of the everyday challenges faced by young people on Croatian islands. Morski reports that more was revealed during a recently held online workshop called “Stay or leave? – young people and the future of the islands.” The workshop was held as part of the “Island Youth for Global Change” (IYGC) project, young islanders offered concrete solutions and agreed on five key measures that would enable them to live long-term on the islands.

The project was implemented by the Island Movement and LAG 5 within the GEAR UP! call, and the workshop participants focused on five key areas: housing, working conditions, higher education, healthcare, and social life outside the tourist season.

life outside of the summer season is needed

Outside of the boiling, tourism-fuelled summer months, social, sports and cultural activities on many islands almost completely die down. Young people emphasise that they are ready to organise activities themselves, but they lack basic infrastructure.

Solution: It is proposed that cities and municipalities issue public calls through which they would provide young people with premises, basic materials and initial support for establishing sports clubs or organising events, after which the young people would take over the running of the activities themselves.

co-financing the purchase of first properties

Property prices on Croatia’s many islands are largely unaffordable for the local population, which has been highlighted as one of the biggest obstacles to starting a family on the island.

Solution: Introduction of a model in which the local self-government co-finances the purchase of an apartment or house. In return, the buyer commits to long-term residence on the island. In the event of limited budget funds, priority would be given to shortage occupations.

equal treatment for both seasonal and domestic employees

Finding affordable accommodation for workers who stay on the island all year round is a major problem, and inequality in working conditions has also been pointed out. While foreign workers often receive free accommodation, food and utilities in addition to their salary, domestic workers are left without these benefits.

Solution: Construction or conversion of year-round staff accommodation facilities (staff houses) available to domestic workers. Alternatively, it is proposed that domestic workers be granted the right to equal benefits or to a cash allowance in the amount that the employer would otherwise allocate for their accommodation (e.g. around 200 euros per month).

making sure students can always reach home via ferry whatever the season

During four- or five-year studies on the mainland, young people’s connection with the island gradually weakens, which often results in permanent departure.

Solution: Co-financing of at least one trip home per month by the municipalities, as well as the establishment and financial support of island student associations in university cities (following the successful example of the Lošinj student association in Zagreb).

the need for specialist doctors on the islands

Travelling to the mainland for routine or specialist examinations entails a large financial and time cost for island families.

Solution: Organisation of visits by specialist doctors to the island once or twice a month, according to a pre-determined schedule, which would raise primary healthcare to a significantly higher level.

World.title: Estonian folktronica band: Nightclubs are the modern village swing
World.content:
For Viljandi folktronica band Oopus, it's clear that nightclubs today fill the same social role the village swing once did, bringing people together through music and dance.

Last weekend, Viljandi hosted the Etnokulp folk music awards, where hometown heroes Oopus swept Album of the Year, Artist of the Year and New Folk Artist of the Year.

The band blends rave culture with traditional Estonian music, and musician Mari Meentalo said electronic dance music and Estonian folk have more in common than may first appear, from repeating melodic lines to the shared aim of keeping people moving.

"Once the music starts, there's no telling when the party will end!" said bandmate Johannes Ahun, adding that Oopus deliberately brings the two worlds together.

Meentalo believes modern-day nightclubs aren't actually that modern of a concept at all.

"Back in the day, people used to gather by the village swing to socialize," she said. "Nowadays, it's nightclubs where people come together and celebrate."

Vinyl, cassette and reel-to-reel tape

Oopus' latest album, "Reivlender," was released not only on digital platforms but also on reel-to-reel tape, cassette, vinyl and CD. Ahun said the band is interested in exploring older physical formats as they make new music, especially given the renewed interest in those formats.

"As we make music, we're learning how people actually used to make it on these older formats," Ahun said, crediting friends and collaborators who helped make the physical releases possible.

"And there are fans in Estonia, young people like us, who still dream of having music on tape," he added.

World.title: 1 dead in Narva care home blaze, cause likely careless smoking
World.content:
One person perished in a fire at a care home in Narva on Tuesday evening, with the cause believed to be smoking without due care and attention, the Rescue Board said.

The fire was confined to a smoking corner and, with the facility's fire doors and compartments in order, did not spread, meaning no evacuation was needed.

The alarm was called in at 8:51 p.m. on Tuesday to the care home on Rahu põik, on the northern outskirts of Narva.

The first Narva rescuers to arrive identified smoke on the second floor of the facility, began ventilating the rooms and discovered the body of a deceased woman in the smoking corner.

Care home staff had extinguished the localized blaze themselves with fire extinguishers, meaning the fire was no longer active by the time firefighters arrived.

Rescue Board (Päästeamet) personnel then checked the entire building with measuring devices. No carbon monoxide was detected, and ambulance crews examined all residents.

Rescue teams from the Narva and Narva-Jõesuu stations and a field manager from Jõhvi took part in the response.

The fire may have started from careless smoking, and the exact circumstances will be established in further proceedings.

A total of 23 fire fatalities have been reported in Estonia so far this year.

World.title: Agency says specialized care shortage critical as 2,000 waiting for service
World.content:
Just over 2,000 people are on the waiting list for specialized care services, with the number remaining at roughly the same level month after month. The Social Insurance Board considers the situation critical.

In April this year, the Supreme Court ruled that if a person needs a place in a specialized care home, the state must provide one and that the state may not budget less money for specialized care than is needed to meet its statutory obligations. Despite this, as of early October, just over 2,000 people are on the waiting list for specialized care services, with the number remaining at roughly the same level month after month.

Lagle Kalberg, head of the specialized care and rehabilitation unit at the Social Insurance Board (SKA), told ERR that the situation in the sector is currently critical.

"We have a very large number of people on the waiting list who need services right now. We have 2,000 people on the waiting list and based on an analysis of their information and feedback, just over 700 have said they are ready to start receiving services immediately if we can offer them a suitable place. In other words, that is one-third of the people currently waiting for services," Kalberg said.

However, SKA cannot help them because, for example, an applicant may want a place close to home but none is available or funding for the service may be lacking.

"So the situation is critical for us," Kalberg said.

In October, 2,049 people are on the waiting list, while there are more than 2,200 service places for which applications have been submitted. Kalberg explained that the difference between the figures is because one person may receive several specialized care services at the same time or be on the waiting list for several such services, as a person is entitled to use up to three services simultaneously.

Compared with the beginning of the year, the waiting list is about 200 people shorter, while the number of service places is roughly unchanged. According to Kalberg, this means more people have been referred to services and more service places have been filled. The change may also be related to adjustments made to working procedures in the spring, which resulted in intensive efforts to call people on the waiting list.

"We contacted them to understand their current situation while they were on the waiting list and, given the vacancies we were able to offer, whether they were ready to start receiving services," the SKA representative said. "The change in our working procedures has resulted in more people moving from the waiting list into services."

Some people choose to leave the waiting list after SKA contacts them and assesses their ability to cope independently, the support available from their family and other services they may be able to receive.

As of early October, 54 service places were vacant. SKA is waiting for people offered those places to respond within 10 days on whether they will accept them.

Tight state finances cannot justify leaving people without services

Under the Supreme Court's ruling this spring, a lack of state funding does not justify leaving a person without assistance if the Social Insurance Board (SKA) has determined that they meet the eligibility requirements for assistance established by law. The state must actively work to ensure that a sufficient number of places are available and, if necessary, cooperate with the private sector and local governments to do so.

During state budget talks, the Ministry of Social Affairs sought an additional €200 million over the next four years to create new specialized care places and raise the salaries of people working in specialized care homes. Secretary General Maarjo Mändmaa, speaking about the plan in early June, also cited the Supreme Court ruling, expressing hope that it would prompt the government to take the ministry's proposal more seriously.

However, the draft state budget submitted to the Riigikogu last week does not provide for such an allocation. The government decided to add up to €37 million to the sector over the next four years and that amount is intended not only for specialized care but for the entire social affairs and health sector.

As the coalition no longer has a majority in the Riigikogu, it needs additional votes to pass the state budget. Media reports have previously speculated that the coalition hopes to secure those votes from the Social Democrats, who, for example, would like to be able to point to additional funding for specialized care as a political achievement. Social Democratic Party (SDE) Chair Lauri Läänemets told ERR last week that his party was not engaging in horse-trading.

The Estonian Chamber of Disabled People has previously advised people left without assistance and their loved ones to seek help through the courts. However, after the draft state budget was unveiled, the chamber's head, Maarja Krais-Leosk, said that although the amount planned for specialized care was not what had been hoped for, the allocation of up to €37 million was still something to welcome.

In mid-September, specialized care service providers held a protest outside the Riigikogu on Toompea to draw attention to the sector's worsening underfunding.

Specialized care services are intended for people diagnosed with mental disorders who, because of their mental health condition, need guidance, counseling, assistance and supervision from a specialized care support worker in their daily lives and whose needs cannot be met through other social welfare support measures.

The aim of specialized care is to develop people's abilities and increase their capacity to live independently.

World.title: Estonia hold on for 0-0 Nations League home draw against Iceland
World.content:
Estonia played out a hard-fought 0-0 draw at home against Iceland in the Nations League on Tuesday, leaving them second in Group C4 after four games.

The same teams opened the cycle on September 26 in Reykjavik, drawing 1-1, with Andri Guðjohnsen (Blackburn Rovers), son of former Chelsea legend Eiður Guðjohnsen, scoring in the 45th minute and defender Maksim Paskotši (KAA Ghent) later equalizing.

Estonia came into the game knowing a win would put them top of the group with two rounds left, and having beaten Luxembourg at the weekend.

Estonia sat second on five points before the match, two behind Iceland, and were without captain Karol Mets (VfL Bochum) through suspension — Paskotši wore the armband in his absence.

Elron put its last train to Keila 25 minutes back in the timetable Tuesday night to accommodate fans, and President Alar Karis, who leaves office on Monday, was present at the match, as was Estonian FA (EJK) President Aivar Pohlak.

On the night, Iceland created two dangerous situations from set pieces early on, with both requiring referee decisions on penalty appeals. The most threatening came in the 12th minute, when a corner struck Levadia midfielder Rasmus Peetson at the near post and Estonian goalkeeper Matvei Igonen (Degerfors) cleared the ball off the goal line.

Peetson has so far emerged as Estonia's most dangerous attacking player in this Nations League window, and he proved it in the first half: early on, Iceland's 'keeper Hákon Valdimarsson (Brentford) dealt with his effort toward the far corner, and in the closing minutes of the half Peetson sent a strong shot into Valdimarsson's body after a good pass from Patrik Kristal.

An hour in, striker Patrik Kristal turned brilliantly on the right and delivered an accurate cross for Estonia into the Icelandic box, but substitute Mattias Käit and Kristal's teammate at FC Thun failed to connect with his head, and the ball fell to forward Robi Saarma (K Pardubice), who was completely unmarked but not ready in time.

Estonia had 13 shots over the match and continued searching for a winner, with manager Jürgen Henn handing a debut to young Levadia midfielder Maksimilian Skvortsov. Iceland were more dangerous in the final quarter-hour, however, but Paskotši, Erko Jonne Tõugjas (Halmstads BK) and Märten Kuusk (Polonia Warsaw) all defended well.

"Very positive result, although we came to win," captain-for-a-night Paskotši told ERR post-match. "Against this team, two draws is quite a good result. Hard fight, lots of running and duels. It maybe wasn't the most beautiful game, but for me as a defender: I really enjoyed it!"

"I knew what group we're actually in. Maybe our previous results haven't been the best, but in this window we showed that these are the games we have to do properly," he said. "I want to really praise all the players. Both those who started and those who came on: they did so much and I hope our fans see that too," he went on.

The UEFA Nations League is a biennial competition in which Europe's national teams are divided into four tiers, with promotion and relegation between them and a path to the European Championship playoffs.

After Tuesday, Iceland lead Group C4 on eight points, Estonia are second with six, while Bulgaria have four points and Luxembourg three.

The next and final fixtures are on November 13 (away to Luxembourg) and November 16 (at home against Bulgaria).

World.title: Isamaa, Center Party and EKRE struggle to agree on no‑confidence text
World.content:
Isamaa, the Estonian Center Party and EKRE want to file a no‑confidence motion against the prime minister Kristen Michal in the coming days, but after several weeks they still have not agreed on the text. The Social Democratic Party does not plan to join the effort.

Leaders of the opposition factions will meet again next Monday to draft the text. Each faction is currently preparing its own version.

"We agreed that each faction will present its ideas on what should be included in the no‑confidence motion, and that work is still ongoing. Based on that, we cannot say that we already have a unified text," said Center Party deputy chair Lauri Laats.

Isamaa board member Priit Sibul said there is broad agreement on the main points.

"I think the issue is in different nuances. There is no doubt that the opposition includes parties that believe Michal should face a no‑confidence vote, and that agreement will be reached. Whether someone in the opposition thinks Michal's government should continue and will not support the motion will be clear in the vote," Sibul said.

Priit Sibul. Source: Siim Lõvi / ERR

"This is comedy at this point. They have been drafting this text for a month and discussing it for months. They have not managed to produce a single motion. The Social Democrats will support it if Isamaa or the Center Party can show what the new functioning government would look like. That proposal has not been presented to the Social Democrats, and until then we cannot join," said Social Democratic Party chair Lauri Läänemets.

If the Social Democrats or the independents do not join the motion, it will fail. EKRE chair Martin Helme noted that the last successful no‑confidence vote was ten years ago.

"No‑confidence motions are not filed primarily to remove a minister or bring down a government, but because political rules have been violated in a way that cannot be ignored. We must respond," Helme said.

Martin Helme. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

Reform Party faction chair Õnne Pillak said the no‑confidence effort has been discussed for a long time.

"For weeks it has been called an interim government, different names are found. But there is no result. And I think there is no expectation either. People expect the country to be firmly led. They want to see things improve," Pillak said.

Helme said the opposition will file the motion next week. Laats and Sibul are not as certain about that timeline. Sibul said the opposition will definitely file it sometime in October.

World.title: Estonian wildlife park bear prefers people over a winter nap
World.content:
Half an hour north of Tartu, a bear at Elistvere Animal Park skipped hibernation last winter and may do so again, preferring regular meals and human attention to a long sleep.

Mõmmu-Ursula the brown bear enjoys Estonia's fall foliage and is preparing for winter, but when the abandoned cub first arrived at the park last year, staff were curious whether she would hibernate. She did not, said animal caretaker Kairi Hermits.

"She'd nap in her den during the day, but still came out to eat every morning and evening," Hermits recalled. Since her meals are provided, she may simply have decided there was no need to sleep through the winter.

"Compared with wildlife, our animals have the advantage of us providing them food each day," she said.

Ursula also really enjoys human interaction, and is even known to climb a tree to look for people whenever the park is closed, including on Mondays.

"She's very eager to interact with people; she loves the attention," Hermits said.

A bear at Elistvere Animal Park. Source: Elistvere Animal Park

Alert your presence, keep your distance

Nonetheless, Hermits urged people to keep their distance from wildlife out in nature.

Wild animals generally avoid contact with people anyway, but she said talking, humming or singing can help alert them to people's presence in the woods and avoid close encounters.

"When you visit friends, you usually ring the doorbell or knock," Hermits explained. "When we visit the forest, we should be polite there too, because we're visiting wildlife."

While urban bear sightings do happen, encounters with brown bears in Estonia are more likely while hiking or foraging. A few simple tips shared by the Estonian Hunters' Society (EJS) can help keep you safe if you run into a brown bear in the wild.

World.title: Estonia's inflation accelerates to 3.5% in September due to fuel costs
World.content:
Estonia's consumer price index (CPI) rose 3.5 percent on year to September, faster than in recent months, driven by higher fuel and housing costs, Statistics Estonia reported.

The price of gasoline went up 33.8 percent during that time, and that of diesel, subject to an excise duty, by 58 percent year on year.

The price of food and non-alcoholic beverages fell by 1.2 percent on year to September, exerting a downward pressure on the overall rise.

Goods were 3.6 percent and services 3.5 percent more expensive than a year earlier.

Statistics Estonia says the on-month CPI figure between August and September this year was for a 0.9 percent rise.

Commenting on the results, Lauri Veski, Consumer Price Statistics Service Manager at Statistics Estonia, said the rate of price increases had been slower for several months but picked up again in September.

"Year on year, the index rise was influenced the most by the higher costs of housing and transport," Veski said. "The index rise was slowed down by the prices of food and non-alcoholic beverages which have fallen year on year."

The rise in fuel prices resulted from the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. Housing costs were primarily influenced by electricity (which went up by 6.1 percent), natural gas through networks (up by 44.5 percent), refuse collection (up 56.6 percent) and wood fuel (10.6 percent).

"Food and non-alcoholic beverages is the commodity group with the biggest weight in the consumer price index. Prices in this group fell by 1.2 percent year on year, which limited the overall index rise," Veski noted.

CPI. Source: Statistics Estonia

Compared with August 2026, gasoline prices were up 9.5 percent and diesel 9.3 percent in September. Clothing and footwear rose 5.9 percent month on month but remained 1.5 percent lower than a year earlier. Electricity cost 4 percent more and natural gas through networks 22.2 percent more.

Rental payments fell by 3.2 percent month on month, and childcare services were 30 percent cheaper — mainly due to changes in Tallinn municipal kindergarten fees, with most families in the capital now exempt. Hotel accommodation was 10.1 percent cheaper and international flights 13.8 percent less.

Food products were 0.5 percent costlier in September than in August, driven by vegetables (1.8 percent), fruits and nuts (1.9 percent) and milk, dairy products and eggs (0.4 percent).

More detailed information is available from Statistics Estonia's website here and here.

World.title: Estonia joins NATO's largest command exercise Steadfast Duel 26
World.content:
NATO's broad command and staff Exercise Steadfast Duel 26 begins Wednesday, and will test how the alliance's command structures and defense plans function in practice.

It is the alliance's first Article 5 exercise incorporating all 32 member states, including its newest members Sweden and Finland, and is also the largest computer-assisted command post exercise (CAX/CPX) taking place this year.

The Estonian component of the exercise will mostly focus on on rehearsing procedures at Estonian Defense Forces (EDF) HQ, and testing coordination between NATO staffs at different levels.

Exercise Steadfast Duel 26 runs to October 15 and is being led by NATO's Joint Warfare Center based in Norway. It is being held in cooperation with US European Command (USEUCOM), and participants include military and civilian representatives from all 32 NATO member states.

"Steadfast Duel is NATO's most important command structure exercise, where NATO's supreme headquarters in Europe and all joint force command staffs rehearse their war plans," said Maj. Gen. Vahur Karus, Estonia's national lead for the exercise and EDF HQ commander.

NATO exercise #SteadfastDuel26 has begun. From 6–15 October, Estonia is rehearsing its defence plan alongside NATO Allies, testing command procedures, information-sharing and coordination across NATO headquarters. #kaitsevägi #EDF #NATO https://t.co/IXgJvqQdDR — Estonian Defence Forces | Eesti Kaitsevägi (@Kaitsevagi) October 6, 2026

Estonia is taking part as a national command element, Karus added, since the exercise framework and scenario allow for the country to rehearse its own war plans in tandem with those of NATO and neighboring states.

"The biggest benefit for us comes from rehearsing the war plan together with partner agencies, because only that way do we understand what each side expects from the other in preparing for and waging war," he said. "The more we can involve Estonian state agencies in this exercise, the stronger and more credible our broad-based national defense becomes," Karus added via a press release.

Estonian participation includes various EDF units, those of allied nations with a presence in Estonia, the NATO staff element in Estonia, the volunteer Estonian Defense League (EDF), and various military and civilian agencies and law enforcement bodies.

World.title: Iraqi policeman killed in terrorist attack near Kirkuk
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Two security sources told Reuters that ISIS terrorists assaulted a federal police post near the northern Iraqi city of Kirkuk on Monday, killing at least one Iraqi federal policeman and injuring four others.

The assailants used semi-automatic machine guns and sniper fire on the federal police unit stationed in Hawija, around 70 kilometers (43 miles) southwest of Kirkuk.

No one immediately claimed responsibility. However, security and army officials indicated ISIS militants, who are still active in the area, were responsible for the attack.

The raid is the first documented assault by ISIS terrorists on Iraqi security forces since US troops withdrew from the country on September 30, terminating the military operation in Iraq.

The United States led the international coalition that aided Iraqi forces in their war against terrorism, including measures to keep the extremist organization from reorganizing.

Washington said that it will continue to offer targeted training and intelligence assistance following the departure, but Iraqi forces would be fully responsible for the country’s security and the suppression of remnants of terrorist groups.

Despite the defeat of the terrorist group over a decade ago, Iraqi security officials told Reuters that the organization still has sleeper cells in the country.

The pullout of the US-led international coalition raised concerns that a security vacuum would allow the terrorist group to recover momentum, with some officials warning that Iraqi security forces would now have to hold the group without the coalition’s military presence.

World.title: Iraq estimates oil price at $58 per barrel in 2027 federal budget
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi government aims to spend 217 trillion Iraqi dinars (around $166 billion) in 2027, assuming an oil price of $58 per barrel, according to parliamentarians familiar with the draft budget.

The measures would result in a fiscal deficit of around 40 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $30.6 billion).

Members of the parliamentary finance committee told Reuters that the draft budget anticipates crude oil exports of around four million barrels per day, including shipments from Iraqi Kurdistan.

The Iraqi cabinet is also studying raising the local currency’s exchange rate to between 1,400 and 1,500 Iraqi dinars per US dollar, up from roughly 1,300 now, according to legislators.

Oil exports generate the majority of the Iraqi government’s revenue, accounting for roughly 80 percent of the general budget’s resources.

The US-Israeli military conflict with Iran has disrupted shipping via the Strait of Hormuz, prompting Iraq to seek other routes for its crude oil exports.

The Iraqi parliament is about to start official deliberations on the 2027 federal budget.

The 2027 budget represents a structural transformation by allocating 150 trillion ($114.5 billion) for traditional line items and 50 trillion Iraqi dinar ($38.2 billion) for a new World Bank-coordinated program-and-performance model to measure expenditure efficiency.

World.title: Chinese refiners increase oil imports from Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Chinese independent refiners are swiftly increasing their imports of Iraqi and Qatari crude to compensate for a sharp decline in Iranian oil supplies.

As their stockpiles near depletion, private refineries in China are paying considerable premiums to acquire alternatives, according to Reuters.

Experts see that the step represents a desperate search for alternatives due to logistical obstacles, rather than a true rebound in Chinese domestic crude demand.

Private refineries in China have historically relied on deeply discounted, sanctioned Iranian oil to optimize their refining margins, previously importing over one million barrels per day. However, the US naval blockade and the higher cost of Russian oil alternatives are two major geopolitical factors that have forced a shift.

A rigorous US blockade linked to the larger crisis involving Iran has trapped at least 50 tankers transporting mostly Iranian petroleum off the Chinese coast, cutting off the refiners’ key supply source.

State-owned Chinese refiners have successfully secured the majority of the available Russian crude oil. As a result of the fierce competition, Russian barrels now command significant premiums of roughly $30 per barrel above Brent, driving smaller independent refiners out.

Refiners have purchased at least 12 million barrels of Iraqi and Qatari oil for October and November delivery, with total estimates ranging from 15 million to 20 million barrels.

Buyers are mostly interested in the sulfur-rich Basrah Medium and Basrah Heavy grades. Independent refiners normally reject these higher grades in favor of lighter Iranian or Russian choices, but they are embracing them since they are readily available.

Major global commodities trading firms such as Vitol Group, Trafigura Group, Mercuria Energy Group, and TotalEnergies SE are facilitating the deals.

This move is being aided by a steady recovery in total exports leaving the Arabian Gulf via the Strait of Hormuz, making Middle Eastern options physically available even as regional tensions remain.

World.title: Turkey to turn Iraq’s Development Road into multi-fuel energy corridor
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Turkey intends to develop the planned Development Road from Iraq’s southern ports to Europe into a multi-fuel energy corridor worth $80 billion annually.

According to Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar, this strategic route will go beyond typical freight transit by incorporating crucial infrastructure for oil, natural gas, and power transmission.

In a statement to Anadolu Agency (AA), Bayraktar expressed Turkey’s enthusiasm for building the Development Road not merely as a transport corridor but also as a strategic energy route. This route would be bolstered by the inclusion of oil, natural gas, and electricity transmission lines along its path.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi instructed in July the establishment of a defined structure to finance and implement the strategic project of the Development Road, assuring the start of practical steps within a planned timeline.

In early June, the head of the state-owned General Company for Ports of Iraq (GCPI), Farhan al-Fartousi, said that the planning process for the project and the al-Faw Grand Port has made tremendous progress, with essential operating plans already submitted to the government.

The project will enter the implementation phase following government approval in the coming months, according to al-Fartousi.

The $17 billion project, which will connect the al-Faw Grand Port in southern Iraq to the Turkish border by constructing a railway and road network, is anticipated to transform Iraq into a transit center by cutting the time it takes to travel from Asia to Europe.

In addition to pipelines for energy transportation, the project’s railway will significantly assist in the transportation of commodities, with a first-phase capacity of 3.5 million tons and a second-phase capacity of 7.5 million tons.

By connecting the port city of Basra to Turkey via an overland route, the logistics project will compete with Egypt’s Suez Canal and establish Basra as a gateway to Europe.

In 2024, Turkey formed a council involving Bulgaria, Hungary, and Serbia to arrange the connection of Europe with Iraq’s Development Road.

As a worldwide corridor for commodities and energy transportation, the project is expected to attract international commerce and create considerable employment opportunities and investment possibilities in Iraq and other countries in the region.

World.title: Iraq’s seaborne oil exports jump to 2.57 million bpd in September
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s crude oil exports rose for the fourth consecutive month in September, growing by over nine percent—equivalent to 218,000 barrels per day—to reach their highest level since the start of the Iran war.

Iraq’s seaborne crude oil exports jumped to 2.57 million barrels per day in September, up from 2.35 million barrels per day in August.

Despite the monthly improvement, Iraqi oil exports in September remained 25 percent lower than the 3.41 million barrels per day recorded during the same month in 2025.

Iraq’s oil exports gradually recovered in September, after hitting a low of 98,000 barrels per day in May.

Iraq’s average crude oil exports plummeted by 52 percent between January and September 2026, to an average of 1.6 million barrels per day, down from 3.34 million barrels per day in the same period in 2025.

The volume of oil exports surpassed three million barrels per day at the beginning of the year before experiencing a major shock due to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which caused shipments to collapse to 540,000 barrels per day in March.

Exports continued to fall sharply, reaching historic lows of more than 90 percent in April and May before gradually recovering to 2.57 million barrels per day in September.

World.title: Iraq targets 1M electric vehicles via Green Taxi initiative
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Environment reaffirmed on Tuesday, October 6, 2026, that private sector investment forms the bedrock of its national “Green Taxi” initiative and the phased transition toward deploying one million electric vehicles (EVs).

Speaking to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Haidar Qasim Al-Darraji, Director General of the General Company for Carbon Economics at the Ministry of Environment, outlined a comprehensive framework to transform Iraq’s transportation grid into an investable, eco-friendly ecosystem.

Al-Darraji emphasized that the green transit transition cannot operate as a conventional state-run enterprise, but rather as an integrated public-private partnership (PPP) bringing together government regulators, commercial banks, private equity investors, energy providers, and automotive innovators.

Under this model, the state will establish statutory and technical codes, streamline the regulatory climate, lay foundational infrastructure, and verify carbon credit baselines. In turn, private industry will handle capital expenditure, vehicle manufacturing, importation, fleet operations, maintenance logistics, and the rollout of solar-powered charging networks.

Inter-agency groundwork is already underway through coordinated channels involving the Ministry of Environment, the Ministry of Transport, and the General Company for Private Transport Management. The bodies are evaluating existing municipal transit garages and public transport depots for conversion into EV charging hubs powered by distributed solar photovoltaic systems.

Clarifying the scale of the transition, Al-Darraji noted that the target of one million electric vehicles is a phased, metrics-driven national roadmap rather than an overnight influx. Rollouts will begin via scalable pilot projects across Baghdad before expanding into the provinces.

The strategic objective is to cultivate an integrated domestic industrial value chain around e-mobility—spanning local assembly, maintenance, bank lending, commercial insurance, ride-hailing software, and monetization under sovereign carbon credit mechanisms—thereby curbing state fiscal burdens and generating skilled technical employment.

In tandem with public sustainability policies, regional automotive distributors are expanding their electrified footprints across the domestic market. Ahmed Al-Ani, Branch Director of Toyota Iraq, revealed to INA that Iraq has emerged as a major regional adopter of hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs), ranking as the second-largest consumer of hybrid cars in the Middle East.

Highlighting consumer demand for green mobility, Al-Ani announced the official domestic market launch of two electrified Toyota flagships: the all-electric bZ4X Touring SUV and the RAV4 Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicle (PHEV), offering extended electric range and modern efficiency tailored to Iraq’s expanding charging landscape.

World.title: US dollar holds above 160,000 IQD in Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The U.S. dollar held firm above the 160,000-dinar threshold across Iraq’s parallel currency markets on Tuesday, October 6, 2026, consolidating Monday’s steep gains across trading hubs in Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra.

The persistent gap between free-market rates and the Central Bank of Iraq’s official peg of 131,000 dinars per $100 continues to hover near 22.5 percent as exchange bureaus navigate heavy cash demand.

Market data showed that exchange bureaus and trading counters in the capital city of Baghdad maintained cash selling rates at 160,500 dinars per $100, while buying bids ticked slightly higher to 160,150 dinars, narrowing the intraday bid-ask spread.

In Erbil, the regional hub of the Kurdistan Region, parallel counters offered greenbacks at 160,000 dinars per $100 against purchase bids of 159,750 dinars. In the southern trade center of Basra, rates rose to match the 160,000 mark, with cash sales quoted at 160,000 dinars per $100 and buying bids settling at 159,500 dinars.

The elevated rates across major cities reflect ongoing liquidity pressures as retail merchants and unbanked importers seek physical foreign currency outside the formal electronic transfer platform. Despite regular market interventions and central bank oversight, speculative buying and regional fiscal uncertainties continue to anchor cash prices above key psychological thresholds.

World.title: Yemen’s Houthis claim attack on Riyadh airport, deny losing territory
World.content:
Sanaa – Yemen’s Houthis claimed an attack on the main airport in the Saudi capital while also denying on Tuesday losing territory to government forces, as fighting intensified.

After declaring a counter-offensive, government forces claimed Monday to have pushed the Houthis out of the Bab al-Mandab area, a key shipping route in the Red Sea, as well as the port city of Mocha, which was captured last month.

Claims by both sides have been impossible to independently verify with the situation on the ground moving fast and access for journalists difficult.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree claimed on Telegram that the group still held all territory recently seized, including strategic areas along the Red Sea coast.

Their fighters “have full control over all their advances on the ground”, he said.

He said the Houthis had carried out dozens of strikes in the past few hours targeting government forces in Yemen’s Al-Jawf and Marib regions, while also attacking Taiz governorate.

On Monday night, the Houthis said they had struck Riyadh airport and a refinery belonging to Saudi state oil giant Aramco.

Loud explosions rattled the Saudi capital on Monday evening.

On Tuesday Saudi Arabia’s civilian aviation authority said at least three people were also wounded in attacks on Jazan and Najran airports near the Yemen border a day earlier.

Saudi Arabia, the main backer of the Yemeni government, has been providing air support for a counter-offensive launched by government forces.

– ‘Victories on several fronts’ –

Yemen’s government forces claimed late Monday that they had achieved “victories on several fronts”, but military sources with the government nevertheless refrained from officially confirming taking Mocha, only saying they had cut the one supply route to the area.

They also said they expelled the Houthis from several areas in Taiz in the southwest, where fighting has surged in recent days.

Yemen’s government has announced a goal of retaking all Houthi territory — home to most of the country’s population, and much of it held for more than a decade.

Yemen’s civil war flared up again in July after years of relative calm, opening a new front in the wider Middle East war that began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February.

The Houthis last month seized control of the entire western coastline of Yemen along the Red Sea in the country’s deadliest fighting in years.

Since then, they have regularly targeted oil and military installations in Saudi Arabia and have declared a maritime blockade on its ships.

Pakistan and Turkey have pledged to deploy troops to Saudi Arabia under a mutual defence pact following weeks of Houthi attacks.

The Yemen conflict has caused a humanitarian crisis. Since the renewed fighting broke out, more than 184,000 people have been displaced from their homes, according to the United Nations.

A spokesman for UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said he was “deeply concerned by the sharp escalation in fighting”. He condemned “the continued Houthi cross-border attacks” on Saudi Arabia.

World.title: 'Inflation man Modi's reign of terror continues': Congress on repo rate hike
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Congress on Wednesday attacked the Centre after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%, saying the move would further increase the financial burden on the public.

Calling Prime Minister Narendra Modi âinflation manâ, the Congress said, âInflation Man Modi's reign of terror continues. Now the public's back will be broken even further.â

The party said the rate hike would push up borrowing costs for home, car, personal and business loans, resulting in higher EMIs and potentially longer repayment periods. âTo curb inflation as per Modi's intent, the RBI has today raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5%,â it said.

"This means your home loan, car loan, personal loan, and business loan interest rates will now increase. Now you'll have to pay higher EMIs, and the loan repayment period will also get extended. The promise was of 'good days,' but what we got were days of extortion," he added.

The RBI's monetary policy committee unanimously approved the hike and shifted its stance from neutral to calibrated tightening, citing stronger-than-expected economic growth and broader price pressures.





The rate increase would raise the monthly EMI on a Rs 1 crore home loan with a 15-year tenure by around Rs 1,500, assuming a base rate of 8.50%. If borrowers keep their EMI unchanged, the higher interest rate could extend the repayment period by roughly six instalments.

The RBI also raised its FY27 real GDP growth forecast by 40 basis points to 7.1%, while increasing its inflation projection by 20 basis points to 5.2%. RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said stronger capacity utilisation, bank credit growth, government capital expenditure and infrastructure spending were supporting investment and demand.

CPI inflation rose to 4.8% in August from 4.5% in July. Malhotra said price pressures had broadened beyond volatile items, with food inflation becoming more widespread, including higher sugar and onion prices.

The Congress said the government's promise of âgood daysâ had instead delivered âdays of extortionâ.

World.title: Opposition seeks President Murmu's appointment over CEC Gyanesh Kumar issue
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Opposition parties on Wednesday sought an appointment with President Droupadi Murmu to raise issues related to chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, sources told news agency ANI.

Rahul Gandhi

World.title: Kharge to host INDIA bloc lunch as opposition plans next move after ‘vote chori’ protest
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A day after INDIA bloc MPs marched towards the Election Commission and Rahul Gandhi staged an hours-long sit-in, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge is set to host opposition MPs for lunch in Delhi.

Kharge has invited INDIA bloc MPs for lunch at 1.30 pm at Sagar Ratna on Janpath, sources informed ANI. The MPs are also expected to sign a letter seeking a meeting with Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

The meeting comes after a dramatic day of protests on Tuesday, when opposition MPs marched from Parliament towards the Election Commission headquarters, demanding a meeting with the election commissioners over their allegations of irregularities in the electoral process.

What happened on Tuesday

The march was stopped by Delhi Police near Akashvani Bhawan, after which opposition MPs staged a sit-in. Rahul Gandhi, along with Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other Congress leaders, had entered the Akashvani Bhawan premises and insisted that the delegation be allowed to meet the election commissioners.

World.title: Ashok Chakra for flydubai pilot Smit Machchar? Rajya Sabha MP Kartikeya Sharma urges PM Modi
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Rajya Sabha member Kartikeya Sharma has written to

Machchar was critically injured during flydubai flight FZ1073 on September 30 after his co-pilot attacked him and attempted to take control of the aircraft.

Despite suffering severe injuries, Machchar remained focused on protecting the 174 passengers on board and continued to carry out his duties under extreme circumstances.

Sharma said Machchar's courage and composure during the crisis reflected the "indomitable spirit" and dedication to duty of Indians.

He said the captain put the safety of passengers ahead of his own well-being despite being seriously injured.

The Rajya Sabha member said recognising Machchar at the national level would not only honour his bravery but also inspire young people across the country. He added that every Indian was proud of the captain's courage.

Sharma urged Prime Minister Modi to consider conferring the 'Ashok Chakra' on Machchar in recognition of his bravery and dedication to duty.





The letter comes days after the alleged hijacking attempt aboard flydubai flight FZ1073. According to reports, Omani co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami attacked Machchar with an axe inside the cockpit in an attempt to bring down the aircraft.

Despite suffering serious injuries, Machchar managed to unlatch the cockpit door, allowing passengers and off-duty crew members to enter and restrain the co-pilot.

World.title: CEC row LIVE: CJP’s Saurav Das to submit ‘intimation letter’ to Delhi Police ahead of October 10 Jantar Mantar protest; security tightened
World.content:
Security was stepped up outside the Parliament Street police station in New Delhi on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) ahead of the planned arrival of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) convenor Saurav Das, who is scheduled to submit an ‘intimation letter’ to the Delhi Police regarding the organisation’s proposed protest pressing for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the revocation of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls at Jantar Mantar on October 10.

Also read: ECI fact-checks claims on Form 6 following SC observation

Around 260 people, including 10 MPs, were detained on October 6 during the INDIA bloc protest march from Parliament to Election Commission of India. Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, K. C. Venugopal and Pawan Khera were among those detained after staging a sit-in at Akashvani Bhawan; all were released later.

Also read: ECI says Opposition MP’s Parliament Annexe meet demand ‘could not be accepted’

“What has been done to my country is treason,” Leader of Opposition (LoP) in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi had said even as the Opposition parties closed ranks on Tuesday (October 6, 2026), marching from Parliament to the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) headquarters to demand the scrapping of special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, restoring the names of deleted voters and sacking of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

World.title: RBI MPC meeting LIVE updates: Repo rate hiked to 5.5%; 'focus is on bringing headline inflation to target of 4%', Governor Sanjay Malhotra says
World.content:
The Reserve Bank of India announced its bi-monthly monetary policy on Wednesday (October 7, 2026), unanimously deciding to increase the repo rate by 25 basis points, from 5.25% to 5.50%. The key rate hike comes after nearly three-and-a half years amid the continuing West Asia conflict.

The real GDP growth for FY27 is projected at 7.1%, while CPI inflation is now projected at 5.2%, Reserve Bank Governor Sanjay Malhotra said after the conclusion of the three-day meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee. The policy stance has been revised to ‘calibrated tightening’ from ‘neutral, he said.

Also read | RBI may deliver two rate hikes by CY 2026: Analysts

The last repo rate hike was in February 2023, when the RBI raised the rate by 0.25%to 6.50%. It kept the rate unchanged through 2023-24 before beginning its rate-cut cycle in 2025.

World.title: CJI agrees to take a call on hearing a plea to recall split verdict in CEC appointments law case
World.content:
The Supreme Court of India on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) agreed to examine and take a call on hearing an application seeking a recall of a split verdict pronounced on September 23 in a case challenging the Election Commissioners’ appointments law.

The application, orally mentioned before Chief Justice of India Surya Kant by senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, questions why one of the judges on the apex court Bench, Justice Satish Chandra Sharma, did not reveal during multiple court proceedings that his son was a standing counsel for the Election Commission of India (ECI).

The application, filed by Naman Sherstra, was mentioned the previous week before Justice Dipankar Datta, who was the lead judge on the Bench which gave the split verdict.

Justice Datta had asked Mr. Sankaranarayanan to mention the application before the Chief Justice as the records of the case had already been returned to the CJI.

Mr. Sherstra has sought a recall of the opinion given by Justice Sharma, who was the puisne judge on the Division Bench headed by Justice Datta, on September 23 on the question of referring the challenge to the constitutional validity of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023 to a five-judge Bench.

While Justice Datta, in his opinion, had declined the reference to a Constitution Bench, Justice Sharma took an opposing view in favour of the reference. Eventually, both judges on the Bench passed a common order for the Chief Justice of India to allocate the case to a Constitution Bench.

The application has objected to this common order, but did not challenge, specifically, the separate opinion given by Justice Datta.

Justice Datta had observed in his opinion that the 2023 law was prima facie wrong to ignore an earlier Constitution Bench judgment in the Anoop Baranwal case, which had included the Chief Justice of India as a neutral member in the Prime Minister-led selection panel for Chief Election Commissioners (CECs) and Election Commissioners (ECs). The 2023 law had replaced the CJI with a Union Minister nominated by the Prime Minister. Justice Datta had said the replacement gave the Executive veto power over CEC/EC appointments and reduced the presence of the Opposition Leader of the Lok Sabha to an ornamental status in the panel. Justice Datta had reminded that the appointment and functioning of Election Commissioners were integral to free and fair elections.

Subsequent to the September 23 verdict, media reports had alleged that Justice Sharma’s son was a standing counsel for the ECI.

Another petitioner, Jaya Thakur, has already filed a curative petition on September 29 to recall the split verdict, alleging “reasonable apprehension of bias and propriety”.

Mr. Shestra, though similarly seeking a recall, did not impute “actual bias, motive or want of good faith” on the part of Justice Sharma.

“The grievance is much narrower- whether, in view of an existing professional engagement of an immediate family member of the judge concerned with the institution whose statutory composition and with the functionaries of such institution whose appointments were directly under challenge, the judge ought to have disclosed the fact of such engagement to the parties when the proceedings were ongoing?” Mr. Sherstra’s application has asked.

The application said, “Siddharth Sharma (son of Justice Satish Chandra Sharma) was appointed as the standing counsel for the ECI before the Madhya Pradesh High Court on July 10, 2024, after the appointment of Gyanesh Kumar and Dr. Sukhbir Singh Sandhu to the poll body”.

“This engagement has continued since the elevation of Gyanesh Kumar as CEC and the appointment of Dr. Vivek Joshi. It is prudent to assume that the incumbent members of the ECI, and specifically Mr. Gyanesh Kumar and Dr. Sukhbir Singh Sandhu, had a direct role and/or had direct knowledge of the appointment of Siddharth Sharma as the standing counsel for the ECI before the Madhya Pradesh High Court,” the application said.

The application said, “The engagement of Justice Satish Chandra Sharma’s son as the standing counsel for the ECI before the Madhya Pradesh High Court was not disclosed to the parties by Justice Satish Chandra Sharma at any point in time during the five hearings in the matter on May 5, May 7, May 14, May 27 and July 30”.

World.title: Bharatbala’s ‘Ramnami’ wins National Award: The story of the Chhattisgarh sect that tattoos ‘Ram’ on their bodies
World.content:
The story of this national award begins with one photograph.

Five years ago, Chennai-based filmmaker Bharatbala travelled to Champa in Chattisgarh, chasing the story of the Ramnami community, an ostracised devotional Hindu sect founded in the 1890s. Back in the 19th Century, they were barred from entering temples because of their caste. As a form of peaceful protest, they decided to immerse their bodies in streaks of carefully placed Sanskrit lettering spelling out the word ‘Ram’, a god in India in whose name miracles and unspeakable horrors alike, have been committed over the years.

Bharatbala says that he was not interested in politicising or marketing Ram when he first heard about the community. “Ram can market himself,” he says. Instead, he wanted to capture the tale of this community reeling from years of untouchability and a riveting history. “I was visiting my father-in-law in Auroville and stumbled upon a French photographer who had travelled around India. One of his images was of the Ramnami," he says. The journey led him straight to Champa where the filmmaker travelled with a lean crew of about six to seven members and spent about 15 days trying to form a relationship and understand the Ramnamis who continue to tattoo themselves head to toe as a form of penance.

In six minutes, the filmmaker seemed to capture several people’s imaginations. Ramnami won the Best Documentary award at the 72nd National Film Award on September 22. Bharatbala received the honour from President Droupadi Murmu, and added that this was a moment of elation.

A mind of one’s own

This moment is not unfamiliar to the filmmaker though. In the years that Bharatbala has spent making 124 films to study India’s vast culture through a 1,000-film odyssey called Virtual Bharat, he seems to have achieved elation. "I feel the youngest now," he laughs. "It's a volcano of love, excitement and creativity. Suddenly I am a man in a hurry, because there is so much more to do."

The pace has been relentless. "We are making three films a month. We are always in some place or the other," he says, adding that they have just wrapped up a film on the production of Ajrakh block printing in Barmer, Rajasthan, and another on an idol maker in Swamimalai, Tamil Nadu. "It's not just about making an idol. It's what he has to shoulder, his devotion to creation," he says.

Bharatbala says that it is people who interest him the most. If one does not document them or several Indian traditions, it is likely that they may remain in the shadows, he adds. It is why he chose to tell the story of the Ramnami community through Manohar, the central subject. The film begins with the line “Hamen kuchh farak nahin padta, hamara tan aur man hi hai mandir."

This placement of this dialogue and shot is important as it establishes Manohar and the rest of the community's philosophy towards life despite the changing times. Bharatbala says that the elders in the community have maintained that they discover the God within. “They don't need to go to the temple. They have found the temple lying within them. For them, this is penance,” he adds.

Yet, he also says that he has noticed an important shift. In the last minute of the film, we watch a young child in the community climbing over Manohar. The child remains tattoo-less. “That is where the spirit of the story lies,” he says.

"They have of course watched the movie. Life has changed in the last five years for them. They have become a destination. Foreign crews have come and filmed the community after our release. They were even called by the Prime Minister. One member of the community gave him a shawl with Ram scrawled all over it,” he says.

Bharatbala is raring to tell many such other tales. He has just completed a feature film on the Maha Kumbh Mela shot in 2025 over 45 days. “The story is about Hindustani classical music, a patriarchal father, and daughters who are taking a legacy forward,” he says. Legendary music composer AR Rahman, who has worked with the director back in 1997 on the iconic ‘Vande Maataram’ song and in the 2013 film Maryan, has collaborated with him on nine out of 12 tracks, he says.

Has the tireless pace and the film made an impact on him? “I am a changed person. I am liberated," he says. "If you are working for somebody, there is a studio, a producer, financial commitments. We have no such pressure. I am a servant of these stories. Nothing else.”

World.title: Pressure rising on Karnataka government to withdraw anti-cow slaughter and anti-conversion laws
World.content:
The Congress government seems to be under pressure as restive Muslim and Christian communities have come together with a demand to act on the party’s promise to withdraw the Karnataka Prevention of Slaughter and Preservation of Cattle Act, 2020, popularly known as the anti-cow slaughter legislation, and the Karnataka Protection of Right to Freedom of Religion Act, 2022, known as the anti-conversion Act.

Besides, Muslims are seeking clarity on the government’s stand over reservation for them under 2B category, and are urging the government to increase the reservation from 4% to 8% based on the population. Christians are demanding a separate 1% reservation under the OBC reservation matrix. The communities have also sought clarity on the imbroglio over the hate speech Bill.

Though former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah had initiated the process to withdraw/amend the legislations in the initial days of the second tenure in 2023, it came under pressure from Hindu mutt seers, who had collectively opposed any such move, forcing the government to backtrack.

While the respective community leaders have met Congress’s legislators and senior leadership separately on multiple occasions to press for their demands, the community leaders are also planning a coordinated effort ahead of the Winter Session in December. “We have waited over three years for the government to act. The community has become restive at the inaction. What is the difference between the Congress and BJP governments, if it continues with the same legislations? Muslims suffered under the BJP and incidents of attack on Christians continue even now,” said Shabeer Ahmed, Karnataka Rajya Muslim Okkoota (KRMO) Steering Committee member. “The Winter Session would be the last possible window for the government to withdraw the legislation, and two communities are working together.”

Also read | Explained | Karnataka’s anti-conversion legislation

In May, after the KRMO announced a muslim convention where “Promises of Congress Government, Gaps in Delivery and Charter of Demands” was released, the State government withdrew the contentious ban on Muslim girls wearing hijab to educational institutions as a damage control measure. The Congress government, however, viewed the convention as embarrassing and that damaged the party’s image. In a controversial move, the BJP government in 2022 had banned wearing the hijab in educational institutions.

“Both communities are coming together in a big way across the State. Jointly strategies have been drawn for certain programmes to create awareness within communities and to take our demand to a logical end. Plans are afoot to hold a massive joint protest in November. Joint protests will also be held in district centres,” acknowledged J.A. Kanthraj, spokesperson of the Archdiocese of Bangalore.

One of the Cabinet Ministers said that the government could move on the two legislations since the Congress has attained majority in the Upper House only recently. Stating that the government was still “mulling over” the legislations, another senior Minister said that the government would abide by the Supreme Court ruling on hate speech in which the apex court said that the current provisions were adequate to address hate speech. Incidentally, the Ministry of Home Affairs stalled the Karnataka Hate Speech and Hate Crimes (Prevention) Bill, 2025, passed by both Houses of the legislature, citing that the provisions of BNS was adequate, after the Karnataka Governor referred the Bill to the President.

Asked if there was any pressure against action on the anti-cow slaughter and anti-conversion laws, the Minister said: “There is no pressure on us. The Law Department will take a call on it.”

When his views were sought, Minister for Health and Family Welfare, Minority Affairs, Haj and Wakf U.T. Khader said: “There is a demand to do it. The government (under Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar) is new. It is aware of the issue and is positively thinking about it.”

World.title: West Bengal poll office says eligible deleted voters can apply through Form 6 to restore name in rolls
World.content:
Kolkata

The West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer’s (CEO) office issued a statement on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) night and said that any eligible voter who has been deleted during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) can apply for their name to be restored through Form 6. The West Bengal CEO said that this list of deleted names is now available online for people to check.

Also read: Byelections 2026 highlights

“For left out eligible voter, the list of ASDD (Absentee, Shifted, Dead, Deleted) voters of SIR 2026 is available at the link ceowestbengal.wb.gov.in/asdsir and also at the respective links on the websites of the District Electoral Officers. Any person in this list, may submit Form 6 online or through BLO for inclusion of his/her name in the Electoral Roll,” the notice issued by the CEO, WB office said late on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) night.

According to the first draft roll published in December 2025, West Bengal had over 58 lakh ASDD voters. Around 24.16 lakh electors were identified as deceased, 32.65 lakh electors as shifted and absent, and 1.38 lakh electors were found to have duplicate enrolments in multiple places.

Amid the rising turmoil over the Election Commission of India and the rising pressure on the poll body for alleged wrongful deletions, the ECI recently said that it will undertake a special drive to restore the names left out during the SIR process. However, this did not initially include West Bengal.

When the final voter roll came out in West Bengal, over 27 lakh people were deleted after the adjudication process found them ineligible. However, after much political turmoil, the Supreme Court set up 19 appellate tribunals to recheck these 27 lakh cases. These 19 tribunals are headed by former judges of the Calcutta High Court.

However, no clarity has been offered on what will happen to the 27 lakh people who appealed to the tribunals to get their names restored. Whether they will also be eligible to fill up Form 6 to get reinstated in the voter rolls remained unclear.

“Why are high ranking former judges being asked to look at appeals? This is the job of the CEO and ERO according to Section 24 of the Representation of Peoples Act. These tribunals are a blunder and they are the reason why many may not be able to access Form 6 in West Bengal, because these people are stuck in between,” former CEO of West Bengal, Jawhar Sircar told The Hindu. He added that the notice published by the current CEO, WB is a clear admission of guilt that there were “wrongful” deletions during the Special Intensive Revision in West Bengal unlike what was claimed by the authorities initially.

World.title: Kochi gang-rape case: Two more, including woman, taken into custody
World.content:
The Kalamassery police investigating the alleged gang-rape of a woman after she was reportedly promised a job at a spa have taken two more people into custody.

Saranya, aka Ammu, and Sanju were taken into custody from Wayanad, District Police Chief (Kochi city) Kaliraj Mahesh Kumar told the media in Kochi on Wednesday. The duo is set to be brought to the Kalamassery police station later in the day.

The police had arrested two men – Sreeraj of Karthikappally, Alappuzha, and Jithu Martin of Thrikkakara, Ernakulam – on Monday in connection with the case. They have been remanded in judicial custody.

3 spas raided

Mr. Mahesh Kumar said the police had raided three spas run by Mr. Sreeraj as part of the probe. “Investigation will be launched into illegal spas in Kochi,” he said.

The alleged incident took place on October 2 at a lodge in the city. The woman was allegedly invited to the lodge after being informed that she had been selected for a manager’s job, then drugged and gang-raped.

Minister for Social Justice V. E. Abdul Gafoor on Tuesday assured all necessary government support to the survivor.

According to a statement issued by the Minister’s office, Mr. Gafoor spoke to the survivor’s partner over the phone and assured that all government assistance, including treatment and legal aid, would be provided to the survivor.

World.title: Rahul fighting SIR, 'diabolical duo' busy filing FIR: Congress
World.content:
The Congress on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) lashed out at the Modi government after the Delhi Police registered an FIR against Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra for allegedly forcibly entering Akashvani Bhawan, saying the "diabolical duo" of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah is "rattled" and "desperate".

The Opposition party also said the writing on the wall is clear.

The Opposition party's attack on the government came after the Delhi Police registered an FIR against the two Congress leaders and their supporters for allegedly forcibly entering Akashvani Bhawan during the Opposition's march against the CEC on October 6.

The FIR was registered after police received a complaint alleging that Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi, their supporters and other MPs accompanying them entered the Akashvani Bhawan premises without permission, the Delhi Police officials said.

Reacting to the development, Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh said, “For almost two years now the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has been relentlessly exposing, through factual evidence, the Vote Chori conspiracy hatched between the PM & the HM on one side and the CEC on the other," Mr. Ramesh said on X.

Crores of genuine voters have lost their Constitutional right to vote through the atrocious process of SIR — "Shahenshah Instigated Removal", Mr. Ramesh charged.

And, when the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha adopts the method of satyagraha to highlight the injustices of SIR, the Delhi Police registers an FIR against him and other leaders, he said.

"The diabolical duo is nervous, rattled and desperate. The writing on the wall is clear," Mr. Ramesh said.

Later, Mr. Ramesh told PTI that while Rahul Gandhi was fighting SIR, the "diabolical duo" was busy filing FIR.

On Tuesday (October 6, 2026), the two Congress leaders were among 260 people detained following an over eight-hour sit-in inside Akashvani Bhawan after an INDIA bloc march towards the Election Commission office was stopped by police.

The opposition MPs were protesting against alleged irregularities in the functioning of the Election Commission under Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, raising the issue of "vote chori".

World.title: FBR introduces rules for electronic scrutiny of taxpayers
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) has begun extending the use of artificial intelligence to scrutinise individual tax returns, enabling its automated system to detect factual and legal mistakes and discrepancies before initiating legal or penal action.

The draft rules, titled “38-B Procedure for electronic scrutiny and intimation of issues detected by the automated system”, have been proposed through amendments to the Income Tax Rules 2002. The draft rules will be finalised after three days, following feedback from stakeholders.

A significant feature of the proposed arrangement is the automated analysis and cross-matching of information available with tax authorities. This will allow the system to compare information declared in income tax returns with other available data and flag potential discrepancies for clarification by taxpayers.

The automated system will identify issues in tax returns and send online advice or advance intimation to taxpayers through the IRIS portal, pointing out factual and legal mistakes or discrepancies. The purpose is to allow taxpayers to clarify the issues, rectify errors or take corrective action before legal or penal proceedings are initiated. The detection of a discrepancy by the automated system, however, will not itself result in enforcement action.

Tax watchdog to use automated system to detect mistakes, discrepancies

Under the proposed mechanism, taxpayers will first be informed electronically about discrepancies detected in their income tax returns and given an opportunity to clarify or rectify them through a prescribed mechanism. The system-generated advance intimation identifying discrepancies may also be sent by the officer of Inland Revenue having jurisdiction over the taxpayer.

The intimation will specify a response period of at least seven days during which the taxpayer can clarify or rectify the discrepancy. If the taxpayer fails to respond within the stipulated period, another reminder will be issued, providing a further period of at least seven days to respond.

The officer of Inland Revenue having jurisdiction over the taxpayer will analyse the taxpayer’s response, or the absence of a response, before taking appropriate action under the relevant provisions of the Income Tax Ordinance and rules.

The proposed arrangement effectively introduces an automated scrutiny layer immediately after processing income tax returns, while retaining the role of the tax officer in determining whether a discrepancy warrants action under the law.

Published in Dawn, October 7th, 2026

World.title: Islamabad ATC indicts Imaan, Hadi in security breach case despite objection over incomplete legal formalities
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Tuesday formally indicted lawyers Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and Hadi Ali Chattha in a case pertaining to the alleged disruption of the security route of an international cricket team and incitement to public unrest.

Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra presided over the proceedings, during which both accused were produced through video link.

At the outset, Hadi objected to the framing of charges, stating that he had not yet been provided copies of the case documents. He argued that charges could not be framed before completion of all legal formalities.

Advocate Zainab Janjua, representing Imaan and Hadi, also opposed the indictment, submitting that neither of them had been provided copies of the case record. She further contended that both the accused had not been allowed to meet their lawyers, and therefore the requirements for framing charges had not been fulfilled.

Despite the objections, the court proceeded with the formal indictment of both accused.

Addressing Imaan and Hadi, Judge Sipra observed that they could challenge the order if they wished to do so.

The court subsequently summoned prosecution witnesses on Friday and directed that both accused be produced before the court at the next hearing.

The proceedings were then adjourned until October 9 (Friday).

The indictment hearing had been postponed on Tuesday after it appeared that Imaan and Hadi could not be produced in court via video link due to a power outage. Judge Sipra had directed jail authorities to ensure the presence of both accused through video link at the next hearing, warning that contempt of court proceedings would be initiated in case of non-compliance.

Imaan and Hadi’s rearrest

The lawyer couple has been in jail since their arrest on Jan 23 in a case registered against them for protesting outside the Islamabad High Court (IHC) and allegedly manhandling the IHC Bar Association (IHCBA) president. The arrest prompted criticism by rights bodies, politicians and journalists, who stressed the couple’s right to a fair trial.

Just a day later, a sessions court sentenced them to 17 years on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca) in a case pertaining to controversial social media posts.

The convictions were widely condemned by lawyers and United Nations (UN) experts .

On Sept 17, following months of litigation before the courts , the Supreme Court suspended their sentences in the case. The SC ordered their release pending the Islamabad High Court’s final verdict on their appeals against the trial court’s decision.

However, the reprieve was short-lived as hours later, Islamabad police arrested the couple again in connection with another case and produced them before an ATC, which sent them to jail on judicial remand.

The fresh case in which the two were arrested was registered at the federal capital’s Kohsar police station on March 22 last year on the complaint of City Magistrate Ghulam Murtaza Chandio.

Imaan and her husband were accused of chanting anti-government slogans and blocking roads and were nominated by name in the FIR. However, at the time of registration of the case, no section of the Anti-Terrorism Act (ATA) had been added.

The FIR included sections 188 (disobedience of an order lawfully promulgated by a public servant), 341 (wrongful restraint), 506 (punishment for criminal intimidation), 353 (assault or use of criminal force to deter a public servant from discharging their official duty) and 186 (obstructing a public servant in the performance of official duties).

World.title: 18 terrorists killed in separate engagements in KP, Balochistan: state media
World.content:
Security forces eliminated 18 terrorists in separate engagements in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, state media reported on Wednesday, citing security sources.

In KP, Pakistan TV said security forces “killed 13 Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists in an intelligence-based operation in North Waziristan, as operations against militant groups continue under the Azm-e-Istehkam vision”.

Separately, in Balochistan’s Mastung district, security forces killed five terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Hindustan, Pakistan TV reported.

It added that security forces recovered heavy weapons and ammunition from the slain terrorists, and clearance and search operations were underway under Operation Radd-ul-Fitna 3.

Fitna al Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan, while the state has designated Balochistan-based terrorist groups as Fitna-al-Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.

Terrorism in KP, Balochistan

KP and Balochistan have witnessed terrorist attacks and security challenges for a long time.

KP, excluding the merged districts, recorded 54 terrorist attacks in August compared with 36 in July, representing an increase of 50 per cent, according to data compiled by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS).

A day earlier, in another North Waziristan IBO, security forces killed five terrorists, state media said.

On October 2, security forces killed seven terrorists in an IBO in North Waziristan. On September 30, security forces killed three terrorists in an IBO in KP’s Mir Ali. A day before that, in an IBO in KP’s Bara area, security forces killed five terrorists. On Sept 28, four terrorists were killed during an IBO in Dera Ismail Khan.

On Sept 26, a dozen people lost their lives while 35 others were injured in a suicide blast that targeted the Aman Mela police checkpost in DI Khan’s Darazinda tehsil. On Sept 18, a major attack in the old Police Lines in KP’s Kohat claimed 23 lives and injured about 100 others. Eight terrorists were killed during an overnight clearance operation . On Sept 17, security forces killed 10 terrorists in separate operations in KP between Sept 15 and 17. Earlier that month, over 20 terrorists were killed during multiple engagements in KP between Sept 3 and 5.

Meanwhile, in Balochistan’s Chagai, security forces killed two terrorists on Sept 29.

The military’s media affairs wing said on Sept 27 that more than 71 terrorists had been killed in Shaban and other areas of Balochistan in the previous 96 hours. On Sept 17, three terrorists were eliminated in an IBO in Balochistan’s Awaran district’s Badrang area. Another three were killed i n Mastung on Sept 14. Earlier in September, 21 terrorists were killed in separate engagements in Nokcha, Chagai, Ziarat Cross, and Pishin.

World.title: PM Shehbaz says terrorism in KP ‘must be stopped at any cost’ in meeting with Amir Muqam
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday said rising terrorism in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa “must be stopped” at any cost.
