Tech.title: A New Study Puts the Heat on Gas Stoves for Commercial Kitchen Air Pollution
Tech.content:
Following a July study that found switching from a household gas stove to an electric one can improve asthma symptoms, a new peer-reviewed study published on Tuesday concluded that workers in restaurant kitchens using gas and propane appliances are exposed to air pollution and heat levels that exceed health guidelines.

The National Restaurant Association reports that over 15.7 million Americans work in the food service industry.

Published in the scientific journal Environmental Research Letters, and in collaboration with chef Christopher Galarza, the study was conducted by researchers from the Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability, the New York University Grossman School of Medicine and PSE Healthy Energy, an independent scientific research institute specializing in bringing science to energy policy.

More from CNET

According to a press release, this is the first US study to compare air quality and heat levels in restaurant kitchens that use gas appliances with those that use all-electric appliances under real-world working conditions. The study is part of PSE Healthy Energy’s Methane and Health Initiative, which uncovers air quality and health risks associated with methane sources to protect public health and the climate.

Researchers measured air temperature and air pollutants produced by gas stoves: methane, nitrogen dioxide, carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide and benzene. Measurements were taken in five employee work areas, both during service and overnight, in 21 gas kitchens, three propane kitchens and three all-electric kitchens in California, New York and Pennsylvania.

“Everyone likely has a favorite restaurant or fast food chain, but most people probably haven’t thought about the equipment being used and how that affects what the staff is experiencing in the kitchen area,” Drew Michanowicz, principal scientist at PSE Healthy Energy, told CNET in an email.

Air pollution findings

When kitchens are not properly ventilated, pollutants can build up and cause harmful health effects, though this depends on individual sensitivity and exposure level.

During the study, it was discovered that in kitchens with gas or propane appliances, at least one health guideline for pollutant exposure was exceeded during cooking hours.

About 70% of gas kitchens in the study surpassed the US Environmental Protection Agency’s 1-hour outdoor air standard for nitrogen dioxide. The outdoor standard was used because there is no comparable indoor standard in the US.

In kitchens with gas or propane appliances, about 170 cumulative hours (about four full work weeks) were recorded in which nitrogen dioxide concentrations exceeded the World Health Organization’s hour-averaged exposure recommendation. This recommendation is roughly equal to the EPA’s outdoor standard, and both apply to the general population.

One kitchen’s 15-minute average nitrogen dioxide level exceeded the National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health’s recommended short-term workplace exposure limit.

Nitrogen dioxide can cause reduced lung function, increased asthma attacks, increased airway inflammation, and worsened cough and wheezing. This gaseous air pollutant has even been tied to causing asthma in children.

The study also found that carbon monoxide and benzene concentrations exceeded California’s 1-hour exposure guidelines in three and five gas kitchens, respectively. Carbon monoxide poisoning symptoms can range from a headache and dizziness to passing out and death. Benzene, on the other hand, is a carcinogen that has been linked to a higher risk of leukemia and other blood cell cancers.

By comparison, no all-electric kitchen exceeded pollution-exposure health guidelines during cooking hours.

“This study emphasizes that the concentrations of pollutants in commercial kitchens with gas-fired appliances can reach levels even higher than what we’ve previously observed in homes with gas stoves,” Yannai Kashtan, an air quality scientist at PSE Healthy Energy, told CNET in an email.

Those actually working in the kitchen aren’t the only ones who could be affected. Rhenizara S/Getty Images

Overnight levels matter too

Even outside cooking hours, exposure remains a concern, according to new evidence from the study.

When gas appliance pilot lights remain lit, and ventilation is turned off, cleaning crews and staff arriving early risk exposure to pollutants. About 71% of the gas kitchens with overnight monitoring recorded higher levels of nitrogen dioxide, carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide, methane and benzene overnight than during service hours.

Aside from contributing to climate change, high concentrations of methane can displace oxygen in the air, causing fatigue, rapid breathing, vomiting, collapse, convulsions, organ damage and death.

When you consider that commercial gas appliances are also used in hospitals, schools and other buildings, the health concerns extend beyond restaurant kitchens.

None of the all-electric kitchens exceeded pollutant guidelines overnight.

Temperature findings

When it came to heat health guidelines, about 68% of gas kitchens with temperature data exceeded 90 degrees Fahrenheit, the Occupational Safety and Health Administration’s proposed high-heat threshold.

Even when temperatures outside were below 75 degrees Fahrenheit, 10 of 13 gas kitchens exceeded 90 degrees Fahrenheit, meaning that high heat in commercial kitchens isn’t directly tied to the weather.

When a temperature monitor was attached to a chef’s shoulder during a 5-hour cooking session, the average temperature was 92 degrees Fahrenheit, with a maximum of 106 degrees Fahrenheit.

Guidelines differ between the general population and the workplace, which could put workers’ health at risk. andresr/Getty Images

A guideline gap in kitchen worker protection

The study compared its findings with both EPA and WHO guidelines for the general population, which prioritize health protection, and with NIOSH and OSHA guidelines, which are occupational. Researchers found fewer instances of kitchens exceeding workplace thresholds.

“Compared to benchmarks for the general population, occupational thresholds are higher because they serve a different purpose by also accounting for industry cost and technical feasibility,” Kashtan said. “If work environments are exceeding health-based thresholds but are compliant with the occupational limits that govern enforcement, this points to a gap in health protection for commercial kitchen workers.”

The study’s limitations

Due to the scarcity of all-electric commercial kitchens, only three were used in this study. However, the researchers stated in the study that their findings remain consistent with prior research on nitrogen dioxide concentrations from gas versus electric appliances.

As about 80% of end-use energy in US commercial cooking is gas, the small number of all-electric kitchens used in the study also reflects the current restaurant industry.

Only restaurant kitchens in three states were used, so this may not reflect the broader US. Participation was voluntary and partly facilitated through professional partnerships, so selection bias may have been introduced, especially given that kitchens willing to participate likely had better working conditions.

While sampling locations were chosen to account for different worker roles in the kitchen, pollutant measurements may differ from actual exposure due to a worker’s movement, health, posture and proximity to emission sources. These locations also weren’t monitored continuously; instead, they were sampled for 5 to 12 minutes per cycle.

Particulate matter and WBGT, which measures occupational heat stress, were not measured.

Ensure that your range hood is maintained and turned on when cooking. SBenitez/Getty Images

Restaurant recommendations

Based on this study, Michanowicz has three recommendations for worker protections in commercial kitchens that use gas appliances.

First, it’s important to ensure that ventilation systems are properly maintained, as these are usually the first line of defense against pollution and excess heat. However, even with these systems in place, restaurant workers who work directly over a cooking surface can still be exposed to pollution and heat before they reach the ventilation system.

While converting a commercial kitchen from gas to electric can be challenging and costly, focusing on electrifying gas ranges and fryers first can yield the greatest benefits for indoor air quality.

“There are also additional benefits that chefs we worked with have mentioned, such as higher worker productivity due to more comfortable kitchen temperatures, reduced cleaning times and reduced burn and explosion risks,” Michanowicz said.

Lastly, for workers in commercial kitchens during off-hours, including cleaning crews, when pilot lights are still on, ventilation systems should be turned on. This applies to workers who arrive early in the morning, as pollution will have built up overnight.

Gas stove household advice

The recommendations for those with gas stoves at home aren’t dissimilar.

“The best way to reduce gas combustion pollution is to eliminate the source – the gas flame – and to get an electric radiant or induction stove,” said Kashtan.

However, if that’s not possible due to cost or because one is a renter, cooking can still be partially electrified with air fryers, electric kettles, rice cookers and portable induction hobs.

And when you do use your gas stove, always make sure your range hood is on, and consider putting an air purifier in your kitchen.

Tech.title: Upcoming Phones We’re Still Expecting in 2026, Along With Some Heading to 2027
Tech.content:
This year started with a few iterative phone launches, but the last few months have taken us back into the exciting phones territory. From the all-new wide Galaxy Z Fold 8 to Apple’s first-ever foldable iPhone Duo, we’re fresh off the flagship launch cycle from Samsung, Google and Apple. Everything from a Galaxy to a Pixel and new Pro iPhones have already been announced. However, there are a few devices left to launch in 2026.

While the ongoing RAM shortage and growing competition in generative AI are making it harder for phone-makers to deliver bold designs without pushing prices too high, we’ve seen some innovative phones this year. However, they came with price hikes and also led Apple to shake things up with its iPhone 18 lineup. We only got the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, alongside the iPhone Duo, whereas the base iPhone 18 is expected to be announced alongside the iPhone 18E and iPhone Air 2 next year.

This year has already seen radical design approaches from the likes of Galaxy Z TriFold and Oppo Find N6, as well as camera innovations from the Ultra models of Vivo, Oppo and Xiaomi. Now, it is already time for their successors and a few of these features to trickle down to their Pro siblings in the upcoming months.

The bottom line? 2026 is far from over, and there are still a few exciting phones left to be revealed.

Phones released in 2026 so far

Apple

The iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max marked the return of vibrant colors to Apple’s highest-end iPhones. Prakhar Khanna/CNET

A split iPhone 18 launch strategy

Apple introduced two new devices in the iPhone 18 series, but unlike previous years, the base model was missing. We got the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max along with the foldable iPhone Duo — the latter, which goes on sale Oct. 23. But there’s no base iPhone 18 or iPhone Air 2. For years, Apple has continued to announce the base iPhone model alongside its Pro siblings, while also experimenting with Mini, Plus and Air variants. This has changed in 2026.

According to a report from The Information and Apple analyst Ming-Chi Kuo, the Cupertino, California-based company was rumored to push the launch of the vanilla iPhone 18 to early 2027 in a bid to make space for the iPhone Duo. After the September 2026 event, it seems like the rumors were true. The standard iPhone 18 is tipped to be released alongside the iPhone 18E in March 2027.

The new Apple iPhone launch cycle might be:

March 2026: iPhone 17E

September 2026: iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max and iPhone Duo

March 2027: iPhone 18, iPhone 18E and iPhone Air 2

September 2027: iPhone Air 3, iPhone 19 Pro/Pro Max and iPhone 20 (named to honor the 20th anniversary of the original iPhone’s 2007 debut)

Samsung

The Galaxy S25 Ultra debuted in January 2025. Josh Steinbauer/CNET

Samsung has seemingly announced all its flagship phones for the year. It started with a tri-fold phone and carried that innovative energy into its mainstream foldable phones. The Korea-based phone-maker has had its ups and downs in 2026, but it has delivered some amazing devices.

In January, it announced the Galaxy Z TriFold, which was extremely limited in availability. The Huawei Mate XT competitor opted for a different folding design; this compromised its usability, but the overall tablet-in-pocket design was terrific nonetheless. The following month, Samsung launched the Galaxy S26 series with forgettable upgrades to the S26 and S26 Plus, but added a unique Privacy Display feature on its top-of-the-line Ultra model. I wish it had added the same privacy capability to the Folds this year. While that didn’t happen, it launched an all-new wide Galaxy Z Fold 8 in July, which has been my favorite folding phone of the year. The new Flip 8 and Fold 8 Ultra are fine in their own ways, but the Fold 8 is the best combination of flip pocket-ability and fold usability.

While we’re unlikely to get any more flagship phones from Samsung this year, the Galaxy S27 series is reportedly bracing for a redesign. According to leakers Ice Universe, Sonny Dickson and Max Jambor, the Galaxy S27 series could adopt a camera bar design similar to the iPhone 17 Pro series.

Google

Google Pixel 11 Pro brings software-led changes. Andrew Lanxon/CNET

Google’s Pixel 11 series arrived in August, focusing on new software features and a bigger camera sensor on the Pixel 11 Pro. The Pixel 11 Pro Fold also got a slightly thinner and lighter design over last year’s Pixel 10 Pro Fold. While a lot of the hardware remained similar to last year’s Pixel 10 series, many of the small revisions added up to noticeable improvements, including faster 25W Qi2.2 wireless charging using the phones’ PixelSnap magnets and the 40% slimmer camera bar on the Pixel 11 over the Pixel 10.

The 2026 Google Pixel lineup is led by useful smart features. CNET’s Mike Sorrentino put it best in his review: “Pixel-specific features like Live Translate are jaw-dropping and show the lengths Google has gone to make accessibility a priority.” The underwhelming HiLight LED feature and $100 price hike across the lineup might sting, but each new Pixel phone can stand its own.

Motorola

Motorola’s Signature 27 has four cameras on the back, but so far, we only know about the 50-megapixel main camera and a 200-megapixel periscope telephoto camera. Motorola

Motorola is all set to launch its Signature 27 phone in the US this year. Unlike the original Motorola Signature, the aggressive flagship will be coming to the US market.

The Motorola Signature 27 will be powered by the newly announced Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 processor, paired with a partial list of high-end features. It could especially benefit from and fill the void left by the recently departed OnePlus phone line. One of the best parts about the upcoming phone is that it’ll match Samsung’s Galaxy and Google’s Pixel lines with a seven-year commitment to software and security support.

During Qualcomm’s annual Snapdragon Summit, Motorola also unveiled several specifications of its upcoming phone. The Signature 27 will include a 50-megapixel main camera, as well as a 200-megapixel periscope telephoto lens to take clear zoom photos from far distances, like at a concert. It’ll likely have another camera on the back, but we don’t know its megapixel count yet.

Motorola is focusing on gamers with its new flagship device. The Signature 27 has a cooling system called ArcticMesh, which combines a diamond-infused thermal gel, liquid metal, copper mesh and a 3D vapor chamber that’s 40% larger than the previous Signature phone. Theoretically, it should help the phone stay cool during intensive gaming and video recording. Motorola’s new phone will come in two colors: a “Pantone Coal Smoke in tactical weave,” which is a darker shade with a woven texture and a “Pantone Capulet Olive in a brushed textile-inspired finish,” which is a green shade with a softer, tactile feel.

Where is OnePlus?

OnePlus has already announced its OnePlus 13 successor: the OnePlus 15. Prakhar Khanna/CNET

However, we won’t get any more OnePlus flagships in the US. In July, the company confirmed that it’ll no longer operate in North America or Europe and won’t launch any further phones in the regions following 2025’s OnePlus 15. It had already merged some of its operations with its parent company Oppo in 2021, but all of its operations will now fall under the Oppo brand. OnePlus will continue to operate in China and India, but it’s unlikely to announce a top-end flagship phone this year.

Tech.title: Oracle Health Hack Exposes Data of Nearly 20M People
Tech.content:
A cyberattack against Oracle Health last year exposed the personal data of almost 20 million people, the Texas attorney general’s office said in a report, according to Bloomberg.

The personal information taken by the attacker included Social Security numbers, addresses and medical information, Oracle disclosed to investigators. The cybersecurity breach happened after Jan. 22, 2025, and Oracle alerted some customers about it in March of that year, Bloomberg reported.

Oracle Health is a division of Oracle, which acquired healthcare technology company Cerner for $28.3 billion in June 2022.

More from CNET

Oracle told its customers that attackers had targeted older Cerner servers before the data stored on them could be migrated to Oracle’s cloud storage service, Bloomberg said. The hacker compromised customer credentials and used them to access two Cerner servers and then copied patient data from those servers, according to UK cybersecurity firm CyPro.

Neither Oracle nor the Texas attorney general specified which hospitals, clinics or other healthcare providers were affected by the data theft.

CNET reached out to both the Texas AG’s office and Oracle, but representatives did not immediately respond.

Who’s affected by the Oracle Health breach?

Oracle healthcare customers include hospitals and clinics in Texas and other states, as well as the Department of Defense and the Department of Veterans Affairs. Of the nearly 20 million people affected, 3 million were Texans.

Christus Health, a nonprofit healthcare system in Texas, and Tri-City Medical Center in California — both affected by the breach — said stolen patient data could include names, Social Security numbers, doctors, diagnoses, medicines and test results, Bloomberg reported.

Christus said that patients whose data was compromised would receive letters about the incident and also would be offered a complimentary two-year membership to credit monitoring and identity protection services.

CyPro noted Tuesday that at least 29 hospital and health systems said they had been affected by the breach.

“The incident demonstrates how older infrastructure can remain a material source of third party risk during cloud migration,” Rob McBride, a CyPro founding partner, wrote. “Even though Oracle says its cloud infrastructure was unaffected, data held on two legacy servers was sufficient to expose information potentially belonging to millions of patients.”

What if your data was stolen?

Stolen data can be used to make scam attempts much more convincing, especially if the would-be criminals know your name, address or healthcare details, says Cliff Steinhauer, director of information security and engagement at the digital safety nonprofit National Cybersecurity Alliance.



“If someone contacts you claiming to be from insurance or a medical provider and asks for sensitive information or demands payment, hang up and call your provider back at a number you know belongs to them (like the back of your insurance card),” Steinhauer told CNET via email.



Steinhauer said that people whose data was stolen in the Oracle breach should find out what data was taken and use any identity or credit monitoring being offered.



“Keep an eye on your credit reports, financial accounts and healthcare statements for anything you don’t recognize,” he added. “It’s always a good idea to freeze your credit with all three major credit reporting bureaus as a preventative measure.”

Tech.title: Shopping for Amazon Deals? This Free Browser Extension Filters Out Fakes
Tech.content:
Developer Josh Pigford built the Knockoff extension to address Amazon’s growing problem with generic, mass-produced brands flooding search results.

Amazon is hosting its Prime Big Deal Days, which means there’s a lot of good stuff on sale right now. It’s one of the biggest online retail shopping events of the year, and you may have to swim through a bunch of generic brands and algorithmically generated names to find what you want. It turns out that there’s an extension that can help with that.

The extension, called Knockoff, makes shopping on Amazon more bearable by graying out or blocking fake brands, increasing visibility for products from actual brands. It’s available for Firefox, Chrome and all Chromium-based web browsers such as Microsoft Edge, Opera and Brave. It’s also available as a Safari extension.

Developer Josh Pigford launched the tool in early July, and it’s since gone viral, with over 100,000 downloads. A few days before the launch, Pigford posted on X, “Built a little chrome extension that lets you dim (or hide!) all the crap, mass-produced, fake brands on Amazon.” The post garnered 22,000 likes.

More from CNET

Knockoff is now live!



Filter out the knockoff crap brands on Amazon.



Sorry to brands like WNPETHOME, EHEYCIGA, YXYL, LU&MN, JOYIN, TOMY, GODONLIF, YOOJEE, LINGTENG, LANEIGE, VISCOO, BIODANCE, COOFANDY, BALENNZ, TOSY and LUENX.https://t.co/9mLk0EAsfG https://t.co/K07lMkepOW — Josh Pigford (@Shpigford) July 7, 2026

It works pretty simply. Once the extension is installed, any products from fake brands, dropshippers or otherwise suspicious vendors are marked and grayed out, highlighting the more reputable brands you might actually know. There’s also an option to automatically hide fake brands so you don’t even see them.

In an interview with 404 Media in July, Pigford said that Knockoff is built on prior extensions that aim to do this, such as AmazonBrandFilter and Amazon Brand Detector. The extension, which runs locally, doesn’t require an account, doesn’t send data to any company servers and doesn’t cost anything. It’s also open-source, and you can find the source code on GitHub.

The extension’s functions are pretty simple to understand. If it’s grayed out, it’s likely a fake brand, but the extension does need some fine-tuning. Joe Hindy/CNET

So, how well does Knockoff work?

Anything sounds good on paper, but the proof is in the pudding. I took Knockoff for a test drive to see how well it filtered the mass-produced junk.

My trial wasn’t terribly complicated. I searched for a variety of products across several categories using Knockoff’s stock settings to see how well the extension would filter out the knockoff brands without any additional tuning.

The short answer is that it did quite well. While searching for vacuum cleaners, it left most of the listings intact since they were from known brands, including Shark, Bissell and Dyson. Only a few listings were grayed out, mostly because no brand name was listed in the product description.

Solar lights fared much worse. Knockoff blocked dozens of listings for lack of brand names and also blocked listings from Jkimk, Technet, Tonulax and other unrecognized brands (most of which are stylized in all capital letters), while keeping listings for established brands, such as Brightown, a real company based in Raleigh, North Carolina.

Some product categories did better than others. Solar lights were awash with fake brands, but vacuums had only a few. Joe Hindy/CNET

Phone cases are where things start to get trickier. The extension blocked brands such as Supfine, Dumkery, Hiearcool and several others. However, it initially also blocked Torras, a well-known case brand with in-store stock at Best Buy, which holds thousands of global patents for many of its products. It doesn’t get much more real than Torras, but the company’s products were flagged because its name is stylized in all caps, which the extension checks. Torras was added as a trusted brand in subsequent updates, so anyone trying it now won’t see this error.

Knockoff listed some lesser-known but still legitimate earbuds brands, such as Tozo and Linsoul, as real companies, while it properly flagged phony hand tool brands, including Wgge and Horusdy. Brands that aren’t recognized by the extension often appear highlighted, but on the product page, the extension flags them as suspected fakes or entirely unrecognized.

It helps that Knockoff has a system for reporting brands that are incorrectly labeled as legitimate (or wrongly marked as fake). If the extension flags a product as fake when it’s legit, you can click the badge and “report as a real brand.” Likewise, if the extension flags a product as legit when it’s really fake, you can click the badge and “report as junk” when you click on a badge over a brand that the extension recognizes. You may need to enable badges for good brands in the settings to do this.

Knockoff lets you report brands that are good or bad to help make the extension more accurate over time. All reports are handled manually. Joe Hindy/CNET

Since Knockoff’s launch, Pigford has released multiple updates that address user responses, including a method to directly send feedback if you want to report a brand, along with bug fixes.

Knockoff is a good start for filtering junk

Overall, Knockoff is a useful extension in a digital marketplace dominated by AI-generated assets and unverified third-party products.

When you’re shopping, the biggest benefit is avoiding low-quality off-brands. Even if you’re not actively shopping for anything, it’s fun (and terrifying) to see how many grayed-out product listings you can find in any given product category. We recommend turning on badges for known brands, but otherwise, the stock settings performed the best.

At the same time, Knockoff shows you brands likely to be fake on Amazon, but it doesn’t tell you which products are actually good or bad. Fake brands often have more fake or bot-written reviews than legitimate brands.

Still, it all depends on what you’re shopping for. If all you need is a pack of zip ties for light cable management or to attach a tomato plant to a garden trellis, the ones sold by dropshippers will work just fine and save you a couple of bucks.

And while Knockoff certainly makes it easier to shop for quality items, the extension still needs some fine-tuning and human analysis. Updates to the extension seem to be doing exactly that, so if you’re just now discovering the tool, it’s likely the extension has improved over time.

Knockoff certainly makes it easier, but it’s still good to know how to spot these yourself, so when your package arrives, you’re happier. Amazon

Avoid fake brands without the extension

An eagle-eyed shopper can spot a knock-off brand from a mile away if they know where and how to look at product listings.

The first step, according to Russell Holly, director of commerce content at CNET, is to look for the brand outside of Amazon.com. “If it seems like a string of random characters and that brand name isn’t selling elsewhere, there’s a good chance the seller is not the manufacturer,” said Holly.

Holly also says to pay closer attention to negative reviews, since brands often fake only positive reviews. Negative reviews can be a better indicator of quality problems that may help explain why a product is cheaper than others in the same category.

Similarly, you can also look for a brand’s product support. If the only way to report a problem is directly to Amazon, Holly says you’re most likely dealing with a dropshipper that doesn’t offer product support if something breaks.

Another way to spot a fake brand is to find the same product sold under multiple brands. An example is a Broserengy alarm clock, Bluetooth speaker, phone charger combo. It is nearly identical to this product from Fansbe, including the RGB lights at the bottom, the placement (and labeling) of the buttons and the auxiliary USB port around the back for charging an accessory. These are two subtly different versions of the same product.

Tech.title: A Court Ruling Killed ‘Click to Cancel.’ NYC Just Brought It Back
Tech.content:
A year after an appeals court effectively canceled a nationwide regulation requiring companies to make it easier to get out of subscriptions, New York City has revived it for those who live there.

Announced last week by Mayor Zohran Mamdani, alongside the city’s top tech officer and consumer protection commissioner, the rule says companies must make it as easy to cancel a subscription as it is to sign up. That applies to gym memberships, a cellphone contract or apps that charge a monthly fee. It’s similar in principle to the “click-to-cancel” rules that were proposed in 2024 during the Biden administration but never fully rolled out. NYC’s law was set by an executive order in January and went into effect on Oct. 1.

“No one should need 45 minutes of hold music to stop paying for something they never wanted,” Mamdani said in the announcement. “If a company can take your money with one click, you should be able to get your money back with one click. And now, if they won’t let you cancel, the city is coming for them.”

More from CNET

Part of “coming for them” is a web page where New Yorkers can file a complaint. The site allows a visitor to search for or add a business, even if it’s not based in New York City, and select from a list of issues, such as, “The business delayed canceling your subscription,” or, “You were not informed of auto-renewal.” A text box and an option to upload documents, such as screenshots, allow for elaboration on what happened. Those filing complaints can also choose the type of outcome they’d like to see, including “refund and cancel subscription.”

Filing a complaint on NYC.gov’s Click to Cancel webpage brings up a form for New Yorkers to fill out. NYC.gov

According to Samuel Levine, commissioner of New York City’s Department of Consumer and Worker Protection, full-time staffers will field those web-submitted complaints. “They’re not going to be diverted into a chatbot doom loop,” Levine told The Verge. “We’re going to have actual people whose full-time job is to help them.”

Businesses that are the subject of a complaint will be investigated, and if they’re found to be in violation of the city rules, they could be fined up to $525 per violation.

Other places, other rules

What will happen in the rest of the country, where, according to a CNET survey, Americans spend on average more than $1,300 a year on subscriptions, some of them unused or subscribed to by accident?

Emily Peterson-Cassin, director of competition and market fairness at the Consumer Federation of America, said New York City’s click-to-cancel law shows how local governments can create new ways to protect consumers. “This innovative move highlights yet again that local and state consumer protection agencies are stepping up to protect consumers even while federal agencies aren’t and provides a roadmap for other regulators to do the same.”

California, for instance, has a rule that requires businesses to get a customer’s explicit consent before they are charged for a subscription renewal.

That law was beefed up last year to include protections like offering cancellation on the same medium the subscription originated; a business can’t, for instance, make you go to a physical location to cancel something you signed up for online. It also requires companies to notify customers before an upcoming renewal charge and to give annual reminders about auto-renewals using the same method of communication used to enroll.

A Maryland law that went into effect in June also requires companies to give customers a “cost-effective, timely and easy-to-use” way to cancel auto-renewals of subscriptions. The law falls under Maryland’s Service Contracts and Consumer Products Guaranty Act and can result in fines (PDF) of up to $10,000 per violation or $25,000 for repeat violations.

Colorado’s equivalent law, the Online Cancellation Act, went into effect in 2025 and mandated that merchants provide a one-step cancellation link. Earlier this year, the act was expanded to include transactions between two businesses or entities.

National ‘click to cancel’ could return

The “patchwork” approach, as some describe these disparate regional laws, is in lieu of the national rule that was stalled because of a procedural error. When the Eighth District Court of Appeals struck it down, the court said it was because the proper regulatory analysis hadn’t been done, not because the court disagreed with its intent or approach.

There are signs that the Federal Trade Commission could be taking the initiative to revive a national click-to-cancel policy, or at least parts of it, but it’s hard to tell from its language. In a January press release, the FTC said it was submitting a draft proposal related to “Negative Option Plans,” another way of saying auto-renewals, in which businesses don’t give customers notice or the option to cancel for ongoing subscription charges. In March, the FTC opened up the floor for public comment after it said it received 100,000 complaints in five years over businesses making cancellations difficult or impossible.

A representative for the FTC told CNET in an email, “We don’t have an update related to this issue” regarding click-to-cancel or the New York City law.

Peterson-Cassin of the CFA said that so far the FTC has mostly focused on disclosing fees rather than banning auto-renewals, “so it’s hard for us to believe they would come up with something as strong as the New York rule.”

However, she said, “Given how much attention there is on this issue and New York’s good example, there is still time for them to do the right thing, and protect all Americans from these predatory subscription traps.”

Have a story tip you want to share with CNET? Reach us at news@cnet.com.

Tech.title: What iOS 27.2 Could Bring to Your iPhone Later This Month
Tech.content:
More than three weeks after Apple released iOS 27 to the general public, the tech giant released the second public beta of iOS 27.2 on Oct. 6. While iOS 27 brought Siri AI and more to your device, this early look at iOS 27.2 shows Siri AI expanding to other languages and a few upgrades in other apps, such as FaceTime.

If you’re wondering what happened to iOS 27.1, Apple has said the foldable iPhone Duo will launch on 27.1 next month, and all devices will be able to update to 27.2 sometime later.

Apple

Since this is a beta, I recommend downloading it only on something other than your primary device. This isn’t the final version of iOS 27.2, so the update might be buggy and battery life may be short — it’s best to keep those troubles on a secondary device.

Also, since this isn’t the final version, more features could end up landing on your iPhone when Apple releases iOS 27.2.

Here are some features developers and beta testers can try now in the second iOS 27.2 public beta. Apple has not said when exactly it will release iOS 27.2 to the general public, but we expect it to land on devices in October.

Siri AI in more languages

Siri AI is available on iOS 27 now. Jeffrey Hazelwood/CNET

In iOS 27, Siri AI is only available in English. And the iOS 27.2 beta expands Siri AI to French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish.

Apple previously said Siri AI would expand to these additional languages, so this shows the company moving quickly on that promise.

Use front and rear cameras simultaneously in Facetime

In the iOS 27.2 beta, you can use your front and rear facing cameras at the same time in Facetime calls. This allows you to Facetime call with a larger group of people — you don’t have to squeeze everyone into a single frame in order to see the person on the other end of the call. However, everyone on the call needs to be on iOS 27 or later for this feature to work.

An anti-snatching feature

According to 9to5Mac, code within the iOS 27.2 beta shows a feature called AutoLock. This is reportedly an anti-theft feature that can lock your device if it detects it’s been snatched out of your hand. For example, AutoLock could lock your iPhone if it detects a sharp acceleration, as if it was snatched out of your hands, or if your device has been unlocked for an extended period of time.

It’s important to note that this feature is not a user-facing option on your iPhone in this beta. Rather, 9to5Mac has reportedly seen internal code related to the feature. That means this feature may not be available when Apple releases iOS 27.2 in October.

Refreshed Podcasts options

The Podcasts app also gets an update in the iOS 27.2 beta. The beta introduces two rows to the top of the Home tab within the app: New Episodes and Continue Playing. This can help you keep track of what podcasts are new and what podcasts you still have to finish.

It’s a small, pleasant addition to the interface, and I appreciate how it helps keep my podcasts organized.

Apple TV profile expansion

In the beta of iOS 27.2, you can create TV Profiles in your Apple TV app. You can assign a profile to your child or someone else and ensure your preferences aren’t messed with.

So if you’re tired of being recommended kids shows after letting your child watch the series Shape Island, you can create a profile for your child and let them watch those quirky little shapes all they want. (But also, it’s possible that I like Shape Island more than my son does, so you should check it out.)

Apple TV multiview on iOS

Another Apple TV update in the iOS 27.2 beta is Multiview. Developers and beta testers who subscribe to Apple TV can watch up to four live sports streams, including streams from Major League Soccer and Formula 1, at once. That way, you don’t miss an important game, or you can look at a map of the racecourse while watching feeds from driver-view cameras.

Updated Health app

The Apple Health app just got a refresh. Apple

Developers and beta testers can see a redesigned Health app in the iOS 27.2 beta. The redesigned app introduces some new features and changes some others.

The Insights tab can give you a look at your daily metrics, such as sleep and fitness activity, and personalized summaries near the top of the page.

The new Longevity tab analyzes health from your devices, like your Apple Watch and iPhone, and creates visualizations for that information. You can also try new movement assessments in this tab, like for flexibility and hearing health. Some of these assessments require you to perform an activity for a few minutes on camera so the app can analyze your movements.

Apple

The redesigned Health app also lets you see your Health Age, which reflects how your daily habits might influence your body. So depending on your habits, this number could go up or down relative to your actual age.

You can also order labs via Quest Diagnostics for $119 through the app.

However, the redesign is expected to launch sometime later this year, despite being featured in this beta.

Those are a few of the new features developers and beta testers can try now with the second public beta of iOS 27.2. There will likely be more betas before the OS is released to the public.

For more, here’s what to know about iOS 27 and why your battery might be draining faster after updating. You can also check out why the iPhone Duo will launch with iOS 27.1.

Tech.title: Mistral’s New ‘Le Chonk’ AI Model Is Big, Open and Built for Agents
Tech.content:
New AI models are coming, and they don’t stop coming.

On the heels of the recent rollout of Claude Opus 5.5 and OpenAI’s GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna, Mistral AI is launching a new flagship model, Mistral Large 4, with a public preview available on Tuesday.

A French company known for its open-source and open-weight LLMs, Mistral AI reports that the Large 4 model “ranks among the best open-weight models of the world” on aggregated metrics and also outperforms European and US models, while also catching up to Chinese competitors, who have been dominating the open-weight sector.

More from CNET

I talked with Mistral Chief Scientist Guillaume Lample and VP of Science Pierre Stock about the new model – affectionately known as “le Chonk” – its specialized capabilities and extreme compute efficiency. Here’s what to know.

Key capabilities of Mistral Large 4

Lample and Stock said that Mistral Large 4 was built to process both text and images, closing performance gaps from previous Mistral models. Specifically, Large 4 touts more advanced cybersecurity and agentic capabilities, as well as a better ability to handle manufacturing- and finance-related tasks.

Cybersecurity

Mistral Large 4 was designed to excel at defensive cybersecurity tasks, including log inspection, code auditing and checking for newly published exploits or vulnerabilities. Beyond defensive measures, Mistral says the new model offers offensive cybersecurity measures to identify and address weaknesses.

Agentic AI

“Really, the core competency we’re looking at for ML4 is agentic capabilities,” said Stock.

Mistral Large 4 was built with a focus on agentic performance for planning, research or handling complex enterprise tasks that would take human experts hours or days to complete. The Mistral AI team said the model reaches “state-of-the-art” performance on critical agentic benchmarks like SWE-bench and Terminal Bench – evaluation frameworks for testing how well agents handle complex tasks – for tasks like coding, analyzing and pulling requests.

Geospatial and grounding capabilities

The Mistral team says the model outperforms competitors in aerial and satellite imagery analysis, with the capacity to identify visual patterns and objects on maps, such as forest fires.

“On grounding capabilities, it outperforms all existing models, including the closed ones,” the press release for the model says. “These are critical as cyberattacks get faster and cheaper, companies write more code than ever and the world needs more chips to keep up with AI demand.”

Grounding is a technique used in AI development to try to eliminate hallucinations – when the LLM generates inaccurate information – by anchoring the AI’s outputs in external resources, like documents and databases, rather than just the materials it was trained on internally. Grounding also helps keep data and information fresh while providing context for the AI’s responses.

Mistral says the new model was also trained on more than 160 languages, including every official language of the European Union, as well as Latin and non-Latin languages, to answer prompts natively.

Mistral will roll out ML4 on Oct. 27. Until then, the model is available for a public preview period, allowing the Mistral team to further assess it with feedback from developers, cybersecurity experts and state officials. The team will also use this period for additional reinforcement learning and fine-tuning. You can try the preview API here.

Tech.title: Apple and AT&T Will Replace Your Brand New iPhone 18 Pro Max if It Can’t Connect
Tech.content:
Barely three weeks after the iPhone 18 Pro Max arrived in customers’ hands, some AT&T customers are unable to make calls or get any cellular data — including dialing 911 in emergencies. Apple and AT&T rolled out a pair of fixes, but if you were bitten by this unusual bug, your shiny new iPhone is permanently broken and needs to be replaced, which Apple will do for free.

Last week, some iPhone 18 Pro Max owners on AT&T’s network reported no cellular access. MacRumors reported that AT&T sent a text message to iPhone 18 Pro Max owners, encouraging them to update to iOS 27.0.1 immediately. MacRumors estimates that thousands of customers have been affected.

On Friday, Apple said it’s issuing a separate carrier-settings patch to pair with the iOS 27.0.1 update. But the patch comes too late for certain owners of the new phone.

More from CNET

An Apple representative told CNET that the updates are intended to guard against this problem in the future and won’t fix the situation for iPhone 18 Pro Max owners who are already experiencing it. Apple will provide a new phone free of charge to those owners. Affected customers should contact Apple Support or AT&T.

In Reddit threads about the issue, some owners confirmed that the 27.0.1 update by itself did not fix the problem, nor did upgrading to the public beta of iOS 27.2.

Only the iPhone 18 Pro Max is affected

So far, the issue seems limited to iPhone 18 Pro Max models on AT&T’s network. I reached out to contacts at T-Mobile and Verizon, and both report they’re not seeing similar reports on their networks. I haven’t experienced the issue on an iPhone 18 Pro that runs on AT&T’s network, which isn’t surprising given that this particular problem affects iPhone 18 Pro Max units, not iPhone 18 Pro phones. A CNET colleague’s iPhone 18 Pro Max on Google Fi (which uses T-Mobile’s network) is not experiencing the issue. I’ve not been able to discern if customers of cellular providers that use AT&T’s network, such as Cricket or US Mobile, have been affected.

It’s unclear whether the lack of connectivity is related to the phone’s hardware. While the standard iPhone 18 Pro is equipped with Apple’s C2 modem, the iPhone 18 Pro Max in the US is the only model with Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X80 modem, as shown in this teardown of the phone by iFixIt. Qualcomm has been Apple’s modem provider for years, but Apple has worked to move away from relying on the third party for the essential phone component. That relationship is due to expire this year.

According to a TechInsights iPhone 18 Pro Max teardown, the X80 modem is also used in the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro Max, but a new millimeter-wave antenna has been added to the 18 Pro Max. Millimeter-wave offers much faster data speeds in areas where the technology is installed, but it can have a shorter range and be reduced by obstacles. Apple’s C2 modem also includes a millimeter-wave antenna.

Qualcomm declined to comment, and a representative directed me to contact Apple for more information.
